*It was a brooding Rowan who made the journey northwards in the aftermath of Arthdale’s destruction. For over a day he tramped up the winding dirt roads of rural Rosaria, staring with blank numbness at the beauty of the landscape that surrounded him.*

*The world might have been content to leave Alexia to languish in that place, but he wouldn’t. It may be an obvious trap, but Rowan was resolved to rescue his wife.*

*It had been months now. Months of uncertainty and silence. No word from the outside, not a peep about Rowan’s whereabouts. She had no idea when it had happened, but Alexia had slowly grown accustomed to life in Castle Bloodmeen.*
*The orc guards no longer caused her to immediately shrink back in fear. The maids and their curiously skimpy outfits had ceased to give her nervous pause. The castle corridors - once dizzyingly convoluted to navigate - had become quite familiar to her.*
*Still, it was a lonely existence. The maids were kind but perfunctory, and Alexia was too intimidated to try speaking to any of the orcs. There was no one else to talk to, no one to share her worries or woes.*
*The only person who she could really converse with was the red demon, Andras. He visited her often, in her chambers and otherwise.*
*She had warmed up to Andras considerably in recent months.*
*She remained cold and aloof to her demonic kidnapper*
*Despite his intimidating form, and her own stubborn intent to remain standoffish, Andras was nothing but kind to her. Slowly, bit by bit, he managed to win her over with his gruff charm.*
*Having at least someone to talk to had brightened her mood considerably. To her surprise, Andras proved to be a sparkling conversationalist.*
*More than once she’d found herself chuckling at his over the top mannerisms, especially during meals, when he would absolutely wolf down everything that was in front of him. It was almost charming in its absolute crudeness.*
*He was brash, but considerate, even regretful for her imprisonment. As time passed, she had grown more and more uncertain as to his true motives. How could a being this personable be one of the demonic beasts of legend?*
*Andras brought her books from the library, took time out of his day to see her, and listened to her worries. He was understanding, sometimes even sympathetic to her plight. She never forgot that he was her captor, or that she was his captive, but… it was hard to simply hate him.*
*He'd began to pull her out of her shell, encouraging her to take walks upon the castle battlements. Andras often accompanied her, regaling her with stories of his youth as a traveling vagabond. To a sheltered village girl who had barely left her home in years, it was all terribly exciting to listen to.*

*She had spent her first lonely weeks in the castle trying to figure out how to escape, all the while suffering through Andras’ crocodile smile every time he visited her on one pretext or another. He was relentless, and she hated it.*
*However, such hopes of freedom proved pointless. Beyond the imposing castle walls, between her and her home, was a barren wasteland. Cold mountains stretched across the horizon, encompassing a withered landscape.*
*Even if she could escape the castle, Alexia was no survivalist. How had she slept through the entire journey here? This desolate place could not possibly be anywhere close to her beautiful, green home in the Rosarian plains.*
*Left with little hope and even less to do, she spent what time she could buried in the Castle’s extensive library, huddled in a quiet corner, reading as much as she could. It helped her to ignore her growing despondency.*
*A knock at the door heralded the arrival of her hated captor.*
Andras: "What’s with the long face?"
Alexia: "Go. Away."
Andras: "Hah! I thought you'd be happy to have a charming, handsome man to keep you company."
Alexia: "Why? Do you know any?"
*To her annoyance, the bastard threw his head back and laughed again. Alexia’s brow knitted together. She carefully saved her page in her book, set it aside, and stood up to face him.*
Alexia: "What do you want? It’s late. I’m going to bed."
Andras: "-And you don’t want me to stay?"
Alexia: "I’d sooner leap from the castle parapets."
Andras: "I'd catch you before you could fall."
Alexia: "-Then I'd bite your hand."
Andras: "Well, you know the saying about the hand that feeds you."
Alexia: "What do you want, Andras?"
Andras: "What, no “Lord Andras, anymore? What happened to all that defiance in Arthdale?"
Andras: "You’re getting soft on me."
Alexia: "I’m sure you know the feeling all too well."
Andras: "Now, now: put the claws away, kitten. I come bearing a gift for you."
Alexia: "I don’t want anything you have to give me."
*He ignored her harsh scowl as he pulled out a small object from his belt. His grin was like a shark’s as he dangled it in front of her.*
*It was a stunningly beautiful necklace, encircled by a gold chain. Set in its center was the largest jewel Alexia had ever seen: a glittering sapphire.*
*It was the kind of thing that royalty might wear. Andras smirked as he held it, balancing the end of the chain on the tip of his index finger as it swayed back and forth.*
Andras: "Beautiful, isn’t it? Like you."
Alexia: "It’s ugly and pretentious. Like you."
Andras: "I want you to wear it."
Alexia: "No."

Andras: "But… it would look so good on you."
Alexia: "Don’t touch me."
Andras: "Brave to a fault. This is my castle, dear."
Andras: "Take the gift. Put it on. It won’t kill you to do so."
Alexia: "Maybe I’d rather you did."
Andras: "-And miss seeing your beloved husband again?"
Alexia: "..."
Andras: "He’s coming to rescue you, you know. And I would hate for anything to happen that might prevent the two of you from reuniting."

Andras: "Try taking it off."
*Dumbfounded, Alexia tried to do as he said. However, the gold chain only lifted a short ways up her neck before it snagged, as if hitting a wall. Desperate, she tried to yank the thing off, but it wouldn’t budge. *
Alexia: "W-what did you-"
Andras: "Oh, did I forget to mention you can’t remove it?"
Andras: "Now touch the gem and speak softly into it, like this."
*Alexia, shaken, took a long, hard look at the thing around her neck.*
Alexia: "If… if it means you’ll finally leave, fine."
*She reached her hand up to hesitantly clasp the gem. *

*Andras’ smile widened. He opened his mouth, but no sound came out.*
*A voice, his voice, spoke just over her shoulder.*
Andras: "An ass? Surely you can do better than that."
*Alexia stumbled back from him, her eyes going wide with terror. Andras laughed, turning away and leaving the room without a second glance back. He paused just before crossing the entryway.*
Andras: "Enjoy your 'solitude' for the next few days, I’m off to find your useless husband."
*The door closed behind him with grim finality, leaving her utterly alone. Alexia, shaken, sat down at the bed.*
Andras: "I'll always be with you, in here."
*A shudder ran through her. She looked down once again at the shimmering blue gem for a very long moment, her uncertain expression reflected in its contours.*
*Rowan was trapped, a sheer rock wall at his back. The only way was forward, into the toothless maw of the croaking monstrosity. The one which saw him as it's next meal.*
*Rowan threw himself to the ground as the toad demon’s tongue catapulted out of its mouth, aiming for Rowan’s center of mass. He rolled to his feet, drawing his sword as its tongue slapped wetly against the rock face to his left.*
*He swung downwards as hard as he could, catching the thing’s tongue with his blade. It sliced cleanly through the quivering flesh, a spurt of greenish blood bursting forth as he severed the head of its tongue from the rest of its body.*
*The chaos-tainted beast croaked and shrank back, its barbed tail whipping upwards in a scorpion’s curl as it huddled into itself, taking a defensive position. Rowan, undeterred, charged the Chidwyr. *
*Its tail-stinger dove down to skewer him, but Rowan juked it as he closed the final distance. It tried to flap its wings to gain traction for takeoff, but he was too quick for it. He slashed its fat neck, opening a gaping wound beneath its mouth as its dumb eyes bulged.*
*A gurgled croak was the only sound it made as it flopped to the ground and expired, nearly knocking him off his feet in its death throes. After nearly a minute of weak struggling, it went still.*
*Rowan sighed, wiping his blade upon the Chidwyr’s warty skin before sheathing it. He looked over the final rise between him and his destination.*
*Rowan had come so far already. Through the immaculate roads of Prothea, through the dark and twisting jungles of Ealoran, past the dilapidated Demon fortress at Deadman’s Pass and across the ruined bogs of Rakshan.*
*He had journeyed far beyond the scope of mortal habitation. North. Ever northwards, ever onwards towards that terrible castle of his nightmares, where Goddess-only knew what awaited him.*
*And there, just over the horizon, jutted a jagged tower, scraping at the sky with its spiky black contours. At long last, his journey was at an end.*
*Bloodmeen Castle. Karnas’ corrupted stronghold.*
*The last time he had crossed this bridge, it had been strewn with the mangled bodies and blood-stained pageantry of the alliance’s finest knights. They had battled for every step, every inch of that terrible span. *
*And it was all for naught: for the moment they cleared the last Orcish defenders and reached the foot of the gates, Karnas unleashed the full terror of his slavering Chaos beasts. Few had returned back across the bridge from that gruesome slaughter; Rowan had been one of the lucky few.*
*It all seemed so long ago now, he thought. And yet, not nearly long enough.*
*His first indication of danger was the faint sight of defenders atop the walls. The pit in his stomach grew. This castle had been left broken and deserted. The Demons really were back.*
*Rowan waited until there was an opening in the patrols. Then, quick and quiet, he made a dash across the bridge, keeping his head low. He could not afford to be spotted.*
*Coming to the gate, he slid off to a side, creeping along the scars of the castle exterior to an unguarded segment of the wall. More than once he had to use handholds to keep himself from plummeting into the abyss below.*
*With a grunt of effort he heaved himself upwards, scrambling over a break in the wall where a trebuchet had gouged a hole halfway up. Clambering upwards, he heaved himself over the crumbling rock, landing in a set of bushes in the courtyard.*
*There were more soldiers in the vestibule, some of them were even human. Several dozen milled about in a group, armed to the teeth and segregated into units. They seemed to be waiting for something… or someone.*
*Rowan picked his way carefully through the reeds and slipped into the castle proper from a small servant entrance, taking care not to be spotted.*
*As he entered the castle confines he brushed past two Orcs on their way towards the courtyard. They paid him no mind. He let out a soft sigh of relief. He was in.*
*He had come to kill the Demons.*
*The monsters that had burned down his home were an existential threat to the continent. Rowan had not fought for so long and so hard against Karnas to allow the forces of Chaos to return once more.*
*If the rest of the world would not take them seriously, then so be it. The Hero of Rosaria himself would rectify that mistake.*
*He was here to save his wife.*
*Alexia was here. Somewhere. She had to be. Whatever danger the Demons posed, they could be dealt with in time. His wife was an innocent bystander, a pawn in their insidious games.*
*Rowan tamped down on the sense of guilt in his chest as he swept into the castle, intent upon discovering her location.*
Rowan: "(I just gotta keep moving and keep my head down. Another faceless mercenary in the crowd.)"
*Heading deeper into the half-ruined castle, he noted with some discomfort how crowded the place was. The castle was full of mercenaries and orcs, and in the distance the distinctive sounds of picks and shovels and hammers could be heard.*
*The castle was being excavated… no, it was being renovated. They were busy repairing the damage of the previous war. *
*Rowan’s stomach turned: this was no mere ‘gathering’ of Orcs beneath the Demon’s rule. How was it possible that a real army was growing here so soon after the last war?*
*As he turned a corner down a long corridor, he caught sight of a curious incongruity: a woman, tall and statuesque, striding down the hallway as if she owned the place.*
*To his relief, she did not spare so much as a glance in his direction as she passed, her nose pressed into a book. Somehow, she managed to navigate the corridor without losing a step.*
*Magicians, mercenaries, Orcs… these Demons were a threat to all Six Realms.*
*His wandering at last led him to a cavernous room behind the throne room. It had once housed the many trophies from Karnas’ conquests: the skulls of drakes and mighty weapons peeled from the dead fingers of heroes. But now…*
Rowan: "What in Solanse?"
*In the center of the room stood a towering frame of… something. Tall, glasslike, it looked almost like a great mirror, reflecting only shadows.*
*Stricken by a queer compulsion, Rowan approached it. He could not see himself reflected in it as he approached. Looking deep into its interior, he could only make out murky potentialities, strange ‘almost somethings’ that lurked just beyond the mind’s eye.*
*As if responding to his approach, the portal lit up with a sudden glare. Rowan stumbled back, astonished, as an image came roaring up from the depths of the mirror, bathing the room in blinding light.*
*When he uncovered his eyes, he was face to face with a world beyond the glass.*
Rowan: "Is that… The Empire of Sand?"
*Ancient, wind-blasted structures sat half-buried in squat squares around the mouth of a steep, craggy canyon. Sand dunes as tall as mountains rose like rolling waves in the distance.*
*A hunch-backed, spotted dog creature lifted its head to stare directly at the doorway, before scampering off into the ruins. Rowan’s jaw dropped.*
*Try putting your hand through.*
*Against his better judgement, Rowan decided to check the authenticity of this mirage. His hand tentatively reached out - and through the portal, as if it wasn’t even there.*
*He was assailed immediately with a sudden rush of heat. A torrid desert breeze rolled across his fingertips. Bits of sand and grit slapped against his palm in the dryness. Rowan pulled his hand back.*
Rowan: "...Goddess. They really can teleport."
*Whatever it is, it’s chaos magic. Don’t risk it.*
*Whether what he was seeing was real or a case of base trickery, Rowan knew better than to meddle in the horrid aspects of Chaotic magic. More than one friend had lost his life to the warping strands of energy let loose by such power.*
*Rowan withdrew his hand, the hairs on the back of his neck standing on end. The desert beyond the portal called to him, seeming just a footstep away.*
Rowan: "(This is much worse than I feared. Not even Karnas had this kind of ability.)"
Rowan: "(If they are capable of this, no one in the whole world is safe.)"
*Rowan’s blood ran cold. On instinct he leapt from the dais, sprinting over to one of the tall pillars that lined the room and throwing himself behind it. He only just slipped out of sight as the iron doors leading to the throne room swung open.*

Andras: "Oh believe me, I will. Try not to think too hard while I’m gone."

Cliohna: "Kneel, and be quiet."
*She flicked her hand, and the man fell to his knees, clawing at his throat. The other acolytes soon followed suit.*

*A thundering *CRACK* pierced the air, and the massive gate of the abbey shattered in an instant. Splinters rained around them as Rowan cursed out loud – or at least was fairly certain he did, his ears ringing.*

*Judging by the display earlier, she was not lacking in power. If he was to rebel against the twins one day… He might need her support, no matter the price.*
*Judging by the display earlier, she was not lacking in power, and her research was crucial to their efforts. I he was to succeed in toppling Solansia’s order, he would need her support, no matter the price.*

*Arzyl settled down back into her original meditative position, cradling the glowing skull in her lap with a protective caress.*
Arzyl: "Then I shall await your return with bated breath, Rowan."
*As Rowan closed the door behind him, he heard the eerie sound of echoless chanting rise up to fill his ears once more.*
*Rowan stood before the towering doors of the throne room like a man about to stride onto a battlefield.*
*Arzyl, arm in arm with him, cast a furtive glance in his direction. She smiled sweetly at his grim expression.*
Arzyl: "Well, Rowan… are you ready?"
Rowan: "About as ready as I’ll ever be."
*Arzyl let out a soft tsk. Her grip tightened on him.*
Arzyl: "Oh, don’t be so shy, my lovely!"
Arzyl: "You may not enjoy such political niceties, but I assure you: they’re essential. As time goes by and Bloodmeen’s stature grows, they’ll only ever grow more commonplace."
Arzyl: "And - it must be said - you look ravishing this evening."
Rowan: "I’m not some debutante for you to display at the ball."
Arzyl: "-Nor is this your first revolution around the diplomatic turntable. You know as well as I do that a toast of wine at dinner can buy a thousand swords on a battlefield."
*The sound of laughter petering in from beyond the throne room doors caused Rowan’s brow to tighten.*
Rowan: "Let’s get this over with."
Arzyl: "After you, my lovely!"
*The doors parted for them, and they stepped into a throne room transformed.*
*Gossamer strands of multifarious colors wound about the room like spiderweb threads, caressing tables and coating the stone floor in curving, coiling patterns and images. It was soft and downy to the touch, making the ground almost carpet-like, yet soft to tread.*
*Great torches had been erected in the rafters, casting merry yellow light upon the rows and rows of feasting tables that covered nearly half the room.*
*At one corner was erected a tall platform, whence a cadre of mortal minstrels performed a saucy tune. Their lilting, trilling voices only just carried over the heavy chatter of the assembled guests, who crowded the open floor like packed sardines.*
*Down one long side of the hall great banquet tables had been set. Rowan watched in mouth-watering awe as servants carried out great loaves of fluffy bread, mounds of leeks, carrots, sweet corn, and turnips white and yellow.*
*They hoisted up fresh boar on a spit, roasted duck swimming in a creamy white sauce, and trenchers dripping full of venison stewed with beer and butter.*
*Great casks of wine were carted in, borne in barrels so aged the oak itself was coated in moss. When the spigots were turned however, wine of a bright, shimmering gold emerged, filling the glasses and goblets of all who cared to partake.*
*And more. So so much more besides. This was no feast, this was a gourmand’s dream.*
*There was an otherworldly beauty to the banquet, a jovial air that went beyond mere decoration or music. Rowan had to stop himself before he broke out into a bright smile.*
Rowan: "Your people prepared all this in a day?"
Arzyl: "Industrious, aren’t they? We are quite fond of banquets."
*In addition to the braziers, bright candles of glowing blue balefire hovered in the air, as if conjured from the aether.*
*The tables, upon closer inspection, were closer to wood sculptures than actual seating arrangements: looking for all the world like a grove of mossy trees bent and shaped into the form of seating arrangements.*
*And there, above in the far rafters: the twinkling of colored stars. Not stars, but jewels. Some as big as one’s fist, collected into rainbow constellations that swept the sky of the room.*
*The sound of ethereal music rolled over everything, adding an ecstatic, urgent calling to the festive atmosphere.*
*Some guests were dressed in their finest velvets, others in full body armor. No matter where Rowan looked, however, there were smiles on all their faces. Quite the feat, for a place as grim as Bloodmeen.*
*An Orc dressed in a fanciful garb banged a large staff upon the stony floor, the loud smacking reverberating across the room and bringing everyone’s attention to the fore.*
Orc Herald: "Introducing Sir Rowan Blackwell! Steward of Bloodmeen, Hero of Rosaria, Paramount Knight, General of the Twins, slayer of Demons and conqueror of realms!"
Orc Herald: "Introducing Lord Rowan Blackwell! Steward of Bloodmeen, Hero of Rosaria, Paramount Knight, General of the Twins, slayer of Demons and conqueror of realms!"
*A loud titter swept across the crowd as all eyes turned to Rowan. Despite his stoic expression a rare blush crept up his face.*
*Rowan cast a side eye at this party’s instigator, but Arzyl remained dutifully blank faced, watching the Herald patiently for her own introduction. After the murmuring died down, a second pounding of the staff ensued.*
Orc Herald: "Introducing Ambassador Arzyl, Lady of the Midnight Court and Representative of Queen Kassandra of the Fae."
*A muted clapping ensued, and Arzyl bowed her head in contrition to the Herald’s kind words. Rowan raised an eyebrow.*
Rowan: "Quite the humble resume you gave yourself. Especially when compared to what was said about me."
*Arzyl smiled, though never made eye contact, her gaze sweeping across the assorted guests who cast furtive glances at them as they strode into the throne room.*
Arzyl: "A proper entrance is arguably the single most important interaction one can have! It sets the tone, and spins the guise with which we surround ourselves."
Rowan: "So you underplay your status?"
Arzyl: "Quite the opposite! My titles and positions in the Midnight Court mean little and nothing to mortals. Those here who do know it’s import hold me in high esteem already."
Arzyl: "Conversely, my stature is increased a hundredfold if the “Hero of Rosaria deigns to take a lowly ambassador from an unknown realm as his equal for an evening."
Rowan: "-Despite the fact that you invited me."
*Her smile grew and grew.*
Arzyl: "Quite right, my lovely. The truth - much like a whore - is valued far more for its appearance than the mundane reality."
Rowan: "…I see the guests are waiting for us."
*Arzyl beamed at his tactful response.*
Arzyl: "Then let us not keep them waiting!"
*May we speak to your courtiers first?*
*Arzyl tittered, fluttering her eyelashes at him as she steered him towards a multifarious cohort of gussied up humanoids standing in the center of - yet distinctly apart from - the party, like a seed amidst soil.*
*As he approached he took in the sheer wonder of the sight of them: like walking into a different world entirely.*
*They were ethereal in their beauty, delicate in their movements. Some were tall, taller than even an Orc, but spindly in body, as if a shallow breeze might break them apart into seafoam.*
*Others were short, diminutive, sporting thick noses and even thicker brows. Heads like boulders hewn from rock, and grassy beards the color of the ocean.*
*All of them - be they human sized or ogre sized were beautiful, without exception. They carried with them distinctly Faelike characteristics: horns, claws, elongated toes or overthin fingers.*
*Their clothing was as resplendent as they were: loose fitting gowns and sharply cut tunics of a far more libertine style than one would find amongst stuffy Rosarian nobility.*
*They were a colourful bunch, both in demeanor and in clothing. Everywhere one looked there were vibrant reds and oranges, shimmering blues and purples, electric yellows and greens. When Rowan felt their gazes fall upon him, he saw those same colors in their otherworldly eyes.*
Arzyl: "Sir Rowan, allow me to introduce to you some of the finest members of the Midnight Court."
Arzyl: "Lord Rowan, allow me to introduce to you some of the finest members of the Midnight Court."
Arzyl: "This is but a sampling of our full glory, of course. I handpicked those who would be in attendance, based on the latest developments in the court during my absence."
Rowan: "…Developments?"
Arzyl: "The Midnight Court is the pinnacle of Fae society, orbiting our dear Queen Kassandra in waiting on her hand-and-foot."
Arzyl: "Such proximity to her luminosity is a coveted position. Everyone always wants a… closer look."
Arzyl: "You can imagine that such jostling for position can breed a bit of squabbling."
Arzyl: "But enough about politics, you simply must say hello!"
*As Rowan stepped up he felt the multifarious eyes of over a dozen immortals turn their gazes upon him. They enclosed him like a circle, with only Arzyl’s steady hand upon his shoulder to ground him to reality.*
*A pale, grinning female extended her hand to Rowan, chitinous black armor encircling her arm up to the wrist. After a moment's hesitation, Rowan took it. She smiled warmly at him, showing pearlescent teeth filed into points.*
Arzyl: "May I introduce: Lady Ordspythe of the Seven Wings."
*Lady Ordspythe’s eyes narrowed on Rowan’s features, studying them with black-eyed intensity.*
Arzyl: "Lady Ordspythe? This is that charming mortal I told you about: Rowan Blackwell."
Lady Ordspythe: "…The little Seneschal? Lady Arzyl, you’ve caught me quite off guard! I did not expect such an august introduction so soon into the party!"
Lady Ordspythe: "How do you do, Sir Rowan? A pleasure to meet you!"
Lady Ordspythe: "How do you do, Lord Rowan? A pleasure to meet you!"
*Rowan saw what Arzyl was doing, and so he played the part of the country bumpkin. Better her courtiers think him just another plaything.*
Rowan: "The pleasure is all mine."
Rowan: "Begging your pardon milady, but if such is your name, then where are your wings?"
*Lady Ordspythe giggled, reaching with too long fingers to deftly cover her laughter. She fluttered her eyelashes.*
Lady Ordspythe: "Why, right in front of you! What do you think I’m wearing?"
*The Fae pirouetted on bifurcated knees, swiveling in place as Rowan got a closer look at her “outfit. What he mistook to be diagonal spiraling designs of colors on loose-fitting, fluffy fabric turned out to be the folded edges of her wings, wrapped around her like a shawl.*
*Arzyl nodded at her, and the frilly Fae nodded back, bowing her head in deference. Rowan felt her scaly hand slip from his grasp.*
*And so it went, one dizzying introduction after the next. The greetings grew more perfunctory the farther down the line it went. Arzyl breezed past a squat, multi-limbed portly man with nary a glance.*
Arzyl: "-And there is Garthor, the self-styled “Lord of Termites, though I hear his deposed wife intends to make a comeback this midsummer. I suppose we’ll have to see which one ultimately eats the other."
*She gestured blithely towards the creature next to him: a long-necked, wall eyed fellow with a hunched back and a too-long mouth. His skin was the color and texture of a frog’s.*
Arzyl: "Harudyz the Speckle-spined — how like a fish out of water he is! A master of the flute, and of bone carving. He sometimes likes to mix the hobbies."
Arzyl: "I think you’ll quite enjoy his music, he is part of the entertainment for this evening."
*Marching together past the menagerie of ethereal beings, they at last came to a halt at the feet of the final courtier. Arzyl’s lip curled at the sight of her.*
*She was small, for a Fae. Yet beautiful beyond words. Her long, body length hair was a dark void, her eyes bright white and twinkling. She was slender, almost delicate, and pale as the moonlight.*
Arzyl: "-And lastly, of course, is Jocelyn Star-Christened. A recent addition to our upper echelon."
Arzyl: "Really, I quite preferred her sun-kissed sister. But, such is the way of duels."
*Jocelyn hopped forward and smiled eagerly, as if she hadn’t heard a thing Arzyl had just said about her. She ignored Rowan completely, her black as night hair drooping to the ground from her obsequious bowing.*
Jocelyn: "My lady, it is an honour-"
*Arzyl’s hand was in her face waving her off almost before she started speaking.*
Arzyl: "Enough. You are here to greet my guest, not bandy words with me."
*Shaken by the rebuke, Jocelyn hurriedly turned to Rowan to properly bow and scrape, but already Arzyl was moving away.*
*She hustled Rowan onwards, peeling him off from the covetous stares the Fae courtiers gave him. He saw the look of jealousy in their eyes, both of murderous hostility and of tortured longing.*
*As if a spell had been broken, they began to disperse amongst the crowds, moving to mingle with their mortal counterparts. They reminded Rowan of nothing so much as a pack of wolves set loose to hunt.*
*He waited till they were all safely out of earshot to comment on the matter.*
Rowan: "That was… interesting."
Arzyl: "High praise indeed! I pride myself on keeping things interesting for the Queen. There is nothing quite so distressing as a dull day at court."
Rowan: "They look like they’d all kill me - or eat me - if they had the chance."
*Arzyl giggled, grinning slyly at him as if he’d told a bawdy joke.*
Arzyl: "And they would! But they shan’t. Because I will not suffer such distractions."
Rowan: "And Queen Kassandra is at ease allowing her people to scheme and bicker in such a manner?"
Arzyl: "Her resplendent majesty is not the type to interfere with the minutiae of court."
Arzyl: "So long as the trappings of tradition and niceties are observed, she does not look overlong at the shadows whence one might lurk."
Rowan: "So is she naive, or simply consciously oblivious?"
*Arzyl tittered.*
Arzyl: "If the result is the same, who is to say which is true?"
Rowan: "…I am beginning to see why you were made Ambassador, Lady Arzyl."
Arzyl: "I’m glad you were paying attention."
*Perhaps we can mingle with some dignitaries from other realms*
Arzyl: "Yes! Yes, of course. It’s practically the reason why we’re here, isn’t it? Sizing up the competition."
Rowan: "I’d be cautious throwing such words around, Ambassador. Ideally, we are all aligned in our mutual interests."
*Arzyl rolled her eyes. She leaned a little closer to Rowan, her voice a breathy whisper in his ear.*
Arzyl: "Yes, and not a single battle in history was won due to the timely defection of a treasured “ally. Let us not be reductive, my lovely."
Arzyl: "If everyone could be on your side, there’d be no need for war at all. You must choose your friends just as carefully as you choose your enemies."
Rowan: "-And you think this kind of open skullduggery credits you as a more valuable ally?"
Arzyl: "Of course! Because I know what is expected of me, and what I desire in return. Far easier to work with an equal than a dupe or a pawn who doesn’t think they are one."
Arzyl: "These others you’ve collected? Well… we shall see, shan’t we?"
*Rowan overheard the familiar drone of Duke Raeve complaining*
*Near the front entryway to the throne room stood a profoundly uncomfortable Duke Raeve, flanked by what few knights had survived the fall of his keep and a small coterie of minor turncoat nobles, now traitors to their former liege lords.*
*As the premier “servant of the Twins in Rosaria, Duke Raeve theoretically had pride of place amongst the assorted dignitaries. But in reality, he was as toothless here as he’d ever been.*
*He stood stiff backed, a faint sneer upon his face as he looked across the assembly of warlords and dignitaries whom he no doubt saw as miles beneath his dignity.*
Arzyl: "Ah, is that the good Duke Raeve, I espy? Your former liege lord, if I’m not mistaken."
Rowan: "You are well informed, my lady."
Arzyl: "How dreadfully ill at ease he looks. Shall we go and welcome him? Perhaps he’d enjoy seeing a familiar face."
Rowan: "If we must."
*Rowan strode up to Duke Doran Raeve with Arzyl on his arm, barely able to disguise his disdain.*
Rowan: "Duke Raeve, welcome to the banquet."
Doran: "Hm? Ah yes, Sir Rowan. Greetings."
Doran: "Hm? Ah yes, Lord Rowan. Greetings."
*The Duke, for his part, seemed entirely oblivious to Rowan’s scowl, treating him instead as merely another face to talk to. A glass of wine was in his hand. He swirled it about in surly disinterest.*
Doran: "What an ugly gathering this is. Brigands and beasts and bastards mingling with the bluebloods."
Doran: "I am Mistress Jezera’s most humble servant, but even I did not think that I’d need to stoop so low."
Doran: "I am Empress Jezera’s most humble servant, but even I did not think that I’d need to stoop so low."
Rowan: "Not all of us can be as ‘loyal’ as you, Duke. Bloodmeen needs allies, soldiers, money."
Rowan: "You can’t just get that by relying exclusively on bluebloods."
*Duke Raeve seemed to only half hear him, his gaze sweeping the attendees like he was sizing up a midden heap. He swirled his glass once more.*
Doran: "Nonetheless, a garish event all round. Have you seen the beasts slithering about here?"
*Rowan felt the tingle of Arzyl’s claws dig slightly into his arm. There was a stillness in her body, like a viper coiled to strike.*
Doran: "I tell you: if these be our allies we won’t want for enemies. Every ratcatcher, frog tamer and wolf hunter in the realms would flock to a place like this."
*Duke Raeve chuckled to himself, taking a soft sip of his wine.*
Doran: "Rich hunting grounds!"
*Raeve’s self satisfied laughter only grew in the aftermath of his punchline. It set Rowan’s teeth on edge. The grin he returned came out closer to a grimace as he stared the Duke down.*
Rowan: "Doran, I have not yet introduced you to my companion."
Rowan: "Duke Raeve, I have not yet introduced you to my companion."
*Duke Raeve’s eyes drifted lazily in Arzyl’s direction, as if seeing her for the first time.*
Doran: "Hm? Yes, yes, hello there."
*Arzyl slipped free from Rowan’s grasp, sliding smoothly into Raeve’s personal space. He let out a small grunt of discomfort.*
Arzyl: "Duke Doran Raeve, as I live and breathe! A pleasure to finally make your personal acquaintance."
Doran: "Er- charmed, I suppose."
Doran: "…Who exactly are you again?"
*Arzyl slunk closer to him, running her hand down his arm much like she did with Rowan. But firmer, with a harsher grip. He let out a gasp of shock at the impertinence.*
Arzyl: "Oh, you would not remember me in specific, my Duke. Only by reputation."
Doran: "What is this? L-let go of me, this instant!"
Arzyl: "Please dear Duke, allow me to properly introduce myself!"
Arzyl: "You see, I spent a few summers in your lands, cavorting with my friends. Beautiful country: a fine and robust people, your subjects."
Arzyl: "You’d remember our visit, I think: your yearly tithes dropped nearly in half."
*Duke Raeve’s face paled. His efforts to free himself slackened.*
Doran: "The… the disappearances? The mutilations in the woods?"
Doran: "That was you?"
Arzyl: "Oh, I am not exclusive in taking credit, though I’ll confess to some of the more creative works discovered by your knights."
*His eyes grew wide as he unsuccessfully tried to shake her off him. Arzyl’s clawed fingers curled tightly about his arm.*
Arzyl: "…Lady Arwen was a particular delight! So slow, running in those heels."
Arzyl: "But - it is as you say: ‘rich hunting grounds.’"
*Raeve turned to Rowan, his mouth babbling as if searching for words. His eyes were begging him to help.*
Doran: "W-who is this woman?!"
*Tell Arzyl off.*
Rowan: "Lady Arzyl, that’s enough."
Rowan: "Duke Raeve is a loyal member of this court. May I remind you that you are the foreign ambassador here, not him?"
Rowan: "If you have a grievance, then take it up with the Twins. But please do not browbeat our dinner guests."
*Arzyl’s eyes dimmed to the point of nothing. She went very still. For the briefest of moments, Rowan wondered if she’d lose her temper.*
*But, just like that, she was back to normal. She let go of her grip on Raeve’s arm, smirking all the while.*
Arzyl: "Of course! How silly of me. One does tend to get too used to the habits of one’s own household, hmm?"
*Arzyl’s slunk away like a contented panther after a meal, returning to Rowan’s side with nary a glance back in the Duke’s direction, much to his relief. She took Rowan by the arm once more.*
Arzyl: "Shall I apologize to the good Duke? I’d hate to be too perfunctory in my contrition."
Rowan: "…That won’t be necessary."
*She nodded to Duke Raeve as if Rowan hadn’t just spoken, her voice taking on an extra note of condescension.*
Arzyl: "Fae customs, you understand. No harm done."
Doran: "I-I…"
Doran: "I must be going!"
Arzyl: "Ah, there he goes. Tromping off to the next watering hole to gorge his gullet on the leavings of his betters."
Arzyl: "You waste your time defending rats like him."
Rowan: "His loyalty is not suspect, which is a lot more than I can say for you, Lady Arzyl."
*Arzyl glared at him, a rare look of genuine annoyance crossing her ageless features.*
Arzyl: "He is prey, unworthy of notice. An ankle-biting social climber who dares pretend to join our hunt."
Rowan: "And what, pray tell, are you then my Lady?"
*Arzyl’s cold gaze held steady to Rowan’s for a long moment. Her arm pulled tighter around his own as she led him onwards into the crowd.*
Arzyl: "I’d take offense, were your thinly veiled jab not so off the mark. It is not the climbing that I ridicule, it’s the climber."
Arzyl: "You would do well to heed the difference, should we ever find ourselves in opposing camps, while you’ve got Duke Raeve sitting as your councilor."
*Dismiss the Duke before things get worse.*
Rowan: "My lord, perhaps it would be for the best if you saw to our Mistress elsewhere."
Rowan: "My lord, perhaps it would be for the best if you saw to our Empress elsewhere."
*The Duke did not even pretend to hear him, his eyes like dinner plates as Arzyl ran a lone fingernail down his chest. Her grin grew predatory.*
Rowan: "Duke Raeve."
*Rowan’s sharp rebuke seemed to shake him from his terrified stupor.*
Doran: "A-ah, yes, Sir Rowan?"
Doran: "A-ah, yes, Lord Rowan?"
Rowan: "I said: ‘I believe Lady Jezera has need of you.’ Why don’t you go and find her?"
*Jezera’s name seemed to shake something loose in his head. He gently pulled away from Arzyl’s grasp, and this time she let him, sliding free from her fingers and taking an unsteady step backwards.*
Doran: "Th-the mistress? Ah yes, the Mistress. I must see to her right away."
*The Duke abruptly pivoted on his heel and began marching away. He paused, turning back to face then with a worried look on his face.*
Doran: "I -ah, bid you both adieu."
*Arzyl’s eyes glowed with sadistic glee.*
Arzyl: "Run along now, Duke. And do try to contain your shivering: it’s unbecoming of high nobility."
Rowan: "…You didn’t need to frighten him like that."
Arzyl: "That I noticed him at all is a testament to his loathsome nature. It’s like watching a herd animal try to run with its predators."
Rowan: "And here I took you for a hobnobber."
Arzyl: "Oh my lovely, I am!"
Arzyl: "But a worm like him? You’d have more luck power politicking with his wine goblet; at least that might get someone worth seducing drunk."
*Defuse the situation.*
Rowan: "Don’t take it so seriously, Doran."
Rowan: "Don’t take it so seriously, Duke Raeve."
Rowan: "Lady Arzyl is, of course, speaking only in jest. You’ve heard of the Fae, I assume?"
*Duke Raeve did not respond, staring into Arzyl’s glowing eyes in blank terror.*
Rowan: "Doran?"
Rowan: "Duke Raeve?"
Doran: "I-I- yes, the children’s fable, what of it?"
Rowan: "She is not a fable, Duke. She is their ambassador."
Rowan: "You will recall that one of the primary traits of the Fae in such stories is their playful, trickstery nature?"
Doran: "I-I… I suppose."
Rowan: "I’m afraid the joke has gone completely over your poor victim’s head, Lady Arzyl."
*Arzyl held Duke Raeve’s gaze for an instant longer than was comfortable, then released him with a smile.*
Arzyl: "My apologies fair Duke, I mistook you for a more jovial fellow. I’d hoped to warm your cockles with some black humour."
Arzyl: "Alas! My jests are wasted upon mortals. A common tragedy, but nonetheless disappointing."
*Duke Raeve, thoroughly bewildered, took an unsteady step back from Arzy, who was grinning like a cat.*
Doran: "Yes, well… I-I suppose you are still learning the specifics of mortal etiquette. I magnanimously forgive you."
Arzyl: "-And I magnanimously accept!"
Doran: "I-I must be going now, Sir Archibald said he has need of my counsel, and I am sorely remiss in speaking to him!"
Rowan: "Farewell, my lord."
Arzyl: "A pleasure. Perhaps we can speak again! Alone next time."
*Arzyl watched him leave before swiveling about to face Rowan. He saw the flash of fangs beneath.*
Arzyl: "A fine misdirection. Now he doesn’t know what to think of me!"
Rowan: "That was… interesting."
*Arzyl let out a dismissive snort, waving her hand about in a theatrical circle.*
Arzyl: "A waste of time, more like. You did a good job keeping him off balance, but you’re coddling a minnow."
Rowan: "If such is the case, why were you batting him around like a cat?"
*Arzyl giggled, sliding smoothly back into place at Rowan’s side with a wink and a smile.*
Arzyl: "Knowing whom to cultivate and whom to dominate is a delicate dance. Too much velvet, and you are seen as a weakling. Too much fist, and you become a tyrant."
Arzyl: "But him? A noble title wearing a man’s skin; as useful as the sunrise underground. Discarded at the first opportunity."
Rowan: "Even men like Doran have their uses."
Arzyl: "Yes, I’m sure he’d be of great use to you, should you have need for arrogantly engraved cutlery bearing the mark of his insipid heraldry."
Arzyl: "A man like that is less than a pawn, he’s a stooge. Use his political leverage, drain him of all his resources, then discard him like a spent shell."
*Name drop Jezera to further torment him.*
*Seeing Duke Raeve’s abject fear was more amusing than he’d expected. Rowan decided to get in on the fun.*
Rowan: "…Who is she?"
Rowan: "This is Lady Arzyl of the Midnight Court, Ambassador of the Fae."
Rowan: "She is hosting this “garish event at the personal request of our Mistress, Jezera."
Rowan: "She is hosting this “garish event at the personal request of our Empress, Jezera."
Doran: "M-mistress Jezera?"
Arzyl: "Jezera is a dear friend of mine. Oh the pillow talk we’ve shared, it’d make a maiden blush!"
Arzyl: "Perhaps when next we meet I could spare a word or two for you, tell her of all the lovely things you’ve said about my party this evening."
Rowan: "I doubt that she’ll be pleased at the Duke’s frank assessment."
Doran: "I-I spoke in haste! Please, I did not intend to insult. Allow me to-"
*Arzyl cooed, leaning still closer to Duke Raeve and pulling the wine glass from his hand. She took a long sip, allowing her dark lipstick to stain the edge.*
Arzyl: "There are many things in this world you are not privy to, good Duke. Your mistress is kind to keep you blind to them."
*Arzyl nodded towards Rowan, turning Duke Raeve’s tremoring chin to point his gaze directly at him.*
Arzyl: "Rowan has seen beyond that veil, to the world that lies past your warm beds and your curtain walls and your silken doublets."
Rowan: "It’s an ugly place, full of wolves and frogs and rats."
Arzyl: "No place for a little mouse like you, wouldn’t you agree: dear, sweet Duke?"
Doran: "I-I-I-"
Rowan: "A word of warning, Doran: your observation of being no longer amongst Rosarian Nobility very much holds true."
Rowan: "Have a care for what that means, and what your place in the pecking order might be should you find yourself friendless at court."
*Rowan stared down the terrified Duke, who shrank back from the both of them. Reveling in the feeling of superiority, Rowan allowed a dark smile to spread across his face.*
Rowan: "…We are friends, aren’t we Doran?"
Doran: "Y-yes! Yes of course we are!"
Arzyl: "Great friends! The best."
Arzyl: "And a good friend knows when to scurry off and leave their betters to their business."
*Arzyl made a soft shooing motion with her hands. Duke Raeve cast a short glance in Rowan’s direction. Seeing his stone face, he nodded in agreement.*
Doran: "O-of course! Of course, of course how silly of me. I quite forgot th-that Lord- that is Sir A-Archibald, he- he uh…"
Doran: "I-I must be going! Farewell!"
*Arzyl turned her cruel grin towards Rowan, her eyes alight with mirth.*
Arzyl: "How delightful! I didn’t expect you to be so willing an accomplice."

*To sleight them.*

Rowan: "Cla-Min. I hope you’re enjoying yourself."
Cla-min: "Of course! A gathering like this? There’s always coin to be made."
Cla-min: "It’s not often my kind are included in the festivities; thank you for inviting us."
Arzyl: "Actually, that was me, my dear."
Arzyl: "Lady Arzyl, at your service!"
*Cla-Min cast a cool glance at Arzyl’s outstretched hand. After a moment's hesitation, she took it.*
Arzyl: "When Rowan told me about the invaluable services your Clan provides the Twins through the leylines, I simply had to invite the lot of you!"
Cla-min: "Hm."
Cla-min: "Imagine that, hearing for years that I'm as wily as a Fae. And now I have the uh... honor to be invited to one of their parties."
Arzyl: "The honour is all mine, my dear! I imagine we could do great things together."
Cla-min: "Of course of course! There's so much gold to be had these days. I must admit, it’s a rare experience to speak to someone whom I have no idea what she might want to buy from me."
*Arzyl smiled, as if supremely flattered by the statement.*
Arzyl: "Oh my clever friend. Surely you know that Fae appetites range far wider than a few shiny bits and bobs. What tickles my fancy cannot be bought with gold."
*Far from seeming intimidated by the loaded statement, Cla-Min kept a neutral expression. She took a long, careful drag off her pipe.*
Cla-min: "Hm. Right. Well, nice meeting you. We’ll catch up later Rowan, yeah?"
Rowan: "I’m looking forward to it."
*Cla-Min flashed a brief smile before turning away from the Fae entirely. The two continued onward, Arzyl laughing all the while.*
Arzyl: "Goodness me, she doesn’t like me at all, does she?"
Rowan: "She doesn’t trust you."
Arzyl: "Of course she doesn’t. Why would she? A grifter trusts nothing but their own gut instincts."
Arzyl: "An admirable trait… for clever prey that don’t wish to be eaten."
*A woman’s bright foreign clothing could be spotted near the dance floor.*
*Indarah hovered near the empty dance floor, clearly attracted to the allure of the music. She hummed along to the bawdy tune the minstrels were playing on the dais.*
*Rowan approached her, and she smiled at him.*
Indarah: "Oh! Rowan. Fancy meeting you here."
Rowan: "Hello Indarah, what brings you to Bloodmeen?"
Indarah: "The Twins wanted some help arranging the throne room to their liking. Give it a “festive atmosphere."
Indarah: "Have you seen the people they’ve got working on this? The Fae?"
Indarah: "Fucking beautiful work. Would kill to have their decorator spend five minutes on the tavern's interior."
Rowan: "Well, you can tell them yourself. Allow me to introduce you to: Lady Arzyl of the Fae."
Arzyl: "Oh! Is that the barkeep? Hello, hello! Lady Ordspythe told me so much about you!"
*Arzyl approached her with an energetic eagerness, taking her hands in hers and shaking them with vigour.*
Arzyl: "An absolute pleasure to meet you in person, Indarah! A wonder, a joy!"
*Indarah cast an uncertain glance in Rowan’s direction. He shrugged helplessly.*
Indarah: "Well, uh. Hello? Nice to meet you?"
Arzyl: "And you as well, my dear! You are as stunning as the stories told!"
Arzyl: "I must say: you are a clever girl, using the Twins as you do. Cutting out the competition while at the same time securing permanent funding!"
Arzyl: "Oh so clever!"
Indarah: "I... what? Are you fucking with me right now?"
Arzyl: "Not at all! Perish the thought! Without intrepid, adventurous women like you, we don’t find any…"
*Her grin grew wide as her eyes glowed with amusement.*
Arzyl: "Women like me."
*Indarah’s face paled. She glanced at Rowan much more sharply, visibly on edge, and leaned away from Aryzl.*
Indarah: "…I need to go now."
*She pulled free from Arzyl’s grasp and marched away, her footsteps quickening the farther away she got from them.*
*Arzyl watched her leave with an almost longing expression. Rowan glared at her.*
Rowan: "What the hell was all that about, Arzyl?"
*She let out a soft sigh.*
Arzyl: "Oh, nothing. Just a bit of hopeless yearning; it’s always the forbidden fruits we most desire, no?"
Arzyl: "I do so love me girls from the Dragon’s Tail. Always so feisty!"
Rowan: "She’s off limits."
Arzyl: "Of course she is! Do you take me for a slobbering glutton?"
Arzyl: "Nevertheless: quite the beauty, that one. I do so hope you are “enjoying her to the fullest."
*The sound of a Dwarf’s grumbling carried across the room*
*The grim Dwarf Skordred stood like a statue frozen in the midsts of the gathering. He made no effort to speak to anyone, his beady eyes shifting this way and that as he glared at the assembled pageantry.*
Skordred: "Mockery, tha’s what it is. A damned mockery."
Rowan: "Skordred, do you have a moment?"
*The Dwarf looked up at Rowan from beneath his hood, revealing a pained scowl.*
Skordred: "Almost a thousand years, this castle has stood, a throne room worthy of the avatar of Chaos."
Skordred: "Blood banquets, orgies and rituals to Kharos have been conducted here. Kings have knelt at its feet, priests of Solansia prayed here like it were an altar."
Skordred: "Tha’ envy o’ the world. A place to rule the world."
Skordred: "…And now this gatherin’ is what’s left of it all. Karnas’d weep at the lows we’ve sunk to."
Arzyl: "-But from humble beginnings, great things can rise, good sir."
Skordred: "…Who are ye?"
Rowan: "Skordred, this is Lady Arzyl, of the Fae."
Arzyl: "You may not know me, my good man,  but I remember this castle, both in its greatest glories and in its most abject destruction."
Arzyl: "Time may wear down this place, but it always returns. And you are a mighty part of that reclamation."
*The Dwarf stared at her a long moment, his jaw working the air.*
Skordred: "What does a forest spirit know of such things?"
Arzyl: "I have seen the armies of the Dark Lords on the march. I have witnessed their black banners waving in the breeze, uncountable in their number."
Arzyl: "We all have our part to play in bringing back those heady days, and every choice we make and ally we gather is a step in that direction."
Arzyl: "Take heart, good sir. Though we are a motley assortment, we are the seed of a new Demon Lord’s army."
Skordred: "I… thank ye, mah lady."
Arzyl: "The pleasure’s all mine. A toast: for battles lost, and wars still to be won."
*The Dwarf took a flagon of golden ale from the table next to him and lifted it, chugging down the thing wholesale. Arzyl surreptitiously led Rowan away in the aftermath.*
Rowan: "…What was that all about?"
Arzyl: "Some men wear their loyalty on their sleeves. So long as you show the proper deference, you can always co-opt them."
Arzyl: "That little architect? Bring him the tiniest bit of solace and he will follow you unto the ends of the earth."
Arzyl: "There is no better servant than a broken dog who misses his master."
*Arzyl pointed out a lone Minotaur in a far corner.*
*Rowan found Greyhide lingering on the far side of the hall, his arms crossed as he watched the revelry in a quiet place behind the pillars. No one, not even the Fae courtiers got close to his hulking form.*
*As Rowan approached he saw the Minotaur stealing glances towards the resplendent banquet table upon which heaps of food and drink were scattered.*
*The bull's expression lifted at Rowan’s arrival, though quickly grew wary as he saw who was draped upon his arm.*
Rowan: "Greyhide. Long day at the forge?"
Greyhide: "Hello, Rowan. Work is work, I cannot complain."
Rowan: "Sorry if all this commotion bothered you at all."
*Greyhide shrugged.*
Greyhide: "I could not hear it till I came up here. But thank you."
Greyhide: "…Who is this?"
*Arzyl beamed as she extended her hand to him, treating him like a treasured suitor.*
Arzyl: "Lady Arzyl, Fae of the Midnight Court. My goodness, but you are a tall one!"
*Greyhide cast an uncertain glance in Rowan’s direction. Rowan shrugged.*
Greyhide: "Hrnh, normal for a Minotaur."
Arzyl: "Ha ha! And a sense of humor too! Dry as a bone, my favorite kind."
Arzyl: "So I take it you’re the fabled blacksmith of Bloodmeen everyone’s been telling me about?"
Greyhide: "I forge. Yes."
Arzyl: "Not a man of many words, I take it?"
Greyhide: "No."
Arzyl: "Good. Better to let your work speak for itself."
*Rowan watched the slightest hint of a smile curve Greyhides lips.*
Greyhide: "Yes."
Arzyl: "Well, I shan’t keep you, then. I know this party may seem a tad much, but I do hope you’ll find time to enjoy yourself, Greyhide."
Arzyl: "…Who knows? Perhaps I may visit you anon in hopes of bringing back a finely crafted dagger from your forge?"
Arzyl: "My kind do love artful craftsmanship."
*Greyhide huffed, letting out an almost half-chuckle.*
Greyhide: "Maybe. We will see."
Greyhide: "It is good to see you, Rowan. Lady Arzyl."
*Taking her cue, Rowan led Arzyl onwards towards the next suitor. She tilted her head back in the direction of the stoic blacksmith.*
Arzyl: "Quite the personality that one’s got."
Rowan: "And here I thought you’d take him for tongue-tied."
Arzyl: "Who, that one? For a Minotaur he practically chatted my ear off! Not all races are granted the gift of gab."
Rowan: "Fae included?"
*Arzyl cooed seductively, running a hand down Rowan’s shoulder.*
Arzyl: "I’ll admit, some are more talented than others. There’s more than one way to hunt prey; I prefer to do so with my tongue."
Rowan: "So am I prey, or a fellow hunter?"
Arzyl: "Both. That’s the delight of it all!"
*On second thought, let’s do something else.*
*Enough introductions, let’s get this over with.*
Arzyl: "Oh Rowan, have you tired of my company already?"
Rowan: "I’m not the “banquet type."
Arzyl: "Nor was I, once upon a time. But we are nothing if not creatures of our environment."
Arzyl: "For what it’s worth, you are a far more canny courtier than you first let on. Though I do believe it’s half past time to really get the festivities started."
Rowan: "What do you mean? Everyone’s already feasting."
*Arzyl let out an amused snort, waving off Rowan’s statement even as she clung to his arm.*
Arzyl: "Oh pssh! This dull prelude? Hardly worthy of a Fae Banquet. We prefer our merrymaking to be far more memorable!"
Arzyl: "Watch now: the musicians are about to take their seats."
Rowan: "Musicians? But the bards are already-"
*True to her word, a small clique of her courtiers marched up to the stage where the musicians were playing a forgettable tune, made for easy listening while the crowd feasted.*
*A few words into their ears, and they rose as one, shuffling offstage to make room for their replacements. There was a strange, cloudy look in the mortal minstrels’ eyes.*
*A bone thin Fae with spindly arms sat down on the too-small stool, pulling out a pale white stringed instrument of a curiously curvaceous shape, almost like a fiddle.*
*He put his long forefinger down upon the instrument, and ran it down the thickest string.*
*It was… beauteous. A long, mournful note. Deep, like a lover’s lament beneath the moonlight. He held the sound in the air for far longer than any mortal instrument, quavering his finger like the sound of sorrowful longing.*
*Then the other Fae sat down in their assigned seats, each pulling out their own, curious instrument. A cherub-like creature with brindled skin played a harp of silvergold; a big, brutish ogre with an Elf’s elegant features pulled a large fat-bottomed drum seemingly from nowhere.*
*The room went silent at the wondrous sound. The fiddler held the note for just long enough for his companions to take their places, then he cut it off sharply with a see-saw from his fingers.*
*A long second of silence followed, and the ogrish Fae beat his drum. Once, twice, three times. And the rythym was set.*
*Then, the true music began. With a flourish of his finger, the fiddler kicked into a jaunty tube that the rest followed by. At once the crowd began to murmur in delight, some standing up out of their seats to sway to the beat.*
*Rowan found himself tapping his toe to the beat, and it was only when Arzyl leaned into his ear and whispered to him that he thought to stop himself.*
Arzyl: "A warning, my lovely: the revelry of the Fae is particularly alluring to mortals. One often finds oneself overwhelmed at the pleasurable sensations it creates."
Arzyl: "Have a care at what you touch, taste, hear, or see, lest you be pitched headfirst into the theatrics yourself."
*Her words sent a chill up Rowan’s spine. He turned to glare at her.*
Rowan: "…What have you done, Arzyl?"
*The Fae did not even have the good grace to look chastened by his glare. She merely laughed.*
Arzyl: "I hosted a banquet! And a marvelous one at that. I hope you did not drink the golden wine."
Arzyl: "Now, I must leave you for a brief moment. The Twins are coming and I wish to ensure that everything is just right for their arrival!"
Rowan: "Why? What are you playing at?"
Arzyl: "Oh do not worry, my lovely: I’m absolutely certain you will enjoy this development!"
*And just like that, she was gone, disappeared into the crowd as the bulk of the hall shifted towards the musicians and their hypnotic music.*
*Rowan felt himself carried by a wave of bodies as everyone jostled to reach the front, to get a better ear to the sound.*
*Those at the front moaned in rapturous joy, holding their hands to their ears as if shuddering at a lovers touch. Farther back, the patrons began to cheer wildly. Hopping and twisting and bouncing to the beat.*
*Rowan watched for a long while, mesmerized, until he caught sight of someone upon the dance floor.*
*She moved like water amongst the revellers, dancing and swaying and spinning about in beauteous grace.*
*It was only when he caught a glimpse of the look on her face that Rowan realized something was terribly wrong. Her body was moving perfectly in time, but her expression was that of distress.*
*She couldn’t stop dancing. None of the people on the dance floor could.*
*Rowan realized something was terribly wrong. None of the people on the dance floor could stop dancing.*
*The mood in the throne room changed. Gone was the staid, polite pageantry of a courtly banquet, replaced with a sort of thrumming energy. A manic energy. A mad energy.*
*Everyone was moving, congregating, gathering together then breaking apart into new groups. Crowds of noblemen, guards and servants shifted this way and that, moving with the music as a state of pitched hysteria took hold in the room.*
*Rowan was swept up in the crowd, moving like a lone fish against the school as he was buffeted across the tide of shifting people.*
*A frenzied bacchanalia took hold of the room as the hall descended into hedonistic rapture. Everyone was rushing to and fro, hurrying from one entertainment to the next.*
*Rowan found himself thrust before the massive food table, where guests were gorging themselves upon the food they found.*
*Chief amongst them was Greyhide, who had seized control of the salad bar and refused to let anyone else near. He stuffed his face with wild abandon, devouring every leaf, green, or other vegetable in sight, far faster than he could chew.*
*A grinning Fae cook with a potbelly and ram’s horns fed him whole cabbages at a time across the table, letting him lick the juices from her clawed fingers when she speared ripe tomatoes and shoved them down his yawning gullet.*
Rowan: "Greyhide! Greyhide! Are you all right?"
*Greyhide let out a low grunt in the back of his throat, then kept chewing. He only paused in his gluttony long enough to grab hold of a barrel of wine and lift it wholesale up to his puffed cheeks.*
*He drank and drank and drank. Rowan tried to get his attention twice more, but the bull didn’t so much as look at him.*
*The crowd pulled him away before he could fight his way through, sweeping him onwards to new and terrible wonders.*
*A lone Fae with wide eyes and a lipless smile folded his arms together as he conferred with the seemingly drunk traitor lords of Rosaria. They swayed in place as they spilled their golden wine about from their goblets.*
Fae Courtier: "But… I’m confused about your mortal concepts of “Nobility. You all serve Jezera, yes?"
Fae Courtier: "But… who is her champion?"
*They all flinched, as if the idea had never occurred in their lives. One drunk fellow blurted out his answer first.*
Sir Archibald: "I am her ladies’ most ardent champion!"
Sir Revenor: "You: Jezera’s champion?! You are a dim witted knave and always have been, Archibald, but I never realized the depths of your delusion!"
Sir Revenor: "I am obviously the most qualified lord to serve her Lady Jezera. You’re not even the dirt beneath her feet."
Sir Archibald: "Care to test your blade, sir? I said: I am Jezera’s champion!"
Doran: "You take her name out of your lying mouth, Sir, or I’ll take it from you!"
Doran: "The lot of you aren’t worth the dirt beneath my mistresses feet! You half born mongrels!"
Sir Archibald: "How dare you, sir!"
Sir Revenor: "How dare you, sir!"
*Rowan watched, gobsmacked, as the small cadre of Rosarian Knights descended into a pile of flailing bodies. Fists flew and curses exchanged as they brawled for the sake of a nonargument.*
*Soon the entire area was cleared, with a dozen knights and lords kicking, biting and choking one another in a mad attempt to win no one’s favor.*
*And there, amongst the rest of them was Duke Raeve, bloody nosed and taking all comers in defense of his beloved Jezera.*
*The Fae whose “innocent question had started all this madness laughed uproariously at the outcome.*
*Rowan was unable to stay in place for long. Like a hurricane the crowd swept him onwards, towards the foot of the throne itself, where a wide circle had been made for a different kind of vice: gambling.*
*Cards and dice, coin and collateral lay scattered across the ground in an almost haphazard fashion. Nearly a dozen games were going on at once, the screams of exhalation mixing with the groans of defeat to create an avaricious chorus.*
*Life’s savings traded hands and back again as men and women gambled everything they had on hand: jewelry, clothing, their ranks and titles, their spouses.*
*And there, at the absolute center of the action, Cla-Min held court. A half dozen men and a giggling Fae with moth wings and four wraithlike arms all sat in a semicircle playing cards with chips that had seemingly appeared from nowhere.*
*A host of her worried family members looked on as Cla-Min slyly smirked, pushing all her chips to the fore.*
*The cards went down… and Cla-Min let out a cry of victory. Her whole family began cheering as the put-upon Fae stared at his losing hand. He sighed, snapped his fingers, and a half dozen fluttering moths carried in several sacks of weighted gold from the rafters.*
*The goblins stared greedily upon the bounty within, their eyes glittering with the sight of stack upon stack of gold bars enough to buy a kingdom. Cla-Min directed them to bring their winnings back to the caravan. The family leapt to obey their matriarch.*
*But… they couldn’t move the sacks. They were rooted to the ground. Several unsuccessful attempts to drag them led to the family gathering around one like a swarm of ants.*
*Rowan watched in horror as they yanked upon the thing, using one another for leverage. Some pulled, others pushed, still more shouted directions.*
*It was useless. But they never stopped trying, even when it became clear all they were doing were making fools of themselves.*
*The pull of the crowd soon dragged Rowan once more back into the river of people. He was swept along a ways, till he managed to extricate himself once more, this time near the banquet tables.*
*Here the Fae courtiers gathered in groups, sipping wine glasses and chortling at the mortals basking on the ground in ecstacy beneath them.*
Skordred: "I… I kinnae believe it!"
Skordred: "Lord Karnas? Is it really ye?"
*A pale Fae with starlight in her hair laughed at Skordred’s dumbfounded look of unabashed joy.*
*She sipped her glass of wine, and mechanically Skordred parroted the action, taking a deep swig of the gold-colored substance in his goblet. His eyes glazed over still further.*
Jocelyn: "Yes, my child it is I: the Demon Lord, Karnas! Returned to claim my rightful place as the ruler of Bloodmeen Castle."
*The Fae made a great show of spreading her arms majestically and spinning about in a circle. The Fae courtiers gathered about Skordred cackled at his look of wonder.*
Skordred: "I-I-"
*Skordred fell to one knee, bowing his head so low it knocked against the ground in his haste to abase himself.*
Skordred: "I beg yer forgiveness mah lord, ye wouldn’t remember me. I served ye in the first war."
Skordred: "I am Skordred, yer humble servant. I have served as chief architect fer yer heirs, but… now yer back!"
*The Fae put a finger theatrically to her chin, as if contemplating the name.*
Jocelyn: "…Skordred?"
Skordred: "Y-yes, lord."
*Jocelyn’s eyes lit up as if recognizing an old friend’s name.*
Jocelyn: "Oh yes, Skordred! How could I forget my most loyal subject?"
*Skordred’s head lifted, his eyes filling with a sort of shocked wonder.*
Skordred: "You… you remember me?"
*The Fae put her hand upon his shoulder, and Skordred trembled.*
Jocelyn: "Of course, my beloved servant! How could I ever forget you? You are my loyal, royal footstool!"
*Skordred’s eyes clouded over momentarily in confusion, but the Fae mimed taking a sip from her wine glass. Skordred did the same, then he relaxed once more.*
Skordred: "I… forgive me, Lord Karnas, but is it really you?"
Jocelyn: "Yes, servant. It is me, in the flesh! Can you not see my mighty wings and rugged horns?"
*Jocelyn, cackling, flapped her arms about in halfhearted imitation of a bird. Skordred let out an awestruck gasp, staring upwards at some unseen, looming wingspan.*
Jocelyn: "Now, on your hands and knees! I need to rest my feet a while."
Skordred: "A-at once, my lord!"
*Skordred rushed to comply, bowing and scraping all the while. The courtiers that surrounded him laughed as Jocelyn sat down upon the wooden bench then propped her feet up upon the hunched Dwarf.*
*Skordred, by contrast, looked blissful. Almost disoriented with glee. The biggest smile Rowan has ever seen him wear was plastered across his face.*
*The crowd, like a ravenous beast, swallowed him whole once more. He felt like he was drowning in a sea of bodies, all stolen by the frenzy of the music.*
*Just as Rowan felt himself being pulled under again by the crushing throng, he felt a strong hand take hold of his wrist, yanking him free from the crowd.*
Arzyl: "Ah, Rowan! There you are! Sane of mind and whole of body. You never cease to impress."
Rowan: "Arzyl!"
Rowan: "This madness has to stop!"
*Arzyl laughed, pulling Rowan along as if the crowd wasn’t even there. She moved with a clarity of purpose, though to where Rowan did not know.*
Arzyl: "Madness? Dear me, did I not warn you what would happen? It is a Fae banquet, after all."
Rowan: "The guests have gone insane!"
Arzyl: "Ah, I’m afraid I must correct you: the guests are quite sane. Just a spot of fun, on our part. Livening things up, you see."
Arzyl: "The glamours will wear off, soon enough. It is quite amusing to see how easily they fall prey to such distractions."
Rowan: " You’ve glamoured the lot of them?! What are you thinking? The Twins will be furious!"
*Arzyl laughed, pulling Rowan closer into the crook of her arm as she strutted through the crowd.*
Arzyl: "Who, sweet Jezera? She adores these games and flights of fancy."
Arzyl: "I dare say we may well be a breath of fresh air in this dreary place! What with all the endless lists and armies and expenditures and war councils."
Arzyl: "Sometimes, the best remedy for boredom is a little harmless fun."
Rowan: "This is not ‘harmless.’"
*Arzyl’s eyes glowed with mirth as she tugged him along towards the musicians.*
Arzyl: "Isn’t it? Tomorrow, they will all wake up safe and sound, none the worse for wear - perhaps a hangover, or two. No one will recall what has occurred."
Arzyl: "Now please, join me for the final dance before the Twins arrive! Don’t worry: I promise to keep you safe."
*With the crowd blocking all exits with the sheer press of people, Rowan was left with little choice. He stepped onto the dance floor, watching as Arzyl led him to a spot at the exact center.*
*It was a courtly quadrille. The Fae courtiers had lined themselves up with their preferred partners. Ambassadors, courtiers, even dazed servants joined in.*
*The music was the beat, and the dance was sharp and precise, yet all the dancers followed it to the letter. The room had become a single, unified choreography.*
*And at the center of it, Rowan and Arzyl danced together. She stared at him intensely, never glancing down as she led them in a flowing pirouette around the floor.*
Arzyl: "…I think there is much we stand to gain from a mutual partnership, Rowan."
Arzyl: "I have seen the going’s on of this court: how the Twins treat you, the burden you bear as their keeper."
Arzyl: "I myself have longed for an equal amongst the mortals, one of your skills and talent."
Rowan: "You don’t even know who I am, nor what I’m capable of."
*Arzyl grinned at him, showing her too-perfect, white teeth.*
Arzyl: "Don’t I? I know your past, I have done my due diligence. Few indeed are those who have borne as many titles as you."
Arzyl: "Peasant, hunter, rogue, soldier, general, hero, traitor, turncloak, brigand, murderer, both slayer and seneschal of demons… You’ve worn almost as many skins as I have!"
Arzyl: "More, counting the number of years between us."
Rowan: "What’s your point, Arzyl?"
Arzyl: "You have great untapped potential, and I speak to more than just your skill with a blade, or the wit of your tongue."
*Rowan stepped to the dance along with her, casting a look around him at the enspelled dinner guests.*
Rowan: "Is this how I can expect to be treated eventually? Will that be my final title: slave?"
*Arzyl’s toothy smile was perfect and pearlescent.*
Arzyl: "My lovely, have I not been up front with you since we first met?"
Arzyl: "It’s not enough to simply play the game. Recognizing the pieces on the board is important too."
Arzyl: "These hangers-on, these drooling sychophants? They are ours to move and sacrifice as we choose, for the sake of our greater goals."
Arzyl: "But you, Rowan? You are an equal - perhaps a potential adversary, but one I’d far prefer to make my friend."
Rowan: "-Until such time as you can usurp me?"
Arzyl: "This is no coup. I have no need for the trappings of mortal power, nor for the Twins in general. You are a far more reasonable man to work with."
Rowan: "Then what is it that you want? An end to the Leyline usage?"
*She shook her head, letting out a dismissive laugh.*
Arzyl: "Please! A problem I can fix in a fortnight. What I ask for will be but child’s play for you to give me."
Rowan: "And that is?"
Arzyl: "The means to maintain my court’s living standards, of course! Think of it like… a tithe."
Rowan: "A tithe of what?"
*Arzyl’s eyes glittered like two dying stars in the void of night.*
Arzyl: "Bodies."
*...*
Rowan: "Bodies."
Arzyl: "Please don’t play dumb, Rowan. Not when I am being so painfully forthright with you."
Arzyl: "You must have guessed by now - or at least was informed by that fool Whitescar - of the means by which the Midnight Court reigns eternal."
Arzyl: "Souls are a transitory thing, contained only by the substance of the bodies that bear them. Every life must end, but not every soul need depart with it."
Arzyl: "That’s it, that’s all: my only asking price. A hundred a year, give or take. Handpicked by my courtiers."
Rowan: "Why ask at all? Why not take them yourselves?"
Arzyl: "Because I am bound by rules that you are not, rules I have today circumvented exclusively because of my relationship to this court."
Arzyl: "Great change is afoot in the world, and you are in need of a reliable ally."
Arzyl: "You will find no better courtier, nor a more level headed advisor. Comparatively speaking, my asking price is a pittance."
Rowan: "All the more reason for me to doubt your offer."
Arzyl: "Not at all! You are bargaining for your interests; I am bargaining for eternity."
*Rowan opened his mouth to retort, but stopped cold when he saw whom the Fae next to them was dancing with.*
*Her cheeks were red from exertion, her hair was matted with sweat. There was a glazed look in her eyes, a half madness of glee. She was laughing and laughing.*
*…She couldn’t stop laughing.*
Rowan: "Alexia?!"
*The dance kicked into high gear, a frantic waltz that sent the different dance partners spinning off away from each other like comets in the sky. Rowan lost sight of her in the press of people, but he could just make out the image of red hair flashing in the eldritch light.*
