*That caught Rowan’s attention. The loss of Orcs in those numbers was pretty unheard of.*
Rowan: "What else did Ulk tell you."
Orc Soldier: "There isn’t much I’m ‘fraid. It all sounds terrible though. He told me that for two days, some patrols been going missing near the Blackrose Forest."
Orc Soldier: "Eventually, Ulk found them. It was a mess, bodies strewn all over the place! Some with their eyes gouged out and others peppered with arrows."
Orc Soldier: "But some… well Ulk says some had thorns driven through their hands and necks. Thorns the size of cocks he said!"
Rowan: "I think if they’re that big, you can just call them spikes."
Orc Soldier: "Yes! Dick-sized spiky thorns! Whoever did this is dangerous, General. But we can’t just let them continue to kill our men. Ulk wants vengeance. So do I."
Rowan: "I’ll go to the forest and figure out who is responsible."
*The burly soldier standing before Rowan closed his eyes and bowed his head respectfully to the ex-Hero.*
Orc Soldier: "Thank you, General. The boys will be happy knowing there will be justice for Ulk’s men. Blood for blood."
Orc Soldier: "Let me see your map. Here, that’s where the patrol was found."
*It was no surprise to Rowan that when he reached the site of the ambush there was nothing to be done. Still, the foreknowledge that there had been a brutal fight didn’t quite prepare him for what he encountered.*
Rowan: "By the Goddess…"
Rowan: "This is a fine mess."
Rowan: "No one deserves to die like this."
*It was a charnel house. Bodies and parts of bodies were strewn about like scattered, shaved grass.*
*An Orc arm here, a head there, part of a torso ripped at the waist. Some had died easily. Others were not so lucky.*
*Rowan walked through the carnage, carefully examining the site and keeping his ears sharp for sounds of trouble.*
*He learned that Human bandits had also been involved in the fighting. Their bodies lay mixed in with the fallen Orcs. As far as he could tell, none of them had suffered as the greenskins had.*
*Close to the tree line, Rowan noticed several Orc warriors whose last moments appeared particularly agonizing. Each sported huge, gaping wounds in their bodies. Rowan did not know a creature that could create the kind of wounds.*
*The sense of dread continued growing, like a rolling carpet of fog over a bog. Then he saw an even worse sight that immediately made the former hero’s stomach turn.*
*Looking up beyond the corpses, he saw a bank of trees that looked different than the others. They seemed new… fresh even. The combination of dewy moss and lighter coloring on the bark struck him as odd since the size of each tree suggested they were far older than saplings.*
*Peering closer, he saw blood staining the bark, dribbling down in quiet channels to the ground. And that’s when he saw them, four desiccated Orc bodies posted near the top of the tall oaks. No rope bound the dead soldiers to the trees. Instead, branches had seemingly grown out, penetrating their bodies and holding them in place at grotesque angles.*
Rowan: "What the hell happened here?"
*It amused Rowan for a moment. It was probably better that he was here instead of Jezera. The twins may have taken one look at the message and simply burned the entire forest down.*
Rowan: "Someone in this Forest has about  as much love for the Twins as I do…"
*A strong wind washed over Rowan. The breeze felt cold and hard against his face; it filled his nose with the stench of death and the striking woodsy smell of the trees around him.*
Rowan: "The bandits... and whatever else attacked the Orcs must have gone deeper into the forest."
*Rowan took a step towards the forest and then paused. The weight of his sword gave him some comfort, but he felt quite exposed beyond that. He realized that he hadn’t actually visited the nearby village yet and perhaps there was a witness there that he could question for more information about the attack.*
* Speak to villagers to get more information.*
*Rowan turned from the forest and set out for the village. It would be prudent to get his hands on a little more information about what he was in for.*
*After speaking to some villagers and a passing merchant, Rowan learned that the bandit group called themselves ‘Dukes’*
*Most of the villagers agreed that recently,  the Dukes had made some sort of arrangement with a group called the Forest-Kin, folk who made their home deep in the forest and had done so for centuries.*
*One man even told Rowan that the Forest-Kin were not people like them, but magical creatures gifted with the essence of the trees, plants, and other life that called the Blackrose home.*
*Interrogating the villagers further, he learned that the Forest-Kin kept to themselves and only made trouble for outsiders who traveled too deep into their boundaries. Most of the residents acted like the Forest-Kin were a nuisance, not a danger, but a few here and there spoke to Rowan with fear in their eyes.*
*“The Forest is growing. I’m sure of it! “Children get lost in there. Just… games or, they’re competing to see who is the bravest. Some… don’t come back. “You’re in charge m’lord. Cut the whole mess down, I say. We’d be better off without those witches and gremlins.*
*It would be natural that the more superstitious among the villagers would blame everything on the scary-looking forest on their doorstep, but Rowan didn’t discount the possibility that the Forest-Kin were not as congenial as some believed.*
*He hoped he would find answers when he went into the forest. Maybe all the stories were just that: myths and fables drummed up by the Dukes. Then he recalled the savagery of the attack and the mutilated corpses which hardly seemed like the work of bandits…*
*After learning as much as he could from the village, Rowan Blackwell turned back to Blackrose Forest and continued his hunt.*
*Go into the forest.*
*Striding deeper and deeper into the forest, the warrior did his best to keep his breathing calm. Large, foreboding-looking oaks pressed in from either side of his path. With each step, he imagined himself a fly, one who realized too late that no matter how many times he kicked, he could not break free of the web he’d fallen into.*
*The fear was his only companion as Rowan continued, but the former hero did his best to bottle it up and focus on better things. With the practice of years behind him, Rowan gulped down his anxiety and continued onwards.*
*An hour passed and Rowan saw no signs of bandits or anything else. Making matters worse, the uneasy feelings gnawing at the back of his mind had persisted. This was no ordinary forest, the twisted roots and insidious-looking trees left him further unsure about the wisdom of his present course.*
*Suddenly, he saw movement, black and sickly-looking roots from the tree on his left were moving. They stretched forth from the base of the mighty sentinel, rising to his eye level and edging closer and closer to where he stood. The sound of wood straining and creaking emerged at either side. Out of the corner of Rowan’s eye, he saw more roots reaching forth to grab him like a pack of vicious hounds.*
*Cut them down.*
*Rowan drew his blade. It wasn’t a particularly ideal tool for chopping wood, but it served well enough when he slashed the nearest root. *
*The chopped limb fell to the ground and one of the clumps of creaking wooden fingers spasmed when he stuck. Another mass attacked, but Rowan’s blade was there again, holding them off with quick strikes.*
*He pressed on, driving deeper and deeper into the dark and foreboding forest.*
*Reacting by some magical means, the roots dodged away from his blade and then raked at Rowan’s legs. Blood spilled to the ground and the roots started trying to bind him and pull him to the forest floor.*
Rowan: "Gah..."
*The roots reached up in the air, becoming more like branches rising for the sky. They wound themselves around Rowan’s wrists, stopping him from slashing and maiming the others.*
*Rowan’s strength did not fail them. Reacting fast, the hunter shoved his entire body forward. That alone helped to break off a few of the roots, including the one holding his sword hand.*
*The gnarled growths tried to respond by snaking after his arms, but Rowan was already cutting and scything his way through these supernaturally guided tendrils.*
*In the end, he cut his way free. Breathing heavily, Rowan pressed on, ever watchful for more traps that might lie in weight.*
Rowan: "Raah… Curse you!"
*As much as his anger fueled him forward, Rowan could not break free. His body was smacked and ripped by the roots and a few thorn-covered vines that emerged in the melee.*
*The pain nearly overwhelmed him, but Rowan finally managed to wrench his sword forward, cutting through one root, and then another. Beaten and bloody, he still managed to stagger forward, leaving the deadly tangle of undergrowth behind.*
*Try to avoid them.*
*Rowan’s eyes quickly found a path between the two approaching masses of stalking roots. The adventurer drove forward, keeping his sword at the ready. Fortunately, his natural speed allowed him to bypass the roots before they ever got close.*
*He kept his grip secure on the hilt of his weapon for any more trouble, but it seemed that no other trees had roots with murderous intent. At least none in the immediate area. After taking a deep breath to calm his nerves, Rowan pressed on, walking ever deeper into the heart of Blackrose Forest.*
*Rowan’s eyes quickly found a path between the two approaching masses of stalking roots. The adventurer drove forward, but fast as he was, he couldn't completely avoid being scratched and bled by the twitching tangles.*
*The jagged, wooden edges of the root cut across his sides and his legs, sending a scattering of his blood down onto the forest floor.*
*Rowan hissed in pain and stumbled for a step, but managed to keep going. Never looking back, Rowan sprinted forward. The pain in his body shouted at him to leave, but he would not hear it.*
*Sometime later, Rowan eventually found something quite different than animated roots trying to wound him. The figure wasn’t moving, but the weight of his sword felt good in the hands as he took in the creature in front of him.*
*Her sharp ears and ashen skin made him think she was some kind of demon. But then his gaze saw that she did not have two legs, but rather a draconic body with four powerful limbs each ending in long, razor-sharp talons.*
Rowan: "… Shagaron?"
*She was the last sort of person Rowan expected to find in the middle of Blackrose Forest. He’d never met a shagaron before, and what he could remember was that the race lived far away in hard mountains and blazing valleys north of a place called the Forgotten City.*
*The Ogress was bound and secured by large roots to the base of a tree. She appeared to be a prisoner by his reckoning.*
*There were several branches plunged into her brawny arms while others were stabbed into the powerful sinew of her lower body and limbs. It was like she was being clawed by two skeletal hands that reached out from the tree. The roots stirred, but not like the ones that Rowan had encountered earlier. The whole affair throbbed and appeared to be draining the woman of her very lifeblood!*
Rowan: "Demonspit!"
*Her head moved in response to his curse and a pair of ice-blue eyes stared at him from her taut, gray features. The Ogress' chin bowed and she slowly blinked. Her expression, first looking a little adrift, even dazed, turned to anger.*
Ygriss: "So she finally decided to kill me."
*Her voice was low, like the rumble of thunder.*
Ygriss: "The tree lady is smarter… nuaah… smarter than she looks."
*The centaur-like being spat at the ground. Here and there, a coating of sap stained her thick black pigtails, and spiderwebs decorated the gold and orange material of her outfit. She had been stuck there for some time.*
*Free her from the tree.*
*Rowan stepped closer. The whole time, the captured woman stared daggers at him, in between coughing. When he raised his sword to cut her bindings, the sharp blue of her pupils looked upon him with steely defiance and no trace of fear.*
*When the blade cut through some of the branches digging into her flesh, Rowan saw the woman’s eyes widen.*
Ygriss: "Ah good! Good… You’re letting me fight to the death. Don’t be fooled by how I look or sound, manchild. Your stupid tree may have been sucking me dry for days, but I’ve still some fight in me!"
*She sounded less like a prisoner and more like a sloven drunk. Rowan paused for a moment before he continued freeing her.*
Rowan: "My name is Rowan Blackwell. And I’m not here to kill you."
Ygriss: "Hah. Ygriss of Stormrock is no fool! I can smell it… my death is coming. The only question is blade or…"
Ygriss: "Tree I guess."
*She tried to chuckle but it all turned into so much coughing that Rowan held back on cutting more of the roots to avoid hitting her accidentally.*
Ygriss: "But I thank you, Rowan.  I feared this rotten shrub would rob me of… a war-whore’s death. I mean… a warrior’s death!"
*He continued reducing the roots to kindling and Rowan realized that if Ygriss’ word could be trusted, the poor creature before him had been sapped of her blood and energy for days. It was easy to imagine the kind of devastation such a plant could cause even the strongest Orc or Human.*
*When the last root was cut, Ygriss glanced at him warily and then began moving her feet. She moved shakily, unsure of her footing while also remaining unsure of his intentions, judging by the way she looked at him.*
Rowan: "What are you doing in here, Ygriss?"
Ygriss: "I came here to hunt. I got bored of killing Driders in the mountains. But the tree lady wasn’t just some sand witch."
Ygriss: "She has real powers. Terrible powers... I cut down some of her guards, but then she moved her hands and it was like… like the entire forest turned on me."
Ygriss: "When the battle was over, some of her… children or sisters I don’t know… They dragged me here. They said I’d, “feed the forest and serve as a warning."
*Tree lady? What do you mean?*
Ygriss: "I don’t know, I didn’t come hunting for names."
*The imprisoned woman cocked her head to the side and her eyes narrowed on Rowan.*
Ygriss: "But you should know her, seeing as you’re one of her bandit saps, hah."
Ygriss: "She’s the one who wouldn’t shut up about, “the duty of the Forest-Kin, and, “Protecting the Green. The little leaf-headed bitch called me an outsider who had come to corrupt and spoil the forest."
Ygriss: "I don’t give two licks about fucking trees. I came here to hunt down the forest demon!"
*The shagaron violently wretched. Her coughs were so loud that several small birds and creatures vacated the area during her pain-filled torrent. After the coughing finally subsided, the draconic creature resumed glaring steadily at Rowan.*
Ygriss: "Get on with it, unless that branch-licker sent you here to drag me over for another speech."
Ygriss: "Then I’d rather stay here and turn into tree food."
*Do you know what happened to the Orcs?*
Rowan: "A group of orcs was slaughtered outside of the forest. Did you have a hand in their deaths?"
*The captured female gave him a puzzled look before coughing hoarsely. Her horned head slowly turned away from him.*
Ygriss: "I’ve killed a lot of things. Not orcs though, no challenge in that."
*The once mighty creature let out a heavy sigh and some of the spirit seemed to crumble from her face.*
Ygriss: "Shit. It looks like my last kill was actually my last-last. Two driders."
*She bounced her head side to side.*
Ygriss: "Could be better… Could be worse too."
*She coughed again and looked back at him. The shagaron seemed resolved to her fate. Then a strange amusement sparked across her eyes.*
Ygriss: "Hah. Manchild… I don’t suppose that after you cut my head off, you might send it back home with a note about my final hunt? Would be the honorable thing to do."
*The woman grunted while stretching out on her big obsidian legs. Her head switched left to right, uttering a resounding CRACK before she rolled her shoulder and returned her steady gaze to Rowan.*
*A thin smile stole across her face. Ygriss looked abundantly relieved to finally be able to stand and move freely once more.*
Ygriss: "You’re not going to kill me are you?"
Rowan: "I never said I was."
*The much larger being leaned her horned head down. Her stature was such that even doing this meant she was still looking down at the man who had freed her.*
Ygriss: "Well how do you like that? Rescued by a manchild. I guess there is a first time for everything. I’ll be sure to-"
Ygriss: "Oh wait!"
*Turning quickly Ygriss faced the tree and then used her powerful front arms to claw through some of the roots and distended spiderwebs.*
*Eventually, she pulled back, brandishing a double-headed spear. Grasping it in her gray fingers, Ygriss suddenly stood a little taller and it was clear the weapon had been made for someone of her size.*
Ygriss: "Never leave home without your spear. Let’s get out of here."
Rowan: "I can’t leave just yet. I need to see this ‘tree lady.’ She and her friends slaughtered several of my men."
*Ygriss pursed her lips and looked like was about to reply when a breeze cut through the space between Human and Ogress. Her pale-blue eyes slowly turned towards the source of the wind. Rowan could almost feel fear rising off of her scaly form.*
Ygriss: "Looks like you’re about to have your chance. But I’m not sticking around for another chat."
*The shagaron quickly moved away from the tree that had only recently been her prison. Rowan noticed her looking down as Grits made her exit. It seemed she had some experience tracking and was doing her best to follow the route he’d taken.*
*Just when he was about to warn her about the roots, a voice called out to him.*
???: "Roohhh…. Waaannnn. Welllll….Commmeee…"
*The sing-songy voice felt more disturbing than the rushing wind continuing to caress and greet his arms. The voice sounded ethereal but also reminded him of the tone of his demonic overlords. Not believing the speaker to be a friend, Rowan drew his blade.*
*Figures moved in the dark forest. Here and there, flashes of green and brown could be seen on their bodies. Then he saw more and more forms appearing, too many to count. Their sudden emergence might have felt somewhat impressive if not for their plainly unwelcomed expressions scrawled across their faces...*
*They weren’t all focused on Rowan either. He saw several moving past him, most likely going after the wounded shagaron.*
Rowan: "You are the ones who slaughtered my Orcs. Whoever leads you, stand before me. This doesn’t have to end in violence."
*A chittering, child-like laughter erupted out from the trees, burrows, roots, and branches. The odds of a dialogue with the forest dwellers rapidly diminished in his mind.*
*The situation was dire. Considering how dangerous the roots alone had been, Rowan didn't want to take his chances right now against such a large number of foes in an unfamiliar and hostile place. He'd seen the, 'tree lady,' it was time to make a retreat.*
*Smoothly he leaned backwards, spun around, and broke into a sprint back towards the path he'd come from. The forest folk who'd broken off to pursue Ygris tried to get in his way, but not all of them realized what he'd done and it was easy to get past them.*
???: "Roohhh…. Waaannnn. Don’t run…"
*The sing-songy voice returned but it was soon outpaced by his heavy breathing as he struggled to get free of Blackrose Forest.*
*Then he was upon the sharagon, awkwardly loping as best as she could with her injuries.*
Ygriss: "Change your mind manthing?"
Rowan: "Save your breath and follow me."
Rowan: "Shut it."
*Her only response was a brief coughing fit.*
*Even with Ygriss trailing behind him, Rowan managed to lose the forest folk and avoid the strange plants that clawed at the pair of them on a couple occasions.*
*Only once did the pair come close to serious danger when they chanced upon the dwellers. Luckily, Rowan spotted them first and was able to stay out of sight until they'd moved on.*
*However, not before seeing the strange green claws that protruded unnaturally from the hands of what he'd thought were humans at first.*
*Even with Ygriss trailing behind him, Rowan managed to lose the forest folk and avoid the strange plants that clawed at the pair of them on a couple occasions.*
*He'd thought that they would be able to make it out of the forest unscathed, but then they chanced upon a small group of the forest dwellers. A brief standoff ended when Rowan cut down the leader, but not before receiving a wound of his own from the strange green claws.*
*Claws that protruded unnaturally from the hands of what he'd thought were humans at first.*
*Rowan hurriedly retraced his steps. There wasn't time to shake the dwellers behind them, not with an injured companion. This way he didn't need to focus as much on finding new routes and leading Ydriss through unfamiliar ground.*
*Unfortunately, in his haste he forgot about the roots he'd stumbled into when he first entered the forest. He was reminded when one grabbed his foot.*
*It took far too long for the two of them to get it free, and by the time they had their pursuers had caught up. Pursuers that clawed and rend at Rowan with strange green claws that protruded unnaturally from the hands of what he'd thought were humans at first.*
*Their only saving grace was that the plants were not discriminate in who they tried to grab. A doom and a salvasion, fate was fickle that day.*
Ygriss: "Phew. Now that was an adventure, manchild! Those berry-munchers are going to regret letting us go. When I come back, I’m going to burn the whole bloody forest to ash! You hear me!"
*The shagaron suddenly stumbled and fell to her ‘knees’. The escape from the forest seemed to have done a severe number on the large beast woman. Hearing her groans and haggard coughs, he imagined that if he hadn’t freed her this day, he would have only found a corpse when he came upon the dark tree.*
Ygriss: "*Cough cough!* Ahhhaa! Traxus’ balls!*

Ygriss: "You’re kind, manchild. But I’ll live. I just need to rest. Hrrhh… I owe you thanks… for saving me."

Ygriss: "That cursed forest would have been the death of me."

Ygriss: "I know an inn… not far from here. It sits on the middle of a mountain, lots of goblins… few miners. It’s a good place to heal… and rest."

*He hadn’t heard a word from Ygriss in hours, and he was shaken from his worry when a grizzled barkeep grunted in his direction.*
Rowan: "She needs a bed and a lot of bandages."

Ygriss: "Am I in Caljuc’s Pit?"
*Not yet.*
*Ygriss smiled at that.*
Ygriss: "Then there is still a chance. Thanks to you, Rowan. You are a strong manthing."

Ygriss: "Hah. Luck had nothing to do with it, manthing. *cough* Agelvega is not done with me yet.*

Rowan: "(And whatever the hell was chasing us in the forest.)"

Rowan: "You’ll take care of her?"

*The mysterious character had been weighing on his mind as he’d hauled Ygriss up the mountain path. It appeared that for all of Ygriss’ strength, the creature had also killed a squad of orcs. But… more than anything, something else about her tugged at the former hero’s curiosity.*
Rowan: "She knows me. Somehow, a creature like that knows me…"
Rowan: "I should travel to meet with Ygiss.She should be healed up by now and might remember more about the tree witch who slaughtered the orcs."

Rowan: "Hello. Is Ygriss still here? The shagaron."

Rowan: "You’re a brave man."

*The barkeep poured a fresh mug of ale and handed it over to Rowan.*
Rowan: "Thanks. I’ll do my best."

*He felt his arrival might be just the good omen she needed. The worse thing for Ygriss’ recovery would be if she ended up pissing off the barkeep and got sent out into the cold while her wounds still needed time to heal.*
Rowan: "Pour me a beer, please. If I’m to warn her about… civilized rules, I better come equipped."
*Rowan gently opened the door, prepared for either a fight or an insult, based on what he’s heard from the owner. When he found Ygriss, the large woman with the lower half like a beast, was on her side, clutching an empty wine bottle, apparently asleep.*
*He took another step into the room and then saw her shuffle groggily. She reached for her spear, stopping only when her blue eyes noticed who had entered her room.*
Ygriss: "Rowan! You’re not a mirage, are you?"
Rowan: "A what? no…  It’s me, Ygriss."
*The boisterous warrior let out a deep rumbling belch that shook the walls of the room. When she was done, Ygriss checked the bottle in her thick gray fingers.*

Ygriss: "Haha. You know me so well. Rowan… Rowan… Rowan. I was beginning to think you had forgotten about me."

*Rowan nodded to the acolyte with the grizzled face and thick mustache. For just a moment, he thought he saw recognition in the older man’s face.*
Rowan: "(Does he know me? I don’t think I know him… but there were many that served under me during the war…)"
*Concerned, Rowan quickly turned from the man and walked with some of the attendants to leave his sight.*
Rowan: "(I need to be more careful.)"
Farmer: "You are sure… that he must go?"
*As he moved from the guard, Rowan noticed the priest talking to a couple, who had an adolescent boy with them.*
Priest: "I wish that I did not have to ask this of you. As does the Goddess. Trust me… I will look after the boy myself."
Priest: "He will guide and protect many more lost souls for months to come."
*The man looked at his wife and then at his child who gave his father a nervous look. A tear rolled down the father’s expression before he nodded to the priest.*
Priest: "Young Pyter. You shall become a guardian of the faith, a warrior of the Goddess, a knight against the darkness."
*The man of the faith handed the father a bag of gold. Rowan was quickly alarmed when he realized that for all the filigree being spouted by the priest, the holy man was brazenly paying a father for his child.*
Farmer: "We will… never forget you Pyter."
Pyter: "Father?"
*Very quickly, one of the acolytes arrived, put two firm hands on the Pyter’s shoulders, and walked him away.*
*Rowan watched the mother weep while her husband held her tight. In front of them, the priest led them in prayer while the frightened child was marched into an adjoining tunnel.*
Rowan: "(He takes some of the young to work as his guards…)"
*Make a decision.*
*Eliminate the priest and enslave his flock.*
Rowan: "(It’s time to put an end to this…)"
*After taking his leave, Rowan returned to the cave. He did not come alone and was joined by his retinue orc warriors.*
*The moment that one of the acolytes caught sight of the greenskins, they screamed before abandoning their companions and their post.*
*Rowan entered the cave with his sword drawn. The priest froze for a moment, and then jabbed a finger in Rowan’s direction.*
Priest: "Blasphemer! Traitor to the Goddess! Take up arms and defend me!"
*The people looked between the priest and the invaders as panic and terror streamed over them like rocks in a riverbed. A moment later, the priest’s call to battle was forgotten.*
*“Orcs! “They’re here to kill us! “The Goddess has abandoned me!*
*The moment he saw that his cause was lost, the priest instead bid a quick retreat. Rowan turned to his sergeant.*
Rowan: "Round them up, but do not kill anyone. I’ll handle the priest."
*Fearing that the priest might have a secret tunnel, Rowan rushed forward with his blade at the ready. He found the man with two acolytes in another branch of the cavern network.*
Priest: "Kill him!"
*Rowan ducked low beneath a sweeping strike as he moved between the two guards. The adventurer’s sword stabbed forward, striking the second guard high in the chest.*
*As the second acolyte fell, the other roared, battering his mace at the Hero. Rowan back-pedaled and dropped his body to the right, using the cave’s walls to his advantage.*
*The acolyte missed his strike, but Rowan did not. With one solid plunge of his longsword, he struck down the remaining guard.*
Priest: "Baelon! You wretch! Uh… my friend… please… there is no need for violence! I have coin… enough for both of us!"
*Rowan was not interested in any more of the priest’s words.* 
*With a sharp blow from the pommel of his blade, the priest was knocked unconscious. Rowan dragged the holy man back to the main area of the cavern.*
*The battle was over and the only ones who had been slain were the acolytes who resisted. Some among the congregation wept while others were simply too despondent to do anything other than stare blankly at one another or nothing at all.*
*Rowan led his orcs and the new batch of prisoners back into the light. In due time,  the new slaves entered Bloodmeen.*
*Even though he hadn’t despoiled another abbey, Rowan felt satisfied with his work.*
Rowan: "(It’s not the perfect outcome, but if a patrol found the congregation, there would have been more chaos and lives lost.)"
Rowan: "(The priest knew Solansia’s words, but he was taking advantage of these people. At least now… they will be ‘safe’.)"
Rowan: "(I should have let some flee so that they would spread the word... Not even caves will protect people from the Twins’ reach.)"
*With the hidden priest taken care of, Rowan left the cave behind and continued traveling across Rosaria.*
*Lead the Priest back to the light.*
*When the priest was alone, Rowan went to speak with him. Upon reaching the man's personal area, Rowan found a particularly obstinate one of the acolytes standing guard. Thankfully he allowed him to pass when the priest intervened.*
Priest: "Peace Alaric. I can see that this man only wishes to speak. Leave us alone."
*Rowan watched warily until the guard finally relented and walked away.*
Priest: "Welcome to my flock newcomer, I am Father Lomen. What is troubling you, my son?"
Rowan: "You are, ‘Father’. You preach about the Goddess, saying she will protect these people. But all you’re doing is lining your pockets…"
Priest: "I... give them hope. Hope when there is none. Demons rampage through these lands terrorizing villages and slaughtering innocents. The Goddess didn’t stop them…"
*The man kept his expression calm and controlled, but in his eyes, Rowan could see the fear rising.*
Priest: "I need the gold to leave. And leave soon. I promise you; I’ll take all those able to travel with me."
Rowan: "You cannot leave Rosaria, father."
Priest: "What choice do I have?!"
Rowan: "Stay… Continue your work and keep hope alive. But… you must stop stealing from those who have nothing."
*The man looked like he was about to succumb to despair. Rowan imagined that this very moment was the first time he’d been chastised for his actions, for his corruption.*
*Somehow, father Lomen found his center, slowly nodded, and finally looked Rowan in the eyes.*
Priest: "Who are you, my child?"
Rowan: "Rowan Blackwell. I serve every man, woman, and child of Rosaria, and I will never give up!"
Rowan: "Rowan Blackwell. And I’m not your child. I just despise liars and cheats. If you’re going to help, father… Help."
Rowan: "Rowan Blackwell. And so long as I live, Rosaria still has a chance."
*The priest nodded, falling to his knees and promising Rowan that he would fix the error of his ways and be the greatest servant the Goddess could ever wish for.*
Priest: "Will you stay with us, Rowan? Help us to rebuild?"
Rowan: "I cannot. I have other matters to handle. But the secret of your cloister will stay safe with me."
Rowan: "So long, father Lomen."
Priest: "Yes… May the Goddess bless you, Rowan Blackwell…"
*With that, Rowan left the subaltern system and continued his exploration of Rosaria.*
*Let the priest continue his business for a price.*
*In the unscrupulous Priest, Rowan saw an angle where all parties would end up benefiting. After the ceremony, he took the opportunity to have a chat with  the priest when he was alone.*
Priest: "You are a cur… and what you speak of is blackmail!"
Rowan: "You should be happy that I found you and not the orcs. A deal is in both of our interests. I won't be able to protect you or your people from them if you don't agree."
Rowan: "You’re wasting your breath, priest. You should be down on your knees, thanking the Goddess that I’m only asking for a piece."
Rowan: "Or I can tell the orcs where you've been hiding  and we’ll all travel to Bloodmeen."
*Terror spread across Father Lomen’s face.*
*The priest’s lip trembled. For a moment, he glanced toward some of his acolytes. Rowan prepared to draw his sword, but eventually, the priest’s back stooped.*
Priest: "You are right. I may be a poor priest, but I will not condemn those who came to me for aid. Speak, tell me what you wish."
*Take a cut of the gold.*
*Rowan made a deal with the priest to receive a portion of all the gold he’d raised from the poor and downtrodden people who came to him for help.*
*For his side of the bargain, the former Hero promised to keep the location of the underground cloister a secret.*
*After striking the bargain, Rowan left the area behind.*
*Information from travelers.*
*Rowan and the priest arranged for one of the acolytes to bring as much information as possible from the people who sought out the hidden church.*
*The church would remain hidden, so long as the flow of secrets and potential spies continued. With their arrangement forged, Rowan continued with his travels.*
*His best recruits.*
*Rowan requested the best of the young men that the priest had recruited. They would serve the castle and the orcs as pages or warriors and hopefully remain safer for it.*
*Seeing a way to bolster the twins’ forces, Rowan took the crème of the crop from the boys the priest had recruited to serve as his guards.*
*When the priest balked, asking about his safety, and that of his congregants, Rowan smirked at him.*
Rowan: "Don’t worry, father. Your safety is now in my hands…"
*If Rowan’s words gave the man any relief, it didn’t show in the slightest.*
*Once his business with the cave was concluded, Rowan split some of his orcs off to send the new warriors to Bloodmeen for training.*
*After that, he continued his travels through Rosaria.*
*Leave and let the priest continue their work.*
*After thinking things over, Rowan decided not to interfere with the priest or his hidden congregation.*
Rowan: "(The priest is helping these people, probably better than I can. He’s not completely innocent, but he’s no Demon.)"
*Rowan thought as he watched the preacher continue offering reassurances and comfort to another group of Rosarians who had come in desperate need of his aide.*
Rowan: "(The priest may be a bit of a weasel, but the people here are buying it.)"
*In the end, Rowan decided not to interfere. He would leave the priest to his unseemly deeds.*
*The ex-Hero believed the man was just as likely to keep a little hope alive as to eventually push his congregants too far and pay a price for it.*
*Rowan left the cave and continued exploring Rosaria.*
*An orc sergeant met with Rowan in the portal chamber. The seasoned warrior bowed respectfully to the General in charge of the Twin’s military forces.*
Rowan: "What is it?"
Orc Soldier: "A report, General. Looks like some humies haven’t gotten the message about who is in charge."
Orc Soldier: "One of our patrols got ambushed."
Rowan: "Who attacked them?"
Orc Soldier: "I guess they thought they were bandits at first, but they had their own banner and kept shouting nonsense about a ‘Free Rosaria’ and… ‘Rosaria Remembers.’"
Rowan: "It shouldn’t be that surprising, given what you and your men do regularly to these villages."
Rowan: "At a certain point, grassroots rebellions are certain to crop up."
Rowan: "So, idealistic bandits then?"
Rowan: "Hm, sounds like some kind of militia."
Orc Soldier: "Whoever they were, they put up a hard fight. Not one of the survivors got away without some kind of wound."
Orc Soldier: "“The humies fought like lions one of them said. Unlike anything he ever saw."
*Rowan mulled over the news. He wasn’t too surprised to hear about some kind of Rosarian resistance to  his Demonic overlords. His people were fiercely protective of their homeland.*
*His brow furrowed with frustration thinking about all those who would die to orc blades before the Twins were done…*
*A revolt of this sort could turn dangerous to an occupying power. If left unchecked, a group like this could form the seed from which an entire network of partisan groups could sprout.*
*Rowan’s fingers dug into the meat of his forearm. He had always known that some would try to rise up. But against the Twins, it was a hopeless endeavor.*
Rowan: "What was the result of the skirmish?"
Orc Soldier: "A good number of us got killed or injured in the first attack. But we managed to regroup."
Orc Soldier: "The boys killed a few and the rest ran for the hills. Reckoned you’d want to know, in case you wanted to look into it."
*If there is time, I’ll look into it.*
Orc Soldier: "Yes, boss. Here, dat’s the location right around there."
Orc Soldier: "Good hunting."
*There are bigger issues at stake.*
Orc Soldier: "Of course, General. Guess I’ll round up some boys myself, then."
*A short hike was all it took to reach the site of the battle. As he crested the final hill, Rowan came upon a flock of carrion birds picking apart the rotting corpse of a horse.*
Rowan: "…Not many corpses for the site of an ambush."
*It took another half-second for Rowan to realize that the fallen horse was the only dead body he could see.*
*A cautious search of the area revealed a small row of freshly dug graves, set off a little ways off the road in a stand of trees.*
Rowan: "Hmm… the  orcs wouldn’t waste their time burying humans."
*Look at the graves.*
*When he inspected the grave markers, he saw various human names cut into the wood. Some of them had the same last names.*
*The more he saw, the less Rowan believed that the group of warriors were any normal kind of bandits.* 
*He left the tiny graveyard behind, vigilant for any impending ambush.*
*Continue exploring the region.*
*He explored the region for hours. Sweat began to dot his brow as Rowan pushed on. On reflection, he could have saved himself some hassle and simply ordered a few patrols to root out the remnants of the group.*
*Miles away from the battle, he found tracks of a wagon. Continuing forward the adventurer spied a wagon on a lonely stretch of dirt road. The transport wasn’t moving, it’s only attendant appeared to be a mule, quietly chewing on chud.*
*Concerned that he might be walking into another trap, Rowan swiftly moved to a better position that gave him cover while keeping the wagon in sight.*
*A small mesa shouldered the road. Knots of small hills and large rocks blanketed the stretch of land like chess pieces on an uneven board. Any number of attackers could be lying in wait for anyone to come walking up the road to inspect the wagon.*
*Ahead of him, Rowan thought he saw some movement. The disturbance was quick as a flap of a bird’s wing and he couldn’t be sure if he’d seen someone hugging the rock, or if it was just his nerves.*
*Be cautious and wait them out.*
*Rowan waited for an hour, adding another complication to what had once been a simple expedition. He laid out on his belly like a wolf about to pounce, his eyes trained on the spot. Finally, he let out an exasperated huff of annoyance.*
Rowan: "(It must have been a trick of the light.)"
*Suddenly, he heard footsteps in the grass behind him. Standing and turning, Rowan unsheathed his blade right as a rock smacked him hard in the face.*
*The pain shattered his thoughts. Rowan stumbled forward in a daze, fingering at his hilt like a drunk fiddling with his house key.*
???: "Bullseye! You better run you stupid- Hey wait. You’re not an orc."
*How did you mistake me for an orc?*
???: "Uh… I mean I saw… Once I saw you lower your guard, I just pounced in."
*He stuck a thin finger towards Rowan and gave the adventurer a look of contempt.*
???: "Y-You should just be happy I realized my mistake, or I would have kept slinging until you dropped."
*Where did you come from?*
???: "Haha. That’s the problem with people like me. We can be anywhere and everywhere at all times!"
*Rowan’s vision cleared slowly and he began noting the features of his attacker. The first thing he noticed was a cloak painted in various pigments of green and brown falling from their shoulders.* 
*He was young, with a gaunt face and bedraggled features. He was clad in piecemeal scraps of leather armor, and carried himself with the air of a fighter.*
???: "Wow. Your eyes look loopy. I really scrambled ya, didn’t I?"
Rowan: "You could say that."
Avery: "Sorry about that lump on your head. The uh… name’s Avery. I thought you were trying to steal from me."
Rowan: "No. I’m just a… traveler. Call me Rowan."
Avery: "Cool. Like that old hero from the stories."
*Avery walked over to the wagon, seeming shockingly indifferent to Rowan’s continued presence. Then he turned around and waved to Rowan.*
Avery: "If you’re done standing around, come on. I need to get this wagon moving."
*Rowan gingerly rubbed his head to abate the throbbing in his temple. *
Rowan: "You trust easily for someone who hasn’t seen more than ten summers."
*Avery snorted in derision and turned a grin in Rowan’s direction.*
Avery: "I know what I’m doing."
Rowan: "You ought to be more careful who you toss stones at."
Avery: "Why?"
Rowan: "Some people might give you the stink eye, others might do worse…"
Avery: "Peh, well then it’s a good thing most people are slow and lazy. Now come on, pop."
*Rush the target*
*Rowan rushed forward like a hawk diving on a rabbit. His feet hammered against the ground. If there were any ambushers lying in wait, he didn't want to make it easy on them.*
*Drops of sweat dripped off his brow as he rounded the clump of rocks, his eyes steely and his grip firm upon the hilt of his blade. Rowan’s sword flashed forward and struck…*
*Nothing.*
*Rowan leaned forward, exhaling slowly, while a bitter squall of disappointment rose in his gut. The adventurer did find a small measure of success as he now found himself in the perfect position to see the front side of the wagon.*
*Rowan didn’t see anyone around. Only the solitary mule hitched to the front end of the wagon.*
*He sheathed his blade and moved up to the wagon. It didn’t take him long to find that one of the wheels had gotten stuck in a small ditch.*
*The wide bed of the wagon was covered but he grabbed the thick blankets and gave them a tug.*
*Rowan’s eyes widened when he took in the hidden collection. He saw swords, spears, shields, and even some odd bits of armor. Several of the weapons weren’t of Rosarian-make either. He saw the brutal edges of savage orc weaponry, even a few that could only have been forged by Greyhide’s skilled hand.*
*Rowan’s ears pricked up as he heard the mule bray with annoyance. The noise from the animal helped cover up a different sound. Footsteps. When Rowan heard them, his hand shot for his sword while he turned his body towards the disturbance.* 
*His fingers bounced off the hilt as a rock collided hard with his face.*
???: "Hah! Bet you didn’t see that coming."
*Rowan saw stars for a moment, his nose smarting from the hard blow to his face. Anger blazed in his mind. Some snot-nosed punk had just gotten the drop on him.*
*The little bastard hefted another rock as if to throw it. Rowan found himself squaring off against a young man with a gaunt face and a cloak made up of patches of green and brown fabric that reminded Rowan of the colors of the landscape he’d traversed for some time.*
???: "Stay away from the wagon. It doesn’t belong to you!"
*Rowan might have laughed a kid warding off the Hero of Rosaria with just a stone and a dagger in his belt… the boy certainly had some stones.*
Rowan: "And who does it belong to? You?"
???: "Yeah it’s mine, what of it?"
???: "We wouldn’t even be talking if that rock had been an arrow, you cur."
*Rowan sighed and had to give a little chuckle to that. The kid was right. After taking a moment to wipe the blood free from his nose and lips, Rowan narrowed his eyes at the wagon guard.*
Rowan: "I’m Rowan. What do I call you?"
*At first, the kid looked a bit unsure about talking. He shifted uneasily on his feet before finally replying.*
Avery: "Call me, Avery!"
*Where are your parents, kid?*
*The moment the words left Rowan’s lips, the color faded from the young warrior’s face. The look of sadness vanished quickly when his jaw tightened and anger boiled across Avery’s eyes.*
Avery: "What’s it to you, ‘Rowan?’ They're dead. Cut down near Reave when the Demons attacked."
Rowan: "And now you’re out here. Alone."
Avery: "I… I’m a soldier… Maybe other people can just accept things as they are, but I’m not going to stop, Rowan! One day we’re going to rid those bastard orcs from our land!"
Rowan: "If you don’t get killed first."
*Avery simply glared at the adventurer.*
Avery: "I’m too fast to ever let a bunch of dumb greenskins catch me."
*What’s in the wagon?*
*Avery straightened up and stood tall before deigning to give Rowan a reply.*
Avery: "Listen. I’m sorry about the rock to the face, but I should really get moving."
*Rowan glanced at the open-backed wagon. A few thick blankets covered up most of the bed, save for one spot Rowan saw the hilts and pommels of various weapons poked out.*
*He had been suspicious the boy might be up to something nefarious, but now he had confirmation.*
*The look of recognition on his face must have been unmistakable because Avery put his body in between Rowan and the weapons.*
*Avery’s eyes shined with fear and he slowly thumbed his sling.*
*Fearful eyes looked at Rowan.*
Rowan: "I don’t think those belong to you, Avery."
*Rowan didn’t step closer, instead, he kept his hands far from his own weapon.*
Avery: "You’re wrong about that. My friends… I found them. And that makes them mine."
Rowan: "I think there is a little more to it than that."
Avery: "Not from where I’m standing. So… you can either help me unstick the wagon, or you can be on your way."
*There are easier ways to get yourself killed than hauling weapons.*
Avery: "What? You don’t think I can handle this?"
Rowan: "If you think you can, then you’re a fool."
Rowan: "You’re trying to sneak weapons through orc-occupied territory, Avery. They won’t just ‘give you a warning’ if they catch you."
Avery: "What’s this ‘trying’ business? Just… just get walking, Rowan."

Rowan: "Listen to me. It’s brave what you’re doing, but you need to leave the wagon, Avery. This place has seen enough blood for the week. I don’t want yours added to it."

Avery: "I’m taking the wagon where it needs to go! And one day, one of these blades could finish off the last demon cursing our land!"
Avery: "If I’m lucky, I’ll be the one to do it."
Rowan: "I’ve had enough of this."
*Rowan headed to the front of the wagon, eager to take control of the situation. The mule turned to him and brayed. The animal tried moving forward, but the mule was not strong enough to free the wheel from the muck.*
*Avery laughed at Rowan.*
Avery: "Don’t strain yourself, Pops."

*Avery folded his arms in front of his chest, looking cockier than before.*
Rowan: "You’re very bold for someone so young. Bold and lucky. I can take the wagon from here, Avery. Don’t worry about the weapons,  I’ll find people who can use them."

Avery: "Solansia help you if you try to take this wagon from me."

Avery: "You don’t know me, Rowan. But hear this, I’m not leaving my wagon…"
Avery: "Just try me! You want another bruise on your skull?"
Rowan: "Maybe you’ll miss."
Avery: "And maybe I’ll smash your eye…"
*Leave Avery and the Wagon.*
*After walking for miles just to receive a black eye for his trouble, Rowan sighed wearily.*
*Put plainly, he did not care about the boy or the wagon, but such a trove of weapons couldn’t simply be forgotten, could they?*
*Send orcs to find Avery and the weapons.*
*Upon returning to the castle, Rowan dispatched a retinue of orcs to the point where he’d left Avery. Even if the little runt had gotten the wagon moving again, it would be simple to follow the wheel tracks.*
*Leave Avery alone.*
*The number of weapons was not… trivial, but it would take more than some swords and shields for anyone to amount to a real threat against the Twins.*
*In the end, Rowan put them, and Avery out of his mind and resumed his exploration of the countryside.*
*Help the kid.*
*After due consideration, Rowan moved over to the wheel moored by the unevenness of the road.*
Rowan: "Doesn’t look like you’re going anywhere without some help."
Avery: "I-I can get the cart moving anytime, on my own."
*Rowan doubted that very much.*
Rowan: "Let me help you, Avery."
*For a few moments, the only sound that broke the silence was the annoyed snort of the mule when it swiped its thick black tail against Avery’s arm.*
Avery: "Alright, you can help me."
Rowan: "Suit yourself. I thought you were trying to help."
Avery: "What are you getting at?"
Rowan: "You think you can deliver these weapons safely on your own? Gods you’re not even going to make it a mile without my help."
Avery: "I know what I’m doing."
Rowan: "Heh, you sound like the nobles back during the war. All their ‘experience’ and all they really knew was how to get people killed for no good reason."

Avery: "Stop. Rowan, please. I uh… I mean you’re here. You may as well help."
