*United in purpose, the two of them managed to free the wagon weighed down by swords and shields.*
Avery: "Yes! That wasn’t hard at all."
*The bright-eyed young man with a cocky swagger remembered to make sure the weapons were safely hidden from view. Laughing and actually cracking a grin at Rowan, Avery hopped up onto the driver’s seat. Rowan moved to get on but found out that he hadn’t received a cordial invitation.*
*“Eeeyaaah!*
*The donkey snorted and Rowan swore he saw the beast of burden clomp the ground when it looked at him with its big dark eyes.*
Avery: "Sshhh… sshhh… it’s okay. He’s with us now. We’re almost home, boy. Just a little further."
*The animal’s gaze lingered on Rowan for a moment before finally relenting.*
Avery: "Alright, hold on tight."
*Two hours later, the wagon approached a desolate stretch of land with a few charred trees. Just like the spot where Rowan had found the wagon, it didn’t look like anyone else was around, but his perception had already failed him once today.*
*Avery hopped off the wagon after bringing it to a stop near one of the trees.*
Avery: "Don’t just stand there, help me unload it! It would be a shame if we came all this way just to get caught here!"
*Rowan joined Avery as the young lad quickly began unloading the trove of human and orc weapons.*
Rowan: "How long did it take to get this much?"
Avery: "It doesn’t matter. All that matters is we keep them hidden."
*The final destination for the weapons turned out to be a spot beneath the stump of a dead tree. A hidden cavity had formed by the twisted roots.*
Rowan: "How did you find this place?"
Avery: "Stay focused."
Rowan: "It will make the work go by faster."
Avery: "… I found it growing up, okay? It was the best hiding spot. And now… well now it hides something important. Let’s just get to work."
Rowan: "I was only asking, Avery."
Avery: "Enough… You know… you’re not like the other soldiers I’ve met since the keep fell."
Rowan: "I haven’t been a proper soldier for a while, Avery."
Avery: "Right but you’re still fighting. That mean there has to be another band somewhere out there?"
*After he spoke, Avery looked afraid to hear Rown’s answer. Eventually, he found his tongue again.*
Avery: "Other people are resisting, right? They’re taking the fight to the orcs?"
*The less we share the better, Avery. Safer that way.*
*The young resistance fighter chewed his bottom lip before nodding quickly.*
Avery: "Right. That’s smart. Okay, enough jabbering. Let’s get to work."
*Yes. There are others out there…*
*A small smile cracked across Avery’s lips. The boy’s cocky facade gave way to genuine hope.*
Avery: "Good. Heh. It would have been unfair if I ended up having all the fun. Let’s get to work."
*You’re the first I’ve met.*
*Avery nodded and then looked away from Rowan. The adventurer saw a blankness in the young lad’s eyes, like hearing those words had burned away some of the young lad’s hope.*
Avery: "Well… doesn’t mean there aren’t others out there. Come on, we’ve got weapons to bury."
*Rowan and Avery wiped beads of sweat from their brow when they finally finished their task. Their arms and backs ached, but the hidden cache was near to bursting with weapons.*
*Avery small hands moved quickly, shifting branches and some brush before shoveling dirt to help conceal the spot. Rowan dusted off his hands and stepped back. The tree now looked the same as the rest of its charred brethren. Were it not for having helped bury the treasure, he’d never assume the tree was anything but what it appeared.*
Avery: "You coming?"
*Avery waited expectantly over at the wagon, looking eager to begin his hunt for weapons and supplies all over again.*
*Wish Avery good luck and return to the castle, keeping his secret safe.*
*Rowan shook his head and smiled at Avery.*
Rowan: "I’ve got other business to handle, Avery. But perhaps we’ll meet on the road again."
*After a moment, Avery nodded and prepared to drive the wagon away from the spot.*
Avery: "Suit yourself, Rowan."
*The boy gave Rowan a cocky smirk.*
Avery: "Having you work for me wouldn’t work for long. You’re too slow for me, Pops. Now get moving. All that sweat and work will be wasted if someone sees you around here."
*Rowan scoffed before waving goodbye to the young rebel. Avery cracked the reins and the mule snorted as it started pulling the wagon. Rowan waited until the trail of dust clouds grew faint.*
*Deciding to do his best to keep the cache hidden, Rowan returned to the dark interior of Castle Bloodmeen. After arriving, he located the orc sergeant.*
Rowan: "I found no sign of any bandits or rebels. If there were any, they must have moved on."
Orc Soldier: "Very good, General."
*The man left and Rowan relaxed. For now… the hidden treasure would only be bothered by Avery and those he trusted.*
*Leave and report the cache to the orc Sergeant to have the weapons secured.*
*Rowan shook his head and pointed in the direction opposite of where Avery was steering the wagon.*
Rowan: "My path goes that way, Avery. Good luck out there."
Avery: "Same to you, Rowan. And don’t give up hope, old man. Things are grim now, but one day we’re going to kill every last greenskin in Rosaria!"
*Avery cracked the reins with a ‘Yeehaw’ and the donkey started trotting, moving the old wagon forward. Rowan waited until the trail of dust clouds grew faint.*
*The moment Rowan stepped out of the portal and returned to Bloodmeen, he sought out the orc Sergeant and quickly reported all that he’d learned.*
Orc Soldier: "Weapons… hidden in a tree? Are you sure about this, General?"
Rowan: "I saw it with my own eyes. Take a detachment with you, the cache may be watched by other rebels or bandits."
Orc Soldier: "Yes General."
*It wasn’t long before the orc returned from a successful mission. Every weapon, shield and piece of armor hidden in the hollow would reach Bloodmeen shortly. When pressed, the sergeant told Rowan there was no news about Avery.*
Rowan: "(At least there is that. Avery has already suffered enough at the hands of the Twins. Hopefully now that the weapons are gone, He’ll keep his head down.)"
Rowan: "(That’s ‘that’ then. It’s a shame Avery or some of the others weren’t caught. We could have turned them into spies to root out other groups…)"
Rowan: "(I’m glad he’s still out there. Perhaps one day, Avery and those others will realize that resisting now will bring them nothing but grief.)"
*His business with Avery and the weapons put to rest, Rowan ventured out from the castle and continued his travels.*
*Pine needles descend in a thorny rain upon the orphan’s head. They collect and tangle in his moppish hair, like the laurel crown of a woodland king.*
*He can feel his heartbeat, quick and pattering as it beats a nervous furor in his chest. Tiny fingers clench tight upon the yew bow in his hand. His toes tremble in his boots, numb from the frosty snow that engulfs his legs up to his ankles.*
*The boy’s left arm strains from the force of the draw, his elbow shivering as his fingers cling fast to the nock of the arrow.* 
*Across the gulf of space and time, he stares, wide eyed, at the tiny creature standing in front of him.* 
*Yellow eyes peer back. Fearless, curious, penetrating. Her black nose wrinkles as it sniffs the air.* 
*The pale fox regards Rowan with curiosity, pausing mid-step in the snow as it waits for the human to make the first move. They are less than a dozen paces away from one another.* 
*And yet, he hesitates.* 
*How did he get here?* 
*Cold memories leak in to fill the yawning cracks. A blur of continuity spreads across his mind: the disappearance of his parents, the sudden, jarring shift from domestic bliss to orphaned isolation.*
*Weeks of frightened solitude. The villagers coming to see him, alone and hungry in the family cabin. Words: explanations and quiet platitudes. He does not register them, he only asks why.*
*They take him into the Elder’s home. Flashes of a strange bed, an unfamiliar hearth and foreign food made by a stranger’s hands scamper through his mind.*
*Questions. Endless, unanswerable questions. No one can tell him anything. No one can explain what’s happened: where they have gone, why he is alone.*
*Tears. Anger. Frustration. A desperate need to search, to find them, to make things go back to the way they were.* 
*He packs his things in secret, squirreling away what food and supplies he can, then makes tracks to Da’s old hunting grounds.*
*And now here he stands: three days into the wild with his supplies exhausted and not one step closer to discovering an answer he would never find.*
*The fox’s reasons for being here are a mystery, but the rumble in Rowan’s belly was far less ambiguous.* 
*He’d never killed anything before.*
*Something hot and wet fills the small boy’s eyes, obscuring but not impeding his vision. He blinks them away. His breath issues forth in great, white gouts from his mouth as he lets loose a shuddering exhale.*
*He looses the nock, and the arrow flies.*
*Quivering fingers release the arrow, and it fires forth with deadly precision. The yew groans as the bowstring twangs in his grasp.*
*A dark bolt speeds across the white landscape, punching into the small fox and sending her sprawling.*
*A startled yelp. Rowan lowers his bow and examines the kill from a distance. He caught her hard in the chest, just above her left leg.* 
*The little creature lies there, sprawled out in the snow, a shock of red glistening on her fur where the arrow has struck.*
*It was a clean kill, as clean as could be expected. Rowan lets out a downcast sigh and trudges over to where the fox has fallen.* 
*The indent of her body in the snowdrift makes it look almost as if she had fallen into a shallow grave.* 
*She lies motionless, her eyes closed as if she is merely resting. For some reason, it makes Rowan’s heart hollow to look at her this way.*
Rowan: "I-I’m sorry."
*The mumbled words slip out of his mouth without thinking as the breeze picks up, sending the boy’s hair tumbling across his face. He whispers a quiet prayer for the fox under his breath.*
*He knows what comes next. The skinning, cleaning, cooking and preparing. He may have made his first kill, but there is still so much to do. Mother had shown him how to do it.* 
*Something about the thought of his mother gives him pause. His hand hesitates as it reaches for his hunting knife.* 
*Wait… how did she do it? Rowan wracks his brain for a moment as he tries to remember his missing mother’s lessons.*
*A sudden terror grips him as he realizes he can recall next to nothing about her.*
*All he can remember are sensations: feelings rather than memories. A quiet recollection of nights spent huddled up by the hearth: of gentle lullabies whispered into dozing ears, a slender finger curling across rosy cheeks in the firelight.*
*Such a warm memory. Such a warm, blurry memory.*
*Rowan grasps at her fading image with desperation. He cannot picture the barest details of her face.The very thought of it causes the boy to panic.*
Fox: "Why?"
*A voice cuts through the frigid stillness, interrupting the dream with its singular incongruity. Rowan lifts his head, his eyes widening as he realizes the dead fox is looking at him. Through blood-caked lips she opens her mouth and whispers.*
Fox: "Why?"
*Horror grips the young boy as he stumbles, falling back onto his hands. His eyes go wide, watching as the injured Fox lifts her head and looks at him. Her body twitches and writhes upon the ground.*
Rowan: "W-what?"
Fox: "Why did you shoot?"
*Rowan’s voice catches in his throat. He tries to form words, but the world is full of sludge.*
Rowan: "I…"
*He waits too long, and his arm grows tired from the strain.*
*The fox and the boy stand across from one another in the snow, time stretching onwards towards eternity. The wind blows a gentle breeze across his face, his hair buffeted by its touch. The same breeze ruffles the fox’s white fur.*
*She stares at him, her yellow eyes fixed to his. Empty of malice, devoid of judgement. She makes no move, content to watch the child decide her fate.*
*Rowan’s vision fills with water for a second time. The bow slips, useless from his hands. He falls to his knees, sniffling and crying as he covers his face to hide his shame.*
*What a worthless son he’s become. His parents had shown him how to hunt a hundred times before. He’d been practicing with a bow since almost before he left his swaddling clothes. He could hit the fox from this distance with his eyes closed.*
*Yet… he cannot bring himself to do so.*
*Father would be ashamed of him. Had their roles been reversed, he would not have hesitated to loose the deadly quarrel. Rowan is sure of it.*
*Or... would he have?* 
*What would his father have said to him in this moment? A sudden panic strikes the boy as he realizes he does not know.*
*He cannot remember his voice, nor his words, nor even his face. He is a figure on the horizon, a hazy image in the mist.* 
*And that is all he will ever be. The little boy cries all the harder.*
Fox: "Why?"
*A voice cuts through the frigid stillness, interrupting the dream with its singular incongruity. Rowan lifts his head, his eyes widening as he realizes the white fox is standing right in front him, close enough to touch.*
*The snowfall has stopped. The world around them has stilled into nothing.*
*The beast looks up at him with a quizzical expression. She opens her mouth, and repeats the question.*
Fox: "Why?"
Rowan: "W-why?"
*Baffled by the sudden twist in the memory, Rowan rubs his tearstained eyes and stares at the talking fox. She curls her snowy tail around herself and sits, lifting her head to stare directly at him.*
Rowan: "Why what?"
Fox: "Why didn’t you shoot?"
*Rowan’s voice catches in his throat. He tries to form words, but the world around him turns to sludge.*
Rowan: "I..."
Rowan: "Guh!"
*Rowan leapt out of bed in a single, swift movement, carrying the blankets with him as he all but cartwheeled back into consciousness.*
*His heart was pounding out of his chest, his mind racing. For a moment he forgot where he was, as lost as he’d been in the dream.*
Rowan: "N-no…"
Rowan: "That wasn’t just a dream."
*No dream he’d had in his life had ever been so lucid. His skin shivered from the sensation of the cold, winter air. His arm still trembled from the stress of drawing the bowstring taut.*
Rowan: "Gods, I haven’t thought about that day in years."
*The events had played out just as the dream had shown them: with the notable exception of the fox talking to him.* 
*The memory was among the earliest he could clearly recall of his childhood. It took the Elder half a week to finally track the half-starved and hypothermic boy down. He’d nearly died.*
*It was there, at that moment, when he had the fate of another’s life in his hands, that Rowan finally came to terms with the truth.*
*His parents weren’t coming back. He could no longer rely on them to keep him safe. From now on, he had to make his own decisions, for good or ill.* 
*...So why was he dreaming of it now?*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered. The first thing that hit him was the sound of screaming. So many directions at once. The effect was pure disorientation.*
*Then came the smell. To say it reeked could not possibly describe it. The scent that assaulted his nostrils would make a man think he would never smell something good again.*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered. He was on the ground. His tunic was dirty. His pike was lying by his side. That was wrong. The knight who commanded his division had told the men that anyone who lost their pike would be flogged. He scrambled to retrieve it on hand and knee.*
Rowan: "Ai-aiden?"
*He looked around. His unit was nowhere to be found. Only...only…*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered. He was on a battlefield. Next to him, two armored men were fighting. Behind him, a member of his unit was being hacked apart by two giant orcish brutes. He looked down and realized that the stain on his tunic was blood.*
*His blood? Someone else’s? There was no time to think about it. There was only instinct. Rowan ran.*
*Shadows darted through the trees. Giant Orcish brutes and armored men wearing full metal facemasks stalked behind them, cutting down routed soldiers.*
*He joined the bloody and chaotic mass flying towards the nearby keep. Men with gaunt faces. They had been turned into animals. Behind them, their once mighty army crumbled. Thousands were dead. Thousands more were sure to die.*
*And in front of them stood the fortress. Built into a cliffside with jagged walls running up impossible angles. An impenetrable bastion camouflaged by the treeline and cliffs.*
*Karst.*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered.*
*He was standing in front of a sealed gate, along with a dozen or more men. They were pushing and shoving. Hands clutching the bars. Body parts were thrust through the small gaps, as if getting one's arm through to the other side might save the rest of him.*
Rosarian Knight: "Please, let us in! Please! By Balast, open the gate!"
*Another man clamored up above the screaming.*
Rosarian Knight: "We’re going to die! You’re going to kill us!"
*A man on the ramparts above them looked down, his face gaunt. He kept glancing back out towards the battlefield. To where the sounds of screaming men and bloody slaughter still emanated.* 
Gatekeeper: "I...gods...I can’t open the gate! I’m sorry. Fuck. They could be coming any second. Go away!"
Rosarian Knight: "Help us!"
Gatekeeper: "They’ll kill us all!"
*The standoff was only broken when another man emerged on the rampart. He wore a soldier’s garb. Blood stained and damaged.*
Rosarian Knight: "Goddess bloody fend. Open the damn gate, you cunt!"
*There was the sound of a scuffle. Rowan couldn’t track it. All he knew was that the gate soon opened in front of him. The trapped men surged forward. One of the survivors in front fell down and was near trampled before rolling to the side.*
*Rowan saw the man’s hand grasping towards the entrance. So close to safety…*
*The moment he crossed the threshold, his ears were struck by a thunder of a sound. Orcish shatter horns blowing. Men went to the ground, clutching their ears. Sound and sensation mixed to the point he could feel a sound. His bones shook and rattled inside of him.*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered. He was standing in front of the soldier who’d forced the gatekeeper to open up. Only now did Rowan see the long gash running down his arm. Where were the healers?*
Rowan: "I’m just… I’m just looking for my unit…"
Rowan: "I was with….er...I was with Duke Raeve’s levy. He must have made it back. He wasn’t in the front."
*The soldier just shook his head sadly.*
Rosarian Knight: "Lived, probably. But, gone. Him and all the other lords with horses. Anyone on four legs scattered to the interior. Didn’t even stop by the keep to pick up his shit."
Rosarian Knight: "Raeve. Crevette. Probably even my own Duke Werden."
Rowan: "Not Werden. He was caught with the vanguard. I saw it. At least, I think I did."
*He spat to the side.*
Rosarian Knight: "Guess that means I don’t have a lord now, eh? Well, doesn’t matter if he’s a coward or a corpse."
Rosarian Knight: "We’re alone."
*Rowan glanced back to the gate, to where the awful sounds of the battlefield still sounded, quieted only by distance and what meager cover the walls offered.* 
*The slaughter continued unabated.*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered.*
*He was walking along the side of the curtain wall, his gaze blurry and unfocused. Everything was numb.*
Rowan: "Aiden? Cal? Anyone?"
*He watched with drooping eyes as a group of men staggered past him, laughing near-hysterical. They held fine booze in their hands, and about their shoulders were draped fine coats of leather pulled over their bloody uniforms.* 
*They stumbled and drank more. Whatever lord the goods once belonged to evidently wouldn’t be coming back for it.*
*But, when Rowan got closer, he saw their wide, teary eyes. To these men, this was a cadaver’s party. A final send-off before the orcs reached the gates.*
*There was a priestess of Solansia huddled in the corner. Rowan couldn’t help but stare at her hair. It was so vivid and red…*
Rowan: "Alexia…"
*The priestess muttered desperate, pathetic prayers. A call to the heavens that would never receive an answer. Long streaks of tears rolled down her face.*
*Rowan stumbled on. His eyes kept fluttering.*
*Then, he was in front of a man he knew. Aiden, from just down the road. He’d been drafted in Trosshoven. Another member of his unit. Rowan was near silent as he applied a rag to the young man’s leg.*
*The gash was ugly. Bits of muscle were exposed. The ground beneath him pooled with blood and piss. If Rowan could have moved him, he would have. If he could have searched for a healer without Aiden bleeding out, he would have.*
*He watched as Aiden frantically twitched and groaned. Every fresh warhorn from outside the walls jolted him again. Rowan was forced to hold his leg down to keep the rag in place. *
Aiden: "My… my sister was just about to give birth. Don’t you know, Rowan, I’m probably an uncle by now?"
Aiden: "Can you believe it, an uncle. Isn’t that incredible?"
Aiden: "..."
Aiden: "I’m going to see him someday. Right? Right? I bet he’ll look just like her. Haha. Maybe afterwards I’ll try to find a girl so I can have one of my own."
Aiden: "Tsk. This is wrong. This is all wrong."
Rowan: "Please…Please hold still. You’re going to make it-"
*Rowan’s hands balled up on the rag. They were near fists by this point. Aiden had broken into a tortured sob, but he just kept going.*
Aiden: "None of this was supposed to happen. I’m good. My priest said so. My parents said so. I did everything I was supposed to."
Aiden: "I’m going to...I can just go. I did my service. I did what I had to do. I’m just going to go home."
Aiden: "Fuck."
Aiden: "She was supposed to protect me. That’s what the priest said. Goddess..."
Aiden: "I just want to see my sister..."
*Rowan bit his tongue. He was so numb, even if he wanted to put his feelings to words, it just wouldn’t happen. It was too much.*
*Aiden’s sobbing grew more frantic and his words became gradually less coherent. Rowan kept on holding the rag down. Just… hold the rag down.*
*Even when Aiden’s body went still, Rowan continued to press it tight against his leg. What else could he do?*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered. Some men from his unit had dragged him from the ground. Someone was shouting his name. Rowan’s eyes kept on fluttering.*
Cal: "Rowan! You need to listen to me! Rowan! Can you hear me!?"
Rowan: "Huh?"
*Suddenly, a sharp pain spread from his cheek. It took him a moment to realize he’d been slapped. Rowan staggered back, blinking. The adrenaline put him back in reality.*
*He looked around. These were men he recognized from his unit.*
Cal: "That’s Aiden, right? Goddess fend, he looks a right mess."
Rowan: "He’s dead."
Cal: "One more then."
*Cal gestured behind him. Two other men from the unit were holding a third. Rowan had to squint to recognize him as Raphael.*
Cal: "Raphael’s in it bad, but we’re looking for a healer. We know some of them had to have made it back in."
*Rowan tested his grip with his hand. Forming a fist and opening it again. Something was missing, but he couldn’t remember what.*
*A healer? He’d seen a priestess, hadn’t he?* 
*...Why hadn’t he thought of that when he was with Aiden? She’d had red hair…*
Rowan: "We have to do something, yeah. I think… I think I saw a healer before. But, I don’t know if she’s in any shape to help him."
*The thought was interrupted by a sound from above. He looked on the ramparts and saw the dark outline of a figure falling. Everyone watched in horror. A few gasped as he hit the ground with a bone chilling crunch.*
Rosarian Knight: "I guess, that’s one way out of here."
*The small band of survivors trudged down the decayed path back the way Rowan had come in. The growing weight dawned on him. He’d lost his pike. Had he left it when tending to Aiden? Or... was it before?*
*Rowan chuckled slightly. If his officer were still intact, he’d be in real trouble.*
*In the distance, Rowan saw a figure curled up against the wall. His eyes widened. Her hair was red...*
Rowan: "Alexia."
*He closed his fists into balls. He needed a weapon. He needed to do something….*
*His eyes fluttered again.* 
*Rowan was striding towards the armory. There had to be something there. He’d left the former survivors of his unit behind. Most of them were too battle shocked to even think.* 
*He found that a small crowd of men had gathered. One burly man had taken center in front of the main weapon rack, and was giving an impromptu speech.*
Burly Soldier: "We need to surrender now. If we give them the keep before they are forced to attack, they may be willing to show mercy."
*A clamoring went around. They’d seen what had happened on the field. They knew what was happening to their comrades outside the walls at that very moment.*
Burly Soldier: "Shut up. Shut up, let me talk!"
Burly Soldier: "Yes. I don’t think the orcs will spare us. But, Zerias is out there with them. He was a duke once. He’s one of them, but he’s not like the others. If we surrender to him, specifically, he might spare us."
Burly Soldier: "Look. Look."
Burly Soldier: "Maybe...maybe they’ll keep us as slaves! I’ve heard of demons doing that. Keeping captured soldiers as slaves, for the mines."
Burly Soldier: "That can’t be worse then-"
*Rowan was done listening to this man. Without concern for the consequences, he walked over to the weapons rack. The defeatist was in the way, so Rowan shoved him lightly to the side.*
Burly Soldier: "Are you crazy, what are you doing?"
Rowan: "I lost my pike. I need a weapon. Probably a bow. And a sword. I’m better with those…"
*The man didn’t intervene, even as Rowan pulled weapons down from the rack. The moment there was a bow in his hand, he felt good again. In the fight before he’d been forced to use that unwieldy stick. But, this was a weapon he knew.*
*He faintly remembered trudging through snow, his sights on a fox…*
Burly Soldier: "You can’t be serious. Look at you. You had to have just come from out there."
*Rowan shrugged.*
Rowan: "There are still people out there. The fight isn’t done."
Rowan: "..."
Rowan: "Can’t just stand around here doing nothing."
*Whatever calm remaining broke. Individual soldiers shouted words that might be extreme in another circumstance. Some were directed at the burly man who’d been giving the speech. Some probably were shouting at him. Rowan didn't much care.*
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered. He walked out of the armory, back towards the gate. But, a dozen or so men followed him from the gathering. It was almost annoying, being followed. One particularly bothersome fellow was hovering at his shoulder, voicing his worries aloud.*
Rosarian Knight: "One man can’t keep the route of retreat open single handedly. The orcs will crash over you like a wave. This is suicide."
Rowan: "Can’t just do nothing."
*The annoying man didn’t stop following him. Neither did any of the others. So Rowan kept marching forward.*
*His eyes fluttered.  He was standing at the edge of the gate again. There were men all around him now. Others who’d seen them leaving. Rowan hadn’t planned any of this. *
*He stopped, and his little band of followers stopped too. Eyes on him. Waiting to see what he did. When he continued, they started back up in tandem.*
*More of the survivors seemed to drift into the small band by the moment. By the time Rowan reached the gate, there must have been at least fifty of them.*
*The gatekeeper raised the portcullis for this small force. Rowan’s grip tightened on his bow, the higher it got. There was a battle to fight on the other side. His day wasn’t done.*
*Then, bloody chaos in front of him, Rowan charged forward. Around him a cry went out. The other men were shouting.* 
*Rowan’s eyes fluttered. Then the sound drifted away. Rowan was alone.*
*He looked behind him, and found a single soldier standing in awe. A female levy with a face that Rowan almost recognized...but he couldn’t place it...*
Female Soldier: "How did you do that?"
Rowan: "How did I do what?"
Female Soldier: "Take command, lead those men back into that awful situation."
Female Soldier: "You kept a level head, when all the world was collapsing around you. No one else did. Just you."
Female Soldier: "You knew what awaited you when you led them back into those woods…"
*Rowan swallowed. His throat felt tight as he realized he wasn’t breathing. He’d never noticed it before in all the chaos of battle, but the soldier’s eyes were a brilliant, piercing yellow.*
Female Soldier: "Why did you choose to go back out there?"
Rowan: "It wasn’t even a choice. I… I just couldn’t sit by and let things happen."
Female Soldier: "Why not?"
*Rowan felt as if his heart was about to burst from his chest.*
Rowan: "Bec-"
Rowan: "Guh!"
*...Someone’s coming.*
*You’d best wake up.*
*Rowan blinked the bleary sleep from his eyes and sat up off the cold ground. How long had he been asleep? His stomach rumbled with unfulfilled hunger.*
*He was… in the dungeons. The Twins had captured him. He’d been their prisoner for months.*
*His head swam as he looked around for the source of the voice that had woken him up.*
Rowan: "Hello?"
*No response. Perhaps he’d just imagined it.*
*Soft footsteps echoed down the dungeon hallway. Rowan watched the flickering shadow beneath the door as the visitor stopped outside his cell.*
*He held his breath. The door swung open with a yawning creak, revealing his tormenter.*
Jezera: "Hello hero, it has been a while."
Rowan: "Demon."
*Jezera’s eyes trailed across his bruised and broken form. Her mouth twisted into a dissatisfied frown.*
Jezera: "It seems my brother’s goons have done a number on you."
Jezera: "I warned you that this would happen, didn’t I?"
Rowan: "Is that what you came down here for? To say ‘I told you so’?"
Jezera: "No. I came to try and talk some sense into you."
Rowan: "And I’m sure I can hazard a guess as to what you think the ‘sensible’ option is."
Jezera: "Isn’t it obvious?"
Jezera: "It’s been months, Rowan. There’s no hope of escape. No one is coming to your rescue."
Jezera: "Are you really this stubborn? Do you honestly intend to rot alone in this cell for the rest of your life?"
Rowan: "Compared to the alternative? Rotting is preferable."
*She sat down across from him on the cold floor of his cell, crossing her legs as she leaned her back against the wall.*
Jezera: "You’ll die here if you refuse Andras’ offer, you realize that."
Rowan: "I know."
Jezera: "Then why persist with this pointless resistance?"
Rowan: "You two aren’t giving me much say in the matter."
Jezera: "Staying here is a choice, Rowan."
*There was an odd cadence to Jezera’s voice, a forlorn tone he could not quite place.*
Jezera: "Why follow a hopeless path, when you know what it will cost you?"
Rowan: "Because some things are worth more to me than my life."
Jezera: "..."
Jezera: "Like what?"
*My honour.*
Jezera: "But what of your wife, Rowan? What of the people you swore to protect?"
Jezera: "You cannot embrace a concept; you cannot hold honour in your arms and tell it that you love it."
Jezera: "No one save Andras and I will know what became of you. Your last valiant act will go unnoticed, unrecognized, unremembered."
Jezera: "Your honour means nothing. It is as fleeting as a gust of wind. What about the life you’re trying to build? The family you’re trying to create?"
Jezera: "What good is honour to a man fettered in chains?"
*My wife.*
Jezera: "And you think defying us will ensure her safety?"
Jezera: "What makes you think we care about Alexia any more than the dozens of your townsfolk that we’ve slaughtered already?"
Jezera: "Will you really choose to die down here without ever seeing her again, deluded in the thought that she’s somehow safe in our clutches?"
Jezera: "Are you really willing to let that happen to the woman you supposedly love?"
*The lives of innocents.*
Jezera: "So you will damn yourself and your loved ones to a terrible fate, all for the sake of… an abstraction?"
Jezera: "What even is an ‘innocent,’ Rowan? How do you measure the value of a stranger's life in comparison to your own?"
Jezera: "You are gambling everything on the erroneous assumption that somewhere, somehow, the scales of cosmic justice will balance in your favour."
Jezera: "You will never live to see if you guessed correctly."
*My pride.*
Jezera: "Your stubbornness is to be admired."
Jezera: "But what good is your pride, if everything you have reason to be proud of has been stripped away?"
Jezera: "We’ve already stolen your life, your wife, your dignity, and your honor. We have been lenient thus far: if I hadn’t overruled Andras, he would have already thrown you into the wulump pit."
Jezera: "Your pride will not protect you from your fate, and it will be a trifling thing to take away from you."
*You wouldn't understand.*
Jezera: "No. I don’t. So help me understand, Rowan."

Servant: "I-I wasn't sure which you wanted me to grab–"

Tue-San: "No. It would appear that many mistakes were made today when it comes to security. A matter that Mai and I will need to discuss in detail later."
*Tue-San glared at her sister bitterly. Tue-Mai cocked her head to the side, confused by her sister's malice.*
Tue-Mai: "I've got guards on it right now–"
Tue-San: "The fact that we are having this conversation is unacceptable, sister. No one should have gotten past your defences in the first place."
*Tue-Row placed a hand on Tue-San’s upper arm, a gesture that seemed to calm her a fraction.*
Tuerow: "Relax, relax. I’m sure that whoever she has on the job is well qualified, Tue-San."
*Tue-San didn't appear convinced, but didn't put up a further argument.*
Rowan: "If you didn’t catch the assassin on the scene, the first step would be to put together a list of suspects. Is there anyone who’d have a motive to make an attempt on your life?"
*Tue-Row and Tue-San stared at each blankly, then looked back at Rowan. Then, the goblin prince broke into laughter, joined by Tue-Mai. *
Tuerow: "How about half of the forest?"
Tuerow: "Rowan, my new friend, do you really believe that I could fight a war of unification throughout the whole damn woods without leaving enemies everywhere?"
Tuerow: "Dozens, maybe even hundreds of dispossessed clan leaders, arrogant former princelings, and folks with sworn vendettas?"
*He coughed weakly, the strain of his laughter less than positive for his current condition. Tue-San rushed over to ensure it wasn’t something serious.*
Tuerow: "This isn't the first attempt on my life, and it certainly won't be the last. Important to be sure, but not worth stressing over. Just gotta up the guards and keep our eyes open."
*Rowan furrowed his eyebrows. Tue-Row’s carefree handling of the issue could’ve been just another sign of his daredevil attitude, but for a variety of reasons, he couldn’t let it slide.*
Rowan: "Tue-Row, when you negotiated your alliance with us, it was under the pretext of being the undisputed ruler of the goblin?"
Rowan: "You almost getting killed not long afterwards is leaving me with a lot of doubts."
Rowan: "So I think we can at least discuss the most likely suspects."
*Tue-Row didn’t answer at first. Tue-San was looking at him with an expression Rowan could not quite read. Finally, a small smile appeared on his lips, and the goblin prince nodded.*
Tue-San: "Mai, mind emptying the room for us?"
Tue-Mai: "You got it, boss."
*Rowan, Tue-Row, and Tue-San waited while the room was emptied of anyone who might overhear such a delicate conversation. Both Tue-Row and Tue-San went silent with contemplation.*
*When the amphitheatre had been emptied save for the four, and Tue-Mai had rejoined them, the conversation restarted.*
Tuerow: "If I had to narrow it down to a list, it wouldn’t be that difficult. It wouldn’t be much of a surprise if I learned any of them were the mastermind."
Tue-Mai: "But there are certainly ones with more motive. If you wanted to gamble about it with me, I’d put all my money on Zii."
*Tue-Row’s smile faded from his face and he eyed Tue-Mai skeptically.*
Tuerow: "…Zii does have a bit of a mean streak, doesn’t she?"
Rowan: "Zii? Is she someone important?"
*Tue-Row started to chuckle, but an annoyed Tue-San stopped him.*
Tuerow: " Important? I’d say so."
Tuerow: "I told you I was getting married, Rowan. Zii is to be the blushing bride."
*Rowan stared at him, waiting for the punchline to their joke. Nothing came. Neither did Tue-San nor Tue-Mai interject to correct him. He was being completely serious.*
*Rowan put a hand on his forehead.*
Rowan: "Your fiancée is on the list?"
Tue-Mai: "Top of the list, I’d say."
Rowan: "Yes, excuse me. Your fiancée is on the top of the list. Thank you Tue-Mai, how silly of me."
Tuerow: "Yes, well, Zii and I have a… complicated relationship, you could say…"
Tuerow: "What I told Jezera was true. Make no mistake, Rowan, when I speak, I do so for all of my people. I am the undisputed master of Blackholt. I broke the clans. I rule Blackholt. And when I am crowned at my wedding, I will be the goblin king."
Tuerow: "…But there are some parties who haven’t accepted the new reality."
Rowan: "That’s the very definition of “disputing something, Tue-Row."
Rowan: "This is what you meant before by “omitting a few details, isn’t it?"
Tuerow: "I suppose so, heh."
Tuerow: "There is still one major armed band out there making trouble. Fighting battles. Giving me headaches like you couldn’t imagine. And Zii runs at the head of them."
Rowan: "So your fiancée is…the leader of a rival army."
Tue-San: "She’s an enemy. She wants to break Tue-Row down into submission and take over Hoz'Holt for herself."
*Her voice was rife with scorn. Tue-Row simply nodded in agreement, as if the thought were almost… amusing?*
*Rowan struggled to wrap his head around their relationship. In his own engagement to Alexia, he recalled the giddiness and lovestruck emotion that sometimes overwhelmed him when he thought of her. But then, political marriages were not unheard of in Rastedel or abroad.*
*Still, such arrangements were normally between allies. Why would you ever marry someone who was callously trying to murder you?*
Rowan: "So this Zii woman is your enemy…And you decided to propose to her?"
*That’s absolutely insane.*
Rowan: "This borders on insanity, Tue-Row."
Tuerow: "As do many great schemes. I am sure The Great Trickster of all people understands it."
*That is surprisingly smart.*
Rowan: "A little unorthodox, but I suppose that’s one way of making allies."
Tuerow: "Ha! I knew that a man called “The Great Trickster would approve of it."
Tuerow: "You can conquer by winning wars. But, there are also other ways to take power. And while it might be hard to know how long it will take you to win a war. Marriage has a higher certainty to it. So I proposed and she agreed."
Tuerow: "But, Zii didn’t agree to everything. I also offered her an armistice right along with the proposal, and…"
Tue-San: "The madwoman remains in the field. She plans to wage bloody war the entire time until their wedding day."
Tuerow: "Yes. That."
*Rowan ran a hand along his cheek and pondered what they were saying. At least one mystery had been resolved. Why had he asked Jezera not to join the campaign on Rosaria immediately? Because he was still in the middle of a war.*
*…With his own bride-to-be…*
Tuerow: "I have a feeling it isn’t Zii, though."
*Tue-Mai opened her mouth to object, but Tue-Row raised a hand to silence her.*
Tuerow: "Sure, she’s bloodthirsty. But, she doesn’t really rely on assassins much, does she? It’s not her style."
*Tue-Row let his voice drop to a lower, darker tone.*
Tuerow: "Besides, when it comes to me, she has another plan."
*Tue-San's face contorted in disgust. Rowan was about to ask him what he meant by “another plan but Tue-Mai evidently still wanted to push the idea further.*
Tue-Mai: "It could still be her, though! You shouldn't discount her because of a 'feeling'. We’ve both fought her. You know what she’s capable of."
Tue-Mai: "Those kinds of assumptions could get you–"
*A knock at the doorway interrupted her. A rugged goblin in guardsmen armour hurried up beside Tue-Mai with a piece of parchment. The conversation stopped dead while they had company.*
*Tue-Mai reviewed it before tucking it away. Tue-san raised a brow at her sister.*
Tue-San: "Well…?"
Tue-Mai: "They've found something they think the assassin might've dropped. Possible weapon, although unlikely; I'm going to go check it out. I'll do a sweep of the city while I'm out."
Tue-San: "Report back what you find."
Tue-Mai: "Aye aye, Sister."
*Tue-Mai gave a mock salute to Rowan and the other goblins before stepping out of the room. Tue-San sighed and shook her head before jumping back into their previous discussion.*
Tue-San: "I'll add Zii to the list, but I have a stronger suspicion toward Che-Lin."
Tuerow: "Che-Lin? Hm… I mean, it’s possible. Certainly a more plausible option than Zii."
Tue-San: "…My Prince, whatever you might think of that hag, you cannot deny she has a motive. When you consider your personal history with her…"
*Rowan tapped his foot.*
Rowan: "That sounds like a promising lead. Care to explain?"
Tuerow: "Che-Lin is the matriarch and high priestess of the Che clan, one of the four great clans. And she’s probably my oldest friend in the entire forest."
Tuerow: "After I took over the Tue clan and the war began, she was the only one willing to rally to my aid. We fought side by side for a long time."
*Tue-San clicked her tongue. Clearly she was not particularly approving of the wistful tone Tue-Row had taken.*
Rowan: "You sound almost fond of her."
Tuerow: "She’s a brilliant woman. I fear, even after all these years, I will always have a certain respect for her."
Rowan: "You respect her, But now you suspect her of trying to murder you?"
*Both goblins just stared at him. Rowan rubbed his forehead again, trying to fight back the building headache.*
Rowan: "Right, goblin politics, of course. But, that still doesn’t explain why you suspect her."
Tuerow: "Last time you came I told you a goblin truism, remember? “If you shiv someone in the back, you better hope they die and all that?"
Rowan: "…Yes?"
Tuerow: "Well, it’s exactly that. I stabbed her in the back."
*Rowan blinked.*
Rowan: "Stabbed. You mean like-"
*Tue-Row mimed the act of stabbing, using his working arm.*
Tuerow: "Literally stabbed her in the back. At a victory party for our combined forces and everything. Oh man, you should have seen her face when I did it. It was perfect."
Rowan: "…Perfect?"
Tuerow: "Well, I feel bad about it, don’t get me wrong. But, surely you understand the thrill of a plan coming together just right?"
Rowan: "…I can’t say I do?"
Rowan: "Mmm. Yeah, I do know that feeling."
Rowan: "…Maybe."
Tue-San: "If it had truly been a perfect plan, you would have actually finished her off."
Tuerow: "Ha! True. Should have aimed for the vitals. Getting her alive turned out not to be the right play"
*Tue-San offered no retort. Rowan stepped back into the conversation, trying to get a handle on what he was hearing.*
Rowan: "Okay, so that would explain why she might wish to see you dead. But…why would you do such a thing in the first place?"
*Tue-San raised an eyebrow.*
Tue-San: "For a human called “The Great Trickster you’re quite dense to deception, aren’t you? One has to wonder if you’re truly this “Great Trickster at all?"
*But, yet again, before she could work herself up, Tue-Row intervened in Rowan’s defence.*
Tuerow: "Don't be so hard on him, Tue-San. Even the most clever of humans might have some difficulty here. Goblin culture and human culture are…different; it's not fair to expect him to see things the way we do."
Tuerow: "Let me try to explain. Humans have their way of doing things. And goblins have our way."
Tuerow: "Humans...I didn’t understand how your people functioned for a long time. But, I have come to learn."
Tuerow: "You can serve an ideal. A god, a concept, a cause. Your people often die for such things. But, what’s more important is that you rely on that loyalty in others. That is the magic you used to destroy us."
Tuerow: "That trust allows your cities to fight as massed armies. Humans lie and cheat and betray at times. But, any goblin whose known humans has had to learn how to deal with that need for mutual trust."
*Rowan raised an eyebrow. He made note of the familiarity Tue-Row spoke with.*
Tuerow: "Goblins are different, but they don’t have to be. Until I came along, the only rule when it comes to goblins and loyalty is this. Your clan before everything. A problem that Che-Lin, for all her brilliance, couldn’t truly see."
Tuerow: "You could say that there’s “rules of the game. And if you stand to gain from betraying someone, well, the rules say it’s all good as far goblins are concerned. It’s a different way of thinking about things."
Rowan: "Is this just you telling me, “Goblin Politics again?"
*Tue-Row shrugged.*
Tuerow: "It’s a state of affairs trying to change it. I want it to be “your people before everything. But, if you wish to accomplish much here, Rowan, you must remember it."
*Rowan pursed his lips. It certainly would explain much of what he’d learned since coming here. But, still. If that’s how goblins see things, how could he trust Tue-Row. Suddenly, the deal with Jezera was looking much shakier than he had suspected. *
Rowan: "…I see."
Tuerow: "That’s what happened with Che-Lin. She just didn’t see things the way I did. And it didn’t matter how fond of her I was if she was standing in the way of unification. I had to do it."
*Tue-San nodded at this point. Practically the first thing that Tue-Row had said about the woman that his majordomo was on board with. *
Rowan: "…You don't seem quite as fond of her as your prince."
Tue-San: "His Excellency’s mind is beyond my question. But, I don’t understand his…nostalgia for her. The old order and all those who stand against Tue-Row's ideals must be crushed."
Tue-San: "She and all her follows blind themselves with the past. They cannot see the future, although it is right in front of their eyes."
*Tue-Row rubbed his shoulder.*
Tuerow: "Che-Lin is a possible culprit, I'll admit. But, I have my doubts about her too. Personal reasons. I’m going to ask you to trust me on this one, Tue-San."
*Tue-San snapped to attention.*
Tue-San: "Always, my Prince."
*Tue-San shifted her glance. Rowan had doubts that Tue-San truly believed what Tue-Row had said. But, the woman’s loyalty to her sovereign seemed without reproach.*
Tue-San: "Then, aside from Zii-Zii and Che-Lin, I think it best to start looking at our own people. It's likely there are traitors in our own numbers; not everyone quite understands the new facts of the world yet."
Rowan: "Someone inside the city?"
*Tue-Row sighed.*
Tuerow: "It pains me to think about it, believe me. But, it's possible. I’ve had to kill a lot of goblins to get where I am. Frankly, more than I’m happy with. And who can say how many people here bent the knee to me, while holding their daggers behind their back?"
Tue-San: "No more dead than was necessary for the cause."
*Tue-San’s harsh certainty stood in contrast to that small, vulnerable chink in Tue-Row’s usual armor of confidence. Rowan knew that followers could believe in a hero more than they believed in themselves. He knew that first hand. Thus, he recognized the look in Tue-Row’s eyes.*
*But, Tue-San wasn’t still focused on Tue-Row. Her attention snapped back to Rowan, her cold, dismissive mask falling back into place.*
Tue-San: "I believe this wraps up the list of suspects. I will-"
*Tue-Row raised his hand, making Tue-San stop.*
Tuerow: "Tue-San, I know what you’re thinking."
Tuerow: "It’s best if you let it out. You know I would rather have the two of you see eye to eye."
*Tue-San’s lips formed a thin line, her gaze still focused on Rowan. The hero felt his blood go cold.*
Rowan: "You can’t be suspecting me?!"
Tue-San: "Your arrival coincides with the assassination attempt. You also have a reputation for deception and trickery, albeit likely exaggerated."
Tue-San: "You speak at behest of demons. All of the goblin people know not to trust the demons. The history of their promises to the goblin nation is long and bloody. The betrayal of the 4th blood. The fall of Samatan. The Fellstar Pact."
Tue-San: "Proud goblins used as pawns, then discarded. Jezera and her brother appear cut from the same cloth."
Rowan: "You presume a great deal about them."
Tue-San: "I presume nothing. We are not without our own agents. Your attempts at teaching orcs discipline are commendable, but a pretty whore and a flask of ale untangles every tongue."
Tue-San: "I presume nothing. Your orcs talk, Blackwell. And we are not without our own agents. I am told they lack discipline and respect for their superiors, present company included."
Tue-San: "As for your Mistress, I handled her correspondence at His Excelency’s request. She reveals more in her letters than she suspects. She thinks herself the smartest person on the continent. She is anything but."
Tue-San: "As for your Empress, I handled her correspondence at His Excelency’s request. She reveals more in her letters than she suspects. She thinks herself the smartest person on the continent. She is anything but."
Tue-San: "We are not fools, Rowan Blackwell, and we will not be taken as such."
*The warning in her voice was unmistakable. Rowan felt a tense shift in the atmosphere as Tue-San glared at him, her clipped voice sending a chill down his spine.*
*And Tue-Row had yet to say a word. The goblin prince waited, silent, perhaps curious what Rowan’s response will be. *
Rowan: "Well, besides the obvious fact that I don’t know much about affairs here in the first place…"
*He has his own interests, separate from the demons.*
Rowan: "…You certainly tore me a new one there, Tue-San."
Tue-San: "These are facts, Rowan Blackwell."
Rowan: "No, no, I agree. The twins have… Issues. Dealing with them can be difficult, to put it mildly."
Rowan: "But, if you want to know why I wouldn’t have done it. Consider this. I need allies, just as much the twins do."
Rowan: "Smart allies who I can rely on. Someone who won’t say the wrong thing to the wrong person, and get themselves splattered over a wall."
Rowan: "If you are everything you claim to be, Tue-Row, then I need you more than I need your people. Soldiers are less useful to me than friends. And since I’ve arrived here, I’ve got nothing but signals of that sort of friendship."
*Rowan stretched his back.*
Tuerow: "Kind words. But, I must push back on that distinction you raised. I and all of goblinkind are a package deal, Rowan."
Rowan: "I wasn’t suggesting otherwise. just, it does mean that I have no interest to seek your deathor replacement. And plenty of reason to ignore or sabotage such an order."
*Why try to kill their only ally?*
Rowan: "Why would I seek to harm someone who has already pledged allegiance to us? Sure, it’s becoming clear that the promise was made under less-then-true conditions. But, all it would do is set negotiations even further."
Tuerow: "It’s a promise I plan to keep, Rowan. I assure you."
Rowan: "I have no doubt. And I know my masters well enough to know that if you follow through you will be rewarded. And if you fail you’ll be punished."
Rowan: "It’s really that simple Tue-San."
*Tue-San narrowed her eyes at him, but he thought nothing of it. He needed the two of them to be compliant, anything else was an added bonus.*
*Trust a human, not a demon.*
Rowan: "I must admit, being something of a rural bumpkin, I’m not sure I could debate your list in an educated way, Tue-San. I’m sure all of that truly happened."
Rowan: "But, those are reasons not to trust the twins. I am not them. I might serve them. I make my own judgments, I have my own honour."
Rowan: "Whatever happened between the goblins and demons in the past? That’s not my business. Don’t trust the demons. Trust me. Tue-Row said himself that’s how humans operate. I wouldn’t harm Tue-Row. And, I’ll make damn sure his loyalty is rewarded."
Rowan: "You both have my word."
*Tue-Row nodded, lips touched by a smile. But, Tue-San’s dark expression did not melt.*
Tue-San: "Hmph. We’ll see if it means anything."
*The Goblins can trust him or he can leave *
*Instead of directly addressing the point, Rowan suddenly rose from his seat. He towered over the diminutive Goblins.*
Tuerow: "Now now, let’s not get hasty here-"
Rowan: "Tue-Row, I do not have time to jump through hoops to prove my trustworthiness. Especially not when  you yourself confessed to backstabbing your allies minutes ago!"
Rowan: "I agreed to stick around and help smooth out an agreed on pact, maybe get some answers while I do so. I didn’t agree to get interrogated this way for matters that I frankly could give two shits about."
Rowan: "I have an entire continent to subdue, so believe me when I say - I don’t have time for this shit."
Tuerow: "So you’re saying you didn’t try to kill me because I am literally not important enough for you to even try."
Rowan: "No offence, but yes."
Tuerow: "Ouch. Sit down, I’ll take it."
*Rowan grunted. He despoisted himself back in the chair, although now the atmosphere was more tense.*
*Tue-San continued to glare, obviously not convinced. Tue-Row waited for a moment, then chuckled and turned to Tue-San.*
Tuerow: "If that’s not enough…"
Tuerow: "I know Rowan, Tue-San. Well, much as you can know someone who you only just met. He wouldn’t try to kill me so quickly, not without getting a better understanding of wether I’m someone he needs to kill."
Tuerow: " And, more importantly, he wouldn’t fail at it."
*He placed his hand over his wound, then hissed as it flared up again. *
Tuerow: "So cross him off the list of suspects. I want Rowan treated as nothing less than a member of my own inner circle. Am I understood?"
*She nodded stiffly and tightened her grip on her notebook.*
Tue-San: "… Of course. My Prince. Rowan shall be beyond reproach."
*Tue-Row smiled, and the tension in the room broke as he turned his attention back to Rowan with an excited gleam in his eye. *
Tuerow: "Now then, let’s put the unfortunate matter of today’s distraction aside, and talk about the real reason I asked you to stay…"
*Rowan wondered if they really should just gloss over Tue-San accusing him of attempted regicide, but in the end, he put it under yet another quirk of “goblin politics, and decided to let the subject lie.*
*The whole ordeal already took too much of his time. and there were other issues that needed to be discussed, possibly addressed as soon as possible. He would learn what they were, at least. Then… *
*Well, Tue-Row was right about one thing - Rowan didn’t like making his move without scouting the field first.*
Tuerow: "Like I said. That I am the Prince of Blackholt, and in time Gobnagoz is no question, but there remain pockets of defiance. And to ensure my rear is protected before I go to war with Rosaria, I must end this final stage of the war within Blackholt."
Tuerow: "And the means to do that is my upcoming nuptials. They must go smoothly. At least by goblin standards. The problems must be stamped out."
Rowan: "And what part do you see me playing in this?"
Tuerow: "I suspect that my lovely bride, Zii, might be planning a final offensive before the wedding. She's gotten particularly boisterous as of late and my spies are telling me she’s up to something."
Tuerow: "Any advantage she gains on the battlefield is an extra bit of leverage she gains on me come wedding day. I cannot allow that."
Tuerow: "We do not need to fight a pitched battle with her. But, between you and me, she tends to get a little… wild if she's left alone for too long. Best to remind her who's top dog to dissuade any notions from her head."
Tue-San: "Or assassination attempts."
*Tue-Row shrugged.*
Tuerow: "Or those."
*Rowan nodded softly.*
Rowan: "And you want the help of a famed general to ensure the battle goes smoothly."
Tuerow: "Well, as of an hour ago I am not at my battlefield best. But, more than that, I instructed Tue-Mai and my generals to learn from maps of your campaigns. Better to have the original."
Tue-San: "Zii is encamped to the North-East at the Central Pass. Travel there and we will have an army waiting for you to employ."
*While Rowan was still thinking about the situation, Tue-Row jumped in to discuss a second issue.*
Tuerow: "Then there’s the matter of Che-Lin. She still holds an independent enclave with whatever holdouts of the Old Clans have refused to bend the knee."
Tuerow: "Fate is a funny thing. She now leads the very people she helped me destroy."
Tuerow: "I could still crush her, perhaps. But it would be time-consuming and costly. And she is no threat to me anymore."
Tue-San: "…Unless she tried to assassinate you."
Tuerow: "…Unless she tried to assassinate me."
Tuerow: "Regardless, I plan to meet with Che-Lin one last time. If she can be persuaded to attend my wedding, it would signal to the other Old Clan holdouts that the time to accept the new order has come. Maybe even convince her to join us."
Rowan: "And for that, you want my help with negotiations."
*Rowan squinted. Compared to the matter of his rebellious fiancée, this seemed a matter that he was less well suited for. But, Tue-Row had given him the impression of a man who wouldn’t ask for Rowan’s help for no reason.*
*But, why?*
Tuerow: "Exactly. Che-Lin holds court at the Gol Tower, directly to the South-East. It won't be very hard to find her."
*Before Rowan could speak, Tue-San jumped in.*
Tue-San: "My prince, while you and Master Blackwell focus on such tasks, my eyes shall remain on Hoz’Holt."
Tue-San: "My prince, while you and Sir Blackwell focus on such tasks, my eyes shall remain on Hoz’Holt."
Tue-San: "There are duties in the city that require my attention, especially with an assassin in our midst. I must find them and ensure they are suitably punished."
Tuerow: "If you think it best. I’d rather we weren’t still spending so much of our time rooting out traitors, but I guess get a choice in that regard. Although…"
*As he spoke, a gleam of inspiration flashed in his eyes.*
Tue-San: "My Prince?"
Tuerow: "Once Rowan has helped me with those two other tasks, should he wish to partner with you in your investigation, I ask that you allow him to accompany you. And as a full investigator, not shuffled off to the side. It should speed things up."
Tue-San: "..."
*Tue-San faced Rowan, her lip curled with a particular mix of emotions. In the end, she voiced no opposition to the idea. *
Tue-San: "You are ever wise, My Prince."
*Rowan listened to the entire exchange silently. In his mind he was still processing all that he had seen and heard since he had come to Hoz’Holt.*
Rowan: "So…let me sum this up. Try to get a handle on what I am hearing…"
Rowan: "You want me to lead a goblin army in battle against your own fiancée, who is, for reasons I can only assume are complex, still in a bloody war with you despite fully intending to actually marry you."
Tuerow: "Correct."
Rowan: "And you want me to help you reignite your friendship with a prior ally who you literally, emphasis on the word literally, backstabbed."
Tuerow: "Still correct."
*Rowan glanced at Tue-San.*
Rowan: "And because you were stabbed immediately after my arrival, you want me to search your city for assassins alongside your assistant who, apologies if this is harsh, but appears to despise me?"
Tue-San: "“Mistrust would be more accurate."
*Tue-Row’s grin only seemed to grow wider.*
Tuerow: "Well, you don’t have to do all of it. Frankly, my new friend, help me on just one and that alone would do wonders for me."
*Rowan buried his head in his hands.*
Rowan: "And here I thought this would be easy."
Tuerow: "Oh, Rowan. You’ll learn soon enough. Nothing is ever easy with goblins."
Tuerow: "But think of it that way. Once all of this will be resolved, all of goblinkind will owe you a debt of gratitude."
Tuerow: "You and me Rowan, against the world. As it was meant to be."
*Rowan sighed.*
Rowan: "I’ll see what I can do."
*If Tue-Row made anything of Rowan’s resistance, he didn’t show it. He was still just smiling.*
*Debris of the forest crunched under Rowan's boots as he approached Tue-Row's battle encampment. But, he was not alone. A team of orcs followed behind, dragging heavy wheelbarrows down the makeshift path. Goblins whispered in their wake, eyes drawn narrow with suspicion.*
*Ever the logician, Rowan made careful note of the gear Tue-Row’s men were armed with. Poor by the standards of humans, especially when it came to the armor. But, the weapons seemed in decent condition at least.*
*It was surely beyond the works of goblin forges. Human-made arms, but not the good stuff.*
*Some hesitant whispers followed Rowan around the encampment. Humans were a rare sight this deep into the Blackholt. But, as usual, it dissipated with the recognition of his clothing.*
*Reaching the center of the encampment, Rowan turned back to the orcs and gestured toward a clearing near the centre.*
Rowan: "Set them down here."
*The orcs obeyed, dropping the and set to work ripping the lids open; swords, spears, arrowheads, and breastplates fell out. More than enough to fill the hands of every fighter in the entire encampment.*
*Whatever soldiers were around camp drew in, eyes shining with awe. More soon emerged from the makeshift barracks built into the trunks of some of the nearby black trees.*
*One of Tue-Row’s men dared to step forward, glancing at Rowan while keeping one hand gripped on the edge of the crate. He gripped it as if its contents were imaginary. As if they would disappear the moment he let go.*
Goblin: "Woah woah. These are for us!?"
Rowan: "Gifts from your new friends at Castle Bloodmeen. Made from our finest ironworks by our expert forgemaster."
Rowan: "Gifts from your new friends at Castle Bloodmeen. Taken from the stores of the human keep at Raeve."
*The goblins hesitated at first, unsure if this was a trap, but once a few grabbed their new weapons without consequence, others quickly joined the fray, admiring each new swing of their sword or twing of their bowstring.*
*Rowan nodded approvingly at the way they handled their weapons. This didn’t seem like a force of novices.*
*They weren't perfect weapons by any means– He’d barely managed to get Andras to approve any weapons transfer at all– but compared to what they were used to fighting with, these were a marked improvement.*
*Rowan turned to see Tue-Row strolling towards him. Mai was at his side, stuffing her face with some sort of pasty. A small crowd of soldiers followed alongside him. They were worse described as guards than admirers getting a chance to be near their idol. *
*The goblin prince seemed practiced at patting backs and giving smiles towards his adoring followers as he moved. It reminded Rowan of the way he’d learned to deal with crowds during his return to Rastedel immediately after the war.*
Tuerow: "Aha! I see you've already spoiled the surprise."
Rowan: "Should I have waited for you to arrive?"
Tuerow: "No, no! By all means, let them have their fun. They’re gifts from your bosses. It would be real rude of me to take the credit."
*Tue-Row picked one of the swords from the crate, testing its swing with approval before carefully placing it back into the crate. It had been with his undamaged arm, of course. The other hung at his side, bandages likely hidden beneath his facsimile of Rowan’s clothes.*
*Best not to advertise his wounded state.*
Tuerow: "Mai, help the men get ready for battle. I'll join you right after I check in with Rowan. Would be rude not to."
Tue-Mai: "Euw goddit -"
*Tue-Mai coughed and swallowed the chunk of pastry in her mouth.*
Tue-Mai: "You got it, boss."
*She nodded, disappearing into the throng of soldiers.*
Rowan: "I’d planned to send the orcs back after the delivery, but I could always ask them to stay."
Tuerow: "If you’d like, though it’s not strictly nessacery. I wouldn’t call this a battle. If all goes according to plan, it will be more like a skirmish. A reminder, if you will, that she's got to keep her men on a tight leash until the wedding."
*Tue-Row gestured for Rowan to follow. Rowan glanced curiously around at the way the camp had been incorporated into the forest itself. The goblins were so used to battles in the woods, using trees themselves to house soldiers seemed almost rote. Rowan wondered how long it took to set up. *
Rowan: "Give me the rundown of the battlefield. Anything I should know before the fighting starts."
Tuerow: "I’m sure you’ve already got a brief look at Blackholt, it’s more of that."
Rowan: "So the usual joys of fighting in a dense forest. Great. Still, let's make sure we’re on the same page here."
*Tue-Row gave him a small nod, and the two sat down to discuss the details of their upcoming skirmish.*
*This was the first opportunity he had to talk with the new prince about anything else than “goblin politics, a term he was growing to despise. And Tue-Row… *
*It was like staring back at his reflection in a lake. The resemblance was uncanny - the attention to logistics, strategic flexibility, and heavy focus on tactical independence of individual units.*
*One maneuver, which Tue-Row called “Drider’s retreat - it was his. It was the same strategy he used near Riverlem Grove, only adapted to Blackholt realities.*

Tuerow: "Expect? The only thing you can expect with Zii is the unexpected. She is a woman of chaos if I've ever met one. She’d make a demon scold her to behave less erratically."

Tuerow: "She’s not even from a clan. Notice the single word name?"

Tuerow: "Or Zii-Zii, if you wish to indulge her. “Zii of clan Zii!, of which she is the head and sole member. Zii doesn’t exactly care for conventions, as you will soon notice."

Tuerow: "But there were no hard feelings in this, you know? When the dust settled, I asked them to join me. Gave them the whole pitch about how Gobnagoz could be their home too. And thanks to Tue-San, many of them now are working to build a better goblin tomorrow."
Tuerow: "But some would have none of it, and they had to go somewhere. This is where they ended up."
*He shook his head, chuckling under his breath. He made it seem like the notion was almost funny. Rowan simply frowned.*
Tuerow: "Zii is an upstart. And she built a coalition of the wildest goblins you’ll ever meet. From angry clannists, to savages from the deep woods, to downright brigands."
Rowan: "Sounds nearly impossible to organize."
Tuerow: "You’d be surprised. I’ll give the woman this, she stays on message. You have me in one corner talking about kingdoms and history and whatnot. But, she keeps it simple. Violence and conquest. Almost primal stuff."
Tuerow: "Maybe it’s just in her blood."
*Rowan raised an eyebrow.*
Rowan: "In her blood? I thought you didn’t know her clan?"
*Tue-Row gave him a mischievous look, glancing at the other goblins nearby before leaning in conspiratorially.*
Tuerow: "Zii isn't just wild in her tactics– she's quite literally a creature of chaos."
Rowan: "What is that supposed to mean?"
*Tue-Row shrugged helplessly, a grin pulling at his lips.*
Tuerow: "You’ve met some of our caravan traveling brethren. I know that for a fact. Ever wonder why some of them look so different from each other? Goblins can have kids with non-goblins. And they may be goblins, but they’ll take after the other parent."

*Rowan pursed his lips and thought of a particular goblin.*

*Tue-Row scratched his face, and offered a small shrug that could mean anything. Rowan took this for a cue to abandon the current line of questions…and never to return to it. He wasn’t sure if he wanted to know.  *
Rowan: "So between that, and her fighting you and possibly trying to kill you… Are you really comfortable with getting married to her? She doesn’t sound like good wife material."

Tuerow: "Well, I certainly didn't propose to her out of some sort of longing from afar, if that's what you're thinking. A leader to his people doesn't have such a benefit."
Tuerow: "I won’t point fingers, but thanks to someone being their usual, efficient self, things have started to move far more quickly than I anticipated. I had to adjust accordingly."
