Tuerow: "We need an army to take over Rosaria, no? Zii brings in the other half. Unless you want us to wait twenty years to raise a new generation of goblins."
*Tue-Row rubbed his chin, a hint of exhaustion in his eyes betraying his otherwise composed demeanor. *
Tuerow: "Having Zii for a wife… It won't be an easy transition. Knowing her personality, I'm certain she'll try to find a way to use this union to her advantage– and I have an inkling of how she plans to do it."
Rowan: "It all sounds like a bit of a gamble then. She doesn't sound like the kind of person that will stop raising havoc just because of a wedding ceremony."
Tuerow: "Oh, I'm counting on it! She’ll be tough as black oak. But a strong king needs a strong queen by his side. Tue-San would never forgive me if I wasted my bachelor status on some wilting forest flower."
Tuerow: "Besides, what's the fun in a marriage without a little conflict?"
*There was something strange about the pointed smirk Tue-Row had, but before Rowan could ask about it, a sudden WHOOOSH!! stopped the men dead in their tracks. Rowan stared at the arrow sunk deep into the tree beside him, just inches from his head.*
*Rowan deflected the next arrow with his sword on reflex. Meanwhile, a counter volley from Tue-Row’s side struck back at the enemy sniper. A small cry echoed at the edge of the forest before a goblin tumbled out from a tree.*
Tuerow: "Guess “my beloved caught wind of our arrival at camp."
*Tue-Row's soldiers rushed to grab up their weapons and supplies. The rustling of trees and screams of distant foes told them of the danger.*
*Rowan frowned. Zii's troops had the advantage of the dense forest for cover, while their base was clearly visible, providing an easy target. They’d need to advance fast and meet the enemy in the woods.*
*Rowan was so lost in tactical consideration, his ally had to shake him back to focus. Tue-Row had an uncharacteristically uncertain expression on his face.*
Tuerow: "Rowan. I'm going to help Tue-Mai with the troops on our left flank. You command the right!"
*Rowan couldn’t help but chuckle as they sprinted in opposite directions.*
Rowan: "I showed up barely an hour ago and we’re already in the middle of an ambush?!"
Tuerow: "Goblin politics, keep up!"
*Soon, Rowan found himself entangled in battle. He drew his sword and shouted orders to his newly assigned subordinates. It was a role Rowan stepped with familiar grace.*
*It helped that Rowan’s subordinates proved shockingly competent. They followed Rowan's commands without question, throwing themselves with spirit against the attackers. Perhaps Rowan was no goblin, but his towering figure and familiar outfit gave him natural authority.*
*Still, the battle proved far from easy. The density of the forest was unlike anything Rowan had fought in before. So too did the very nature of goblin warfighting. They flew in and out of his view. Despite the difference in kit, it was often hard to discern if any particular unit were his men or Zii’s. *
*Yet, Rowan could not stay out of the fray, merely issuing orders. He was as clearly a focal point for his men as Zii’s. It was not long before the fighting on the right flank turned into a series of savage rushes towards him. A foolish strategy, likely to cost lives.*
*If one broke through the spears of his subordinates, they fell easily under the swipe of his sword. It came with a familiar rush of energy. The thrill of battle. His body moved on raw instinct, tearing through attackers without a second thought.*
*Momentarily, he’d stop and look at fallen foes. Zii’s men were half-dressed in rags, armed with rusted weapons and even sharpened stone. Fanatical, near-suicidal fighters…but limited by supplies.*
*More of them fell wounded than dead. A common feature of goblin combat. Why go for a kill strike when a captive was more valuable?*
Goblin: "Commander Rowan!"
*Rowan deflected an arrow off his sword before glancing toward the subordinate.*
Goblin: "Word from the spotter in the high branches. The Wyrd Women are here. They’re coming right for us!"
*Rowan looked to the point of contact. It looked like the enemy was falling back. Probably not to retreat though. There was a charge coming…*
Rowan: "Specifics, soldier. What’s a Wyrd Woman?"
Goblin: "You don’t know-"
Goblin: "Apologies. They are…her honour guard. Female fighters who take no mercy. It is rumored they drink the blood of fallen foes…"
*The goblin glanced nervously between the trees, as though they would descend on him at any moment. Rowan glanced around as well, though more from prudence than from fear. He hadn’t noticed how close he had become to the front line. *
Rowan: "Damn it."
*Had those suicidal rushes towards him been an effort to soften the segment of the line in front of him? He needed to get back before–*
???: "YAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHH!!!"
*A battle cry echoed through the forest, practically shaking the terrain itself. Rowan gripped the hilt of his sword, shifting into a defensive position. He scanned the forest, the sounds of battle nearby keeping him alert.*
Rowan: "What was–"
*His words cut off by the sudden charge of hundreds of darkened forms through the forest. Only, now the ones at the head of the formation had the curved shapes of young women. The rank of his soldiers in front steeled themselves, though he could see the fear on their faces.*
*The two forces crashed in dramatic faction, screams and the pounding of weapons on shields were everywhere.*
*In the chaos, he nearly missed something important. There was something in the trees that had made it behind his lines. A young woman – or perhaps something closer to a beast. She bent low, a furry tail swishing behind her as she stalked her prey.*
*It took Rowan a moment to register that he was that prey.*
Rowan: "Get back!!"
*He shoved his subordinate back, swinging his sword up to the charging monster. She moved with unnatural speed and grace, undeterred by the uneven ground as she beelined for the hero.*
*Rowan blinked. There were a pair of large axes in her hands and she swung them both wildly. Rowan’s sword barely moved up in time. The metal clashed violently. The force of the blow was so strong that it traveled up his arms. It may as well have been a hammer.*
*It brought her close enough to look into her eyes. Her wild, near bestial eyes. Then, she let out a sudden, high giggle. Rowan squinted.*
*So this was the queen-to-be.*
Zii-Zii: "A-hee-hee-hee~~!! You're stronger than you look!! Oh, this will be so much fun!"
Rowan: "I don't–"
*But, his words were cut off by Zii swinging an axe, this time directed at his head. Rowan ducked, sliding his foot forward to trip her. Yet, it failed. She bounced backward with all the agility of a cat.*
Zii-Zii: "Cheating is no fun, you know!! But I love a man willing to play dirty!"
*Rowan was caught off guard as Zii dove forward, slamming her forehead against his stomach. The hero stumbled back, clutching his stomach. He looked up to see an axe flying in his direction.*
*He barely caught the blow with his sword, but the strength of his steel against the crudely made hilt of her weapon was enough to slice it in half. Zii gasped. She barely had time to jump away before Rowan's sword could open her stomach.*
*Rowan expected some sort of anger at the destruction of her weapon, but the bestial goblin’s eyes glittered with pure excitement. She tossed the remains of the axe over her shoulder, discarding it without a second thought.*
*She’d started to giggle again, swaying from side to side. The fact that she was a goblin was clear up close. But, that swishing tail behind her could fool someone. Rowan’s eyes trailed its back-and-forth swishing.*
*Which is exactly when she sprung.*
*Rowan didn't understand what happened; one moment he was shielding himself from her onslaught, and the next, she had him pinned to the ground. Zii straddled the hero and held his arms down with unnatural strength, her small body shaking with eager giggles.*
Zii-Zii: "Zii-Zii winsssss~~!!"
*Rowan gasped as her hips dug forward, grinding into him. He tried to push upward but couldn't budge. He grit his teeth. He’d fought orcs with less arm strength than her. What was she?*
*He didn't know what to make of her strength nor the fact she was staring down at him like a piece of meat she couldn't wait to devour. When she smiled, it revealed a mouth of dangerously sharp teeth.*
Zii-Zii: "I was sooo looking forward to meeting you, Great Trickster!! This has gone even better than I planned!"
Rowan: "Funny. I don’t recall my presence being announced ahead of time."
Zii-Zii: "Ohoho~? You really didn’t think I would know? I have eyes everywhere, silly! Zii-Zii knows everything."
Rowan: "…Goblin politics…"
*She bounced atop of him with another girlish giggle, her crotch pressing down ever so softly on his abdomen. He also was quite aware of how her breasts hovered over him, practically overshadowing her face.*
*From her level of restraint, it didn’t seem like his demise was imminent. Still, this was a precarious position, to say the least..*
*Try to shove her off.*
*Rowan shifted, just enough to claw some of the soil from the ground into his palm. The goblin warlord seemed sufficiently distracted with her fresh capture.*
*Distracted enough, it seemed, not to notice when Rowan's hand slipped from her grasp.*
*A second later, the entire handful of dirt had been shoved into her open mouth. Fast enough that she hadn’t been given a chase to bite down on him with those monstrous teeth.*
Zii-Zii: "MMPH?!"
*Rowan shoved her diminutive body off, with enough force to send her tumbling. Soon, he was back on his feet, sword in a defensive stance, he wasn't willing to take any more chances.*
Zii-Zii: "BLECK! BLEEEECK!"
*Zii-Zii spit the soil back onto the ground, scraping her tongue clean with her hands.*
*But, before the fight could rejoin, Rowan heard the sound of someone approaching the little duel. Multiple footsteps.*
Tuerow: "Ah, I see you've met my bride-to-be, Rowan. And here I was worried that I’d have to introduce you."
*He turned to see Tue-Row and Tue-Mai standing together only a short distance behind them. Around them was a host of his soldiers, bows drawn.*
*Dazed, Rowan turned to the other side. Some of Zii’s troops were lining up behind her. Chief among them, the lightly dressed but heavily armed female fighters that had been called the Wyrd Women.*
*Zii’s tail wagged.*
*Try to think of another way.*
*Rowan shifted, but the movement was useless against Zii's bullish strength. He needed to think of another way out of this, one that preferably wouldn't end in her death– or his own. That was a political can of worms Rowan wasn't ready to open.*
Zii-Zii: "Not struggling, hm?"
Rowan: "Trying to think how not to kill you by accident."
Zii-Zii: "Ooooh, you don’t have to worry about that. Zii-Zii’s sturdier than she looks!"
Zii-Zii: "And she likes it rough."
*He swallowed heavily. Before he could decide on his next move, the fight was interrupted.*
Tuerow: "Ah, I see you've met my bride-to-be, Rowan. And here I was worried that I’d have to introduce you."
*He turned to see Tue-Row and Tue-Mai standing together only a short distance behind them. Around them was a host of his soldiers, bows drawn.*
*Dazed, Rowan turned to the other side. Some of Zii’s troops were lining up behind her. Chief among them, the lightly armed female fighters that had been called the Wyrd Women.*
*Tue-Row didn't bother to hide the amused smirk on his face as he took in Zii's compromising position over the hero.*
Tuerow: "Zii, would you kindly release my guest? Unless you’re enjoying the view too much to move, Rowan."
Rowan: "That would be preferable, thanks."
*The bestial woman let out a low giggle, matching her glare with her fiance’s. Her whole body wiggled, even more excited to see Tue-Row than Rowan. Her tail even wagged, as though she were an excited puppy.*
*After a deliberate delay, she playfully shook her head and released Rowan, as if she were disappointed to let a toy go. Rowan scrambled back to Tue-Row's side, happy to be free of whatever potential danger being her captive implied.*
*Rowan forced a smile, ignoring the pain in his arms from where Zii had squeezed them. Damn, she was strong. Was that part of whatever strange process had made her so different?*
Zii-Zii: "Now, there you are! You missed all the fun, Tue-Row~!! Zii-Zii was worried you’d be boring and never even show!"
*The goblins flanking Zii had serious expressions. They held their weapons– a crude mixture of spears, maces, and swords– with intensity as they stared down their opposing numbers on either side.*

Tuerow: "Now now, Zii. If you were really that worried about it, you wouldn’t have sent a distraction force towards my wing while you and your elites went to hassle Rowan. A waste of your own resources, don’t you think?"
Zii-Zii: "A waste!? Ehehehe. How could it be? Something delicious has walked in and made a mess of the whole game, and you expect me not to have a taste?~"
Zii-Zii: "Really… Darling. You should have seen through Zii-Zii’s plan sooner. Mmm. Unless, you’re not as interesting as I thought~."
*Rowan felt her eyes trail over him again with animalistic exhilaration. An awkward laugh burst out of him; he wasn't sure whether to feel more annoyed or amused with her.*
*Tue-Row rubbed his chin with a sigh.*
Tuerow: "Zii, let’s put this nonsense to bed. The wedding day is coming soon, and you know I’m not going to just let you win in the field. It’s time to parlay and actually–"
Zii-Zii: "A parlay? Tch! Where's the fun in that?!"
Tuerow: "I don't believe war is supposed to be fun–"
Zii-Zii: "Then why do they make it so damn exciting?"
*As if to emphasize the point, Zii picked up her remaining axe and ran her long canine tongue along its blade. Rowan tensed, half expecting her to break the negotiation and attack.*
*Tue-Row crossed his arms, more disappointed than scared. Yet, Zii just continued to wag.*
Tuerow: "You never change, woman."
Tuerow: "How about this then. You stay in the field. Continue waving around your army and pretending you can stand up to me. All fine."
Tuerow: "But, we have important things to arrange, Zii. A wedding."
Tuerow: "At the very least, you need to stop forcing yourself on my emissaries. I’m a tolerant man, Zii, but this is too much."
*Zii smirked at Rowan. Considering her behavior when she’d knocked him to the ground before, the revelation was barely even surprising.*
Zii-Zii: "Well maybe you should get an emissary that's harder for Zii-Zii to rape then~~ I– Hm."

Tuerow: "Now, suppose for a moment that someone wished to see my forces routed and my position as prince taken from me. It would be natural for such a person to be a suspect in any…let’s say, assasination attempts."

Tuerow: "Zii. Tell me the truth. Did you try to have me killed?"

*She just laughed, as if he told a funny joke.*
Zii-Zii: "A-hee-hee-hee-heeee~~!!"
*Zii-Zii gripped her stomach and doubled over in laughter.*
Zii-Zii: "Me? You suspect your sweet Zii-Zii of…of sullying herself with assassins!? Oooh, that’s a good one."

Zii-Zii: "Darling, if your mighty Zii-Zii wanted to make a splatter of a worthy foe’s guts, I wouldn’t have some other squirrel-for-brains do it! I would murder them by my own blades!"

Zii-Zii: "…Blade!"

Tuerow: "A fair point, I suppose."
Zii-Zii: "Mmm. I knew you’d see it that way, Darling…"
Zii-Zii: "Though, since you’ve finally come. No more wasting Zii-Zii’s time! You know you can’t hide the real reason you’re here from me. I’ve been waiting this entire time!"
Zii-Zii: "Ehehehe. And poor Zii-Zii just can’t can’t stand a man who’d leave her waiting~!"

*Rowan blinked and turned to Tue-Row.*
Rowan: "So fighting Zii was just a pretext for something else? Seriously?"
*Tue-Row winked at him before turning back to Zii.*
Tuerow: "Since you've so kindly agreed to meet with me, with no coercion necessary at all, would you turn around so this worthy opponent could bestow a gift upon you?"

*Tue-Mai walked over to Tue-Row and placed a velvet box in his hand. Rowan leaned forward, eyebrow raised. Was this some sort of Goblin custom?*
Tuerow: "Zii, my future Queen. May I have the honour of presenting you with your Wife Gift?"
*Zii spun around with sparkling eyes. Tue-Row revealed the content of the, a shimmering gold necklace inside. It was quite the spectacle, with jewels circling the rim and a band so large that it would cover her neck. Almost a large choker, rather than a necklace.*
*From the relative scant wealth he’d seen displayed in his time here in Blackholt so far, such a treasure must have been rare indeed.*
*She didn’t show the slightest hesitation in yanking her hair out of the way and displaying her bare neck to a man who she was quite literally at war with. Tue-Row strode forward and clasped the necklace around her neck. *
*Rowan leaned toward Tue-Mai, his voice dropped to a whisper.*
Rowan: "A Wife Gift?"

Tue-Mai: "Ya don’t know what that is? Ach. Don’t ya give one to your wife before you marry her? And don’t she give you one too when you marry?"

Tue-Mai: "Huh. Well, that’s just bad luck then. If you don't give them to each other how will the tie be solidified?"

Tuerow: "It looks quite lovely on you. You’re going to be the star at the center of our wedding."
Zii-Zii: "Mhmmm~~!! It's shiny!!"

Zii-Zii: "Ah, but Darling. You came all this way and killed so many of my friends. But, your Husband Gift isn't even ready yet!! You gotta wait!"

*Zii ignored his light jab, and instead leaped forward, bringing her face close to his. She leaned in to kiss him - but Tue-Row's hand shot up, cupping her cheek just moments before she could steal one.*
Zii-Zii: "Awww… One day I will catch you with your guard down."
Tuerow: "You won’t. But I expect you to keep trying."
*He allowed her to give him a quick kiss, but when she started back toward her Wyld Women, intent on showing them her new jewelry, he caught her arm to stop her. *
Tuerow: "Ah-ah, not so fast. I would also like this gift to be a reminder that this is my commitment to you and to our future. And maybe the next time you think of breaking our truce before the wedding, you’ll think twice about how much it actually benefits either of us."
Zii-Zii: "Ehehehe. Is that my sweet darling telling me that I have to behave myself?"
Tuerow: "…I’m telling you to avoid your worst impulses."
Zii-Zii: "But they’re the most fun ones!"

*Her cheeks were burning, and her lips quivered with an awkward smile. Heartsong’s tail flicked back and forth behind her in nervous twitches.*
Heartsong: "H-here I am."
Rowan: "Please, for both our sakes: drop the act."
Rowan: "Just be yourself."
Heartsong: "I will. I promise."
*Take control of the dream… and of her.*
*The memory was over, Rowan had followed it to its logical conclusion. And yet… the dream still continued. It seemed his mnemonic stowaway had something else in store for him.*
*The moments dragged by. He cast a short glance in the Elder’s direction. She clearly didn’t intend to show herself. If this really was a dream, then perhaps...*
Rowan: "Say, Elder?"
Elder: "Yes, my boy?"
Rowan: "Would you care to join me for dinner? Alexia is out for the day, and I’m in for a lonely meal otherwise."
Elder: "Oh, I wouldn’t want to impose. There is still so much to do around the village for the harvest festival, and I needed to check in on Tobias’ latest-"
*Rowan closed his eyes and concentrated, picturing the interior of his home in Arthdale, recalling as much of it as he could, down to the smallest detail.*
Rowan: "Please…"
Rowan: "I insist."
*Reality itself reshaped to the whims of Rowan’s imagination. The Elder let out a gasp as the world around them shifted and warped.*
*The small table where Rowan and Alexia had once dined together appeared between them, welcoming in its rustic simplicity.*
*Two places were set on the table, laid out with plain wood platters and wooden utensils. A small assortment of fruits and nuts and cheeses filled the plates.*
*It was astounding the level of detail Rowan could see. This wasn’t just what he could specifically remember, it was the entire memory.*
*Rowan smiled and gestured towards the chair opposite to his own in a polite invitation. The Elder’s lower lip quivered.*
Elder: "Rowan, I-"
Rowan: "Take a seat. Your old bones must be weary."
*The Elder’s eyes flicked down towards the table and then back to Rowan. A nervous smile spread across his face.*
Elder: "I-I suppose I could sit. Just for a little while."
*Rowan watched the Elder ease slowly into his chair, letting out a soft sigh as he bent his crooked back into the unyielding wood. It brought a wistful smile to Rowan’s face.*
Rowan: "You’re quite good at that."
Elder: "At what?"
Rowan: "Moving like he would. It’s uncanny: you really do look like he did in his later years."
Rowan: "He’d often struggle to sit down - something in his lower back, I think. I used to try to help him, but he’d just wave me off."
Rowan: "He was a very stubborn fellow."
*The Elder’s cheeks reddened with a most uncharacteristic blush.*
Elder: "You… really loved him."
*I really did.*
Rowan: "He was a good man. I miss him terribly."
Rowan: "Our final encounter was… unpleasant."
*Maybe. I don’t know.*
Elder: "He loved you. It’s obvious the way he spoke of you."
Rowan: "More’s the pity for him, then. Look what it earned him."
*At one point, I must have...*
Elder: "You don’t give yourself enough credit, Rowan."
Rowan: "-Or maybe you give me altogether too much. He certainly did."
Elder: "It’s wrong, what Andras did. What he made you do."
*I made a hard choice, I have no regrets.*
Elder: "Truly? None at all?"
*What’s done is done.*
Rowan: "The past is the past. I can no more change it than I can overturn a mountain."
Rowan: "The only thing left to do is to live with the choices I’ve made."
Elder: "But… have you never wondered? At what might have been?"
*Had I known, I would have chosen differently.*
Rowan: "My mistake was in thinking I could salvage something from the ashes."
Elder: "But... don’t you worry that that’s exactly what is happening to you, now?"
*The Elder blushed again and looked down at his lap, his fatherly disposition giving way to a far more timid body language.*
Elder: "F-forgive me Rowan, I don’t mean to pass judgment on you."
Elder: "I wish I had a fraction of the courage that you showed in that moment. Were I in your position, I would have never been able to decide."
Rowan: "I recall a similar line of discussion, when you were pretending to be Jezera in the dungeon."
Rowan: "What is it about my choices that fascinates you so?"
Elder: "The fact that you can make them at all."
Rowan: "Everyone makes decisions in life."
Elder: "But few can make them as decisively as you do. Not on such a grand scale."
Rowan: "And that is why the Fae want my help?"
Elder: "It’s why I want your help."
*Rowan’s eyes softened.*
Rowan: "…You don’t have to be so afraid of me. Will you at least talk to me, face to face?"
*Rowan’s eyes narrowed in annoyance.*
Rowan: "Enough. I’ve been more than patient with you. Show yourself."
*Rowan gave her a meaningful look.*
Rowan: "If it’s all the same to you, I’d prefer to talk to the real you, right now."
*The Elder blinked, glancing down at his lap. He let out a soft sigh and nodded.*
*The Elder’s body blurred and warped, reshaping itself to the familiar white-haired creature from before. Gone was the mischievous gleam in her eye, now she all but trembled in her seat when his gaze settled upon her. *
Heartsong: "H-here…"
Heartsong: "Here I am."
Rowan: "Here you are."
Rowan: "What should I call you? Or would you prefer simply “the white fox?"
*She giggled, casting a shy look at him from beneath her bangs with her strikingly yellow eyes.*
Heartsong: "My name is Heartsong."
*A pleasure to meet the real you at last.*
*She perked up a bit at that, sitting just a little bit straighter and meeting his gaze.*
Heartsong: "A-and you as well, Rowan!"
Rowan: "You’ve led me on a merry chase across my subconscious, I must say."
*Heartsong’s blush crept further up her cheeks. She glanced down at her lap again, unable to maintain eye contact with him for long.*
Heartsong: "Actually, i-in retrospect... I think I wanted you to catch me."
Rowan: "Well, it seems that you've been caught. But to what end?"
*Well, Heartsong? Have you anything to say for yourself?*
Heartsong: "I-I…"
*She closed her eyes and put a hand to her face, dragging her clawed nails down her brow.*
Heartsong: "Sol save us all, I must have practiced this conversation with myself a hundred times."
Rowan: "Take a breath — if that even matters in a dream?"
Rowan: "We’re not going anywhere, and frankly I’d like an explanation. This time it was like you wanted me to catch you."
*I will only say this once: no more memories, do you understand me?*
Rowan: "Whatever you were hoping to learn from me, you’ve found it. I’ve indulged your curiosity long enough."
Rowan: "My memories are my own, and not yours to tamper with. If you want to say something to me, you can damn well say it to my face."
*Heartsong shrank down into herself, her ears flattening back against her head.*
Heartsong: "O-okay…"
Rowan: "Promise me."
Heartsong: "I-I won’t! I promise!"
Heartsong: "I just… I want to help you."
Rowan: "Last we spoke, it seemed like you were trying to enlist my help."
Heartsong: "I-I am! I mean- we are… but I want to help you, too."
Rowan: "You’re not making much sense."
Heartsong: "I’m s-sorry! This isn’t how I thought things would go between us."
*Rowan leaned back in his chair, affecting a relaxed posture. Despite the brave front she was trying to put up, the Fae was fearfully shy.*
Rowan: "Take your time. I’m a captive audience, after all."
*She took in a deep breath, and exhaled heavily.*
Heartsong: "M-my people stand at a crossroads, Rowan."
Heartsong: "For centuries we’ve lived in peace, watching the waking world from afar. But over time, we have become divided. Hateful to each other."
Heartsong: "Now we are pulled in two directions. My father, Whitescar, and auntie- er, Lady Arzyl… they’re at each other’s throats. And I don’t know how to stop it."
Heartsong: "This business with the Twins is just the latest - and most dangerous - conflict. Only Queen Kassandra still keeps the peace between them, and even then, only just."
Rowan: "What does this have to do with the Fae and threatening the Twins over the use of the leylines?"
*Heartsong’s ears pulled back against her head.*
Heartsong: "…Why do you think there are two ambassadors currently representing one people? They have different visions of what that might mean."
Heartsong: "I don’t want this war to happen, I don’t want people to die."
Heartsong: "But... I’m a nobody, a recluse. I barely interact with my fellow Fae. I can’t stop what I know is coming, not alone."
Heartsong: "I don't want to get involved, but I’m scared of what will happen if I just stand by and watch, like-"
Heartsong: "…Like I do with everything else."
Rowan: "So why me?"
Rowan: "Why go to all this trouble, sift through my memories, drag me through these dreams, just to bring me here?"
Heartsong: "Because you are someone who I believe would understand. Ever since I first discovered your dream grove, I have felt that."
Rowan: "And just how long have you been watching me?"
*Heartsong’s face flushed cherry red. She glanced down at the table, lips quivering.*
Heartsong: "L-longer than I care to admit. Enough to have witnessed most of your memories."
Rowan: "How many?"
Heartsong: "Almost all of them."
Rowan: "…So you know everything about me."
*Heartsong nodded.*
Heartsong: "-As much as anyone can ever know the mind and soul of another."
*That’s… oddly flattering.*
Rowan: "…I never expected my life’s story to be captivating material for the idle whimsies of a Fae."
*Heartsong allowed a playful smile to slide onto her face. Rowan saw the brief flash of a toothy canine.*
Heartsong: "You aren’t an idle whimsy to me, Rowan."
*Rowan watched as her hands settled nervously atop the table. Sharp claws drew gentle circles on the wood as she looked at him.*
Heartsong: "You are… something else, entirely."
*That’s disturbing.*
Rowan: "No one should ever be privy to someone else’s personal experiences like that."
Heartsong: "Y-you have nothing to be ashamed of, I swear! I-I’m in awe of all you’ve accomplished. It’s why I want your help."
Heartsong: "I wouldn’t have watched for so long if you hadn’t captivated me so. You are so… so very unique, even for a mortal."
Rowan: "So what exactly are you proposing here? An alliance? A secret deal?"
Heartsong: "A promise. My help, and your trust in dealing with the Fae together."
Rowan: "No strings attached?"
Heartsong: "No strings. I know how much you hate them."
Heartsong: "Think of it as me helping you ease one more burden off your shoulders. After all, with all that’s going on in Rosaria, you need the Fae right now like-"
Rowan: "…Like I need a hole in the head."
Heartsong: "Yes! Just so."
Rowan: "..."
Rowan: "It’s like I’m talking to a stranger who knows my every word."
Heartsong: "Then I hope you’ll take it as a sign of my sincerity when I swear that no one knows about us, Fae or otherwise."
Heartsong: "What I tell you, and what you tell me are for our ears alone. I will never betray that trust."
*Rowan considered her words. She was too earnest to be lying, her wide-eyed nature bordered on an almost doelike innocence.*
*But given her powers, such innocence was a danger to everyone involved. In the wrong hands…*
Rowan: "Not to be unsympathetic to your people, but I’m not exactly in the best position myself to be managing the disputes of the Fae."
*Rowan considered her words. She was too gullible, too guileless to be playing some greater game with him. Perhaps she really was this naive.*
*Rowan could use that.*
Rowan: "What’s in it for me? It sounds like you’re just asking me to add the Fae’s problems to my own, considerable list."
*Rowan considered her words. She was too earnest to be lying. But her trusting nature would make her easy prey for wolves seeking to use her.*
*…Though, her powers would make for an impressive chess piece.*
Rowan: "You’re asking me to help your kind with a problem that seems entirely their own."
Heartsong: "I wouldn’t have come to you if I didn’t think we had something to offer."
Heartsong: "My people are slow to trust, but we are fierce allies. You have seen the ease with which we traverse the leylines, and we know many paths the Twins do not. We would be grateful, I know we would."
Rowan: "And what do you get out of all this?"
Heartsong: "I just want to help you however I can."
Rowan: "Why?"
*Her eyes widened. The very question seemed to baffle her.*
Heartsong: "W-what do you mean?"
Rowan: "What possible reason could you have to want to help me?"
Heartsong: "Because… you deserve it?"
*Rowan blinked once. Twice. Of all the reasons the Fae could have given, he never would have expected that answer.*
Heartsong: "So are we in agreement, then?"
Rowan: "Maybe. Provisionally, if your information proves useful. I can’t promise how things will turn out with either Arzyl or Whitescar in that regard. Things could get ugly in spite of my intervention."
Heartsong: "I would never ask you to make such a promise. Your word alone means more than I can say."
*Rowan gestured with his hand to the fictional room in which they sat.*
Rowan: "So this is to be our conference room, then? A place to plan strategy?"
*Heartsong giggled, her tail swishing in mischievous arcs behind her.*
Heartsong: "It’s a dream, Rowan. It can be anything you want it to be, as you showed but a minute ago!"
Heartsong: "There are things that I know that my father and Lady Arzyl will wish to keep from you. My people are secretive; we do not like to reveal ourselves to outsiders."
Rowan: "So I’ve learned firsthand."
*Heartsong blushed, unable to meet his gaze.*
Heartsong: "I will tell you everything I know, in time… maybe you can find a path that doesn’t lead to bloodshed."
Rowan: "How do we seal the deal, then? A spell, some kind of ritual-"
*Heartsong tried and failed to stifle another giggle.*
Heartsong: "I think the Elder may have read you a few too many bedtime stories about us."
Rowan: "Heh. You would know, wouldn’t you?"
*The mischievous glint returned to her yellow eyes. Heartsong let out a low, almost purring growl.*
Heartsong: "Would you prefer I swear an oath of loyalty to you, instead?"
*There was a wavy, shivering feel in the air, and then everything changed again.*
*With a start he realized he was seated like a king atop the Throne of Bloodmeen.*
*Heartsong kneeled in supplication far below him at the foot of the dais. She looked up at him in expectant eagerness.*
*Very well, proceed.*
*Heartsong settled her hands in front of her, and tilted her head up to look at him. Her smile grew wide, like a fond, old friend.*
Heartsong: "I swear by Sol and the spirit that binds us…"
Heartsong: "To help and to serve you however I can, wherever I can, whenever I can."
Heartsong: "This I swear within the dragon’s dream, with faith that his slumbering ears will hear."
Heartsong: "I will follow you, Rowan Blackwell, wherever you may lead me."
*Her eyes held onto him for a long moment. A mischievous grin grew on her face.*
Heartsong: "Now, and forever."
*She bowed her head low against the ground, supplicating herself completely.*
*Several beats passed as she knelt at his altar. There was a strange sort of power in looking down on her from this place.*
Rowan: "All right, you’ve made your point."
*Heartsong lifted her head again, her tail wagging happily behind her as she beamed.*
Heartsong: "Just so!"
*A promise, remember? No oaths.*
Heartsong: "They are one and the same, Rowan. For a Fae, a promise is sacred."
Rowan: "Maybe. But to me there’s an important difference."
Rowan: "An oath is a verbal contract with no substance, as easy to break as anything else. But a promise implies trust."
Rowan: "Trust between two equals."
Heartsong: "I… I only offered it to prove I’d never break my word to you."
Rowan: "It’s a bad thing to break a promise…"
*Rowan’s thoughts returned for a fleeting moment to that instant at Briarbridge, staring into the Elders eyes for the final time. Heartsongs gaze held to him now in much the same manner.*
Rowan: "But it’s a worse thing to let a promise break you. Some promises - when made for the right reasons - ought to be broken. And I'd rather you had the choice."
Heartsong: "..."
*And just like that, they were back at Rowan’s dinner table, sitting face to face.*
Heartsong: "I promise to help you, Rowan. However I can."
Rowan: "And I promise to help you, Heartsong. However I can."
*She smiled at him, and he smiled back.*
Rowan: "What do you want from me? What do you have to gain from sifting through my memories like this?"
Heartsong: "I’m just trying to understand you."
Rowan: "I think you understand more than enough at this point. Where are we, right now?"
Heartsong: "Your dream grove."
Rowan: "My what?"
Heartsong: "Your dream grove. Your spiritual center within the Netherweald."
Rowan: "You’re talking in riddles again."
Heartsong: "I-I’m sorry! The Netherweald is… well, it’s the realm of spirits and dreams. It exists parallel to the world you know. It’s my home."
Heartsong: "The Leylines are its physical manifestation in your reality. We Fae live within them."
Rowan: "And my dream grove is…?"
Heartsong: "Your particular section of the Netherweald, one that all soul-bearing mortals possess."
Heartsong: "It is the spiritual representation of all your dreams, your memories, and your experiences. Like a grove in a forest."
Heartsong: "You visit this place whenever you sleep. It is tied to you; it exists within you."
Heartsong: "Think of me like a watcher at the door, staring into the room that constitutes your life."
Rowan: "So I noticed."
*Heartsong’s lips quivered as she glanced down, unable to meet his gaze. Her pale tail drooped towards the nonexistent ground behind her.*
Heartsong: "…I’m sorry for spying on you. I didn’t mean to impose."
*It’s okay.*
Rowan: "…It’s all right."
Rowan: "All things considered, I suppose there are worse memories you could have had me recall."
*I guess we can move on from it.*
Rowan: "Just so long as you understand that it's not okay to invade my memories."
Heartsong: "I did not intend to ‘invade’ your memories, Rowan."
*Don’t do that again without my permission.*
Rowan: "Whatever you were hoping to learn from me, you’ve found it. I’ve indulged your curiosity long enough."
Rowan: "My memories are my own, and not yours to tamper with. If you want to say something to me, you can damn well say it to my face."
*Heartsong shrank down into herself, her ears flattening back against her head.*
Heartsong: "O-okay…"
Heartsong: "I just… I want to help you."
Rowan: "Last we spoke, it seemed like you were trying to enlist my help."
Heartsong: "I-I am! I mean- we are… but I want to help you, too."
Rowan: "You’re not making much sense."
Heartsong: "I’m s-sorry! This isn’t how I thought things would go between us."
*Rowan folded his arms over his chest, affecting a relaxed posture. Despite the brave front she was trying to put up, the Fae was fearfully shy. *
Rowan: "Take your time. I’m a captive audience, after all."
*She took in a deep breath, and exhaled heavily. *

Heartsong: "…Like I do with everything else."
Rowan: "So why me?"

Heartsong: "Almost all of them."

*Heartsong giggled, her tail swishing in mischievous arcs behind her.*
Heartsong: "It’s a dream, Rowan. It can be anything you want it to be."
*Rowan considered the thought. He closed his eyes, concentrating on the memory of Bloodmeen Castle, of walking the walls at dusk.*
*To Rowans shock, when he opened his eyes, he was elsewhere, standing at the top of the gate wall. The sun was dying, the last rays of light peeking over the shattered hills that surrounded them.*
*Heartsong stood, side by side with him. Together they leaned against the crenellation, overlooking the castle.*
*She playfully nudged his shoulder.*
Heartsong: "You’re good at that."
Rowan: "Good at what?"
Heartsong: "Manifesting your will on the dream. You can even overpower a Fae’s influence."
Heartsong: "…There are things that I know that my father and Lady Arzyl will wish to keep from you. My people are secretive; we do not like to reveal ourselves to outsiders."

Heartsong: "They are one and the same, Rowan. For a Fae, a promise is sacred."

Rowan: "An oath is a verbal contract with no substance, as easy to break as anything else. But a promise implies trust."

Heartsong: "I… I only offered it to prove I’d never break my word to you."
Rowan: "It’s a bad thing to break a promise…"
*Rowan’s thoughts returned for a fleeting moment to that instant at Briarbridge, staring into the Elders eyes for the final time. Heartsongs gaze held to him now in much the same manner.*
Rowan: "But it’s a worse thing to let a promise break you. Some promises - when made for the right reasons - ought to be broken. And I'd rather you had the choice."
Heartsong: "..."
*And just like that, they were back at Rowan’s dinner table, sitting face to face.*
Heartsong: "I promise to help you, Rowan. However I can."
Rowan: "And I promise to help you, Heartsong. However I can."
*She smiled at him, and he smiled back.*
Heartsong: "…I wish this dream didn’t have to end so soon. It’s been a joy to talk to you."
Rowan: "The dream is ending?"
*Heartsong nodded, casting a glance around her. It was only then that Rowan noticed that the world was beginning to blur.*
Heartsong: "You’re waking up."

*The Fae flashed him a coy grin.*
Heartsong: "For now."
*She shyly offered Rowan her hand.*
Heartsong: "Would you… like me to show you the way back?"
*There was something specific in the offer of her outstretched hand. Something unspoken; a teasing fondness in her eyes.*
*Taking her hand would be making an entirely different kind of promise to her.*
*He took Heartsong’s hand, and felt his heartbeat quicken.*
*He took her slender hand in his, feeling the warmth of an unspoken connection.*
Rowan: "I would like that."
*She beamed, gently pulling him along with her.*
Heartsong: "Then, follow me."
*She led him by the hand to the edge of black nothingness, to the shore of a colorless pool almost indiscernible from the rest of the dream.*
*They stood there, hand in hand, staring into the abyss. At the very bottom of that nothingness, Rowan could just make out two windows of light.*
Heartsong: "…Are you ready to wake up?"
Rowan: "Yes."
Heartsong: "Then on three."
Heartsong: "One… two- hup!"
Rowan: "Gah!"
*The playful fox leapt a second too early, catching Rowan off-guard and dragging him down after her. He felt the sensation of falling, but it was as if they were moving in slow motion.*
*Together, the two plummeted towards the pair of peeking windows, opening up to bright light.*
*Heartsong laughed as she looked back at him, her yellow eyes gleaming with mischief. *
Rowan: "That was a dirty trick."
Heartsong: "Hehe! You’re fun to tease."
*He felt her hand squeeze his own, Heartsong’s expression softened. She leaned her face to his, and for a moment he thought-*
*Her lips brushed across his cheek. She pulled back, flashing a glimpse of her canines as she smiled at him.*
Heartsong: "…Goodbye for now, Ahmreval."
Rowan: "What does “Ahmreval mea-"
Rowan: "Guh!"
*Rowan’s head hit the pillow as if he’d just landed from a fall. He sat up in a rush, his heart pounding out of his chest as an image of the Fae’s last expression flashed through his mind.*
*He tried to calm his thudding heartbeat, but it only seemed to quicken at the thought of her. Rowan’s hand went to his cheek.*
*After a moment of reflection, he let out a small laugh.*
Rowan: "Goddess, what have I gotten myself into?"
*He politely declined the offer.*
*Rowan gently waved her off.*
Rowan: "I think I can find my own way back."
*If she was insulted by the rejection, she did not show it. Heartsong’s smile only broadened at the statement.*
Heartsong: "Yes, just so. Then until we meet again, Rowan."
*Now even Heartsong herself began to blur. She moved to turn away, but paused for a brief moment to look back at him.*
Heartsong: "…He was right to love you, you know? Whatever came after."

*The only thing left that he could see were a pair of curious yellow eyes, watching him in the darkness.*
Heartsong: "You know who."
*Rowan’s eyes peeked open, taking in the sight of the warm morning sun rising through his window. He laid there for a moment, listening to the sound of birds tittering in the distance.*
*For the first time in what felt like years, he awoke with a smile on his face.*
*So the little stowaway wanted to play games with him? Fine. He’d play games.*
*Try making the ‘Elder’ think he’s going senile.*
Rowan: "Ah forgive me, Elder, just a poor joke on my part. What were we talking about?"
Elder: "Your time in the war."

*Try changing the scenery and see
Rowan: "My apologies Elder, this is all a bit difficult to talk about."

*Rowan concentrated, imagining the fanciful scenario in his head. A world where the sun was the color of a lime.*
*His eyes peeked open to see midday on a lime green world.*
Elder: "…No more than usual, I suppose."
*Try giving the Elder a phobia he never had.*

*The old man crinkled his brow, as if struggling to remember his own opinion on the subject.*
Elder: "I… I did? That doesn't sound right."

Elder: "THRICE DAMNED CRITTERS! S-solansia preserve me, get it off! Get. It. Off!"
*Rowan watched with increasing amusement as the old man struggled futilely to brush it off his arm.*
*So… he could control not only the dream, but the Fae’s perception within the dream. Interesting.*
*It was high time he put this trickster Fae in her place. And he knew just the memory to do it.*
*The best way to teach a lesson, after all, was to use one he’d already taught to someone else.*
Rowan: "-I suppose we should be stopping soon, we’re nearly at the spot I chose."
Elder: "W-what-"
Elder: "What do you mean?"
*Rowan - now confident in what he was doing - closed his eyes and concentrated on the image in his head. The world around them turned to putty.*
*And just like that, they were on the outskirts of Arthdale, standing together at the base of a set of high hills that loomed over the landscape.*
*Just the sight of it brought a wistful smile to Rowan’s face. A happy memory of a simpler time.*

*He blinked, and suddenly he was staring at his young pupil. Fiery eyed and eager for his instruction.*

*Helayna - after a half-seconds pause - huffed and swept her fire red bangs to the side.*
Helayna: "Of course, I can! It’s just lugging around whatever equipment we need right, right? I’d just believed that we’d start by focusing on-"

Helayna: "Sir, have you considered that I’m wearing plate armour? Would it not be better if I changed into a tunic?"

*There was a great big smile on her freckled face as she accepted the pack. She threw it over her shoulder with a brash cavalierness that Rowan had not expected. Back then, it had charmed Rowan… just a little bit. *
*Meanwhile, his stowaway continued to play her part in the modified dream accurately. The Fae had no idea he’d even changed anything in the dream. As far as she was aware, she’d always been Helayna.*

Heartsong: "I..."

Heartsong: "You have a powerful will, Rowan. It gives you incredible latitude whenever someone like me visits your dream grove."

*Sensing Rowan’s dickering, the village leader called on his men to open fire. Rowan dodged to one side as a crossbow bolt twanged, shooting forth with sudden fury.* 
*The Dryad lets out an inhuman cry of anger and swarmed forward, lashing out with her vines as she slashed at villagers left and right. What followed was a short but brutal fight, one that left several villagers limbless and headless upon the ground.* 
*The townsfolk, faced with an ethereal being of far greater power than they, scattered in moments. The only one who maintained his composure throughout was the village leader, who bravely (or perhaps foolishly) rushed the Dryad as his friends were dying around him.* 
*They exchanged a few blows before the Dryad grabbed him by the neck, lifting him off the ground as the villager’s feet dangled. The leader cast a long, last look in Rowan’s direction, the fear and anger in his eyes palpable as the Dryad shoved her fist through his chest.* 
*Rowan looked away as the leader’s eyes rolled into the back of his head and the Dryad let him go, crumpling bonelessly to the ground.*
*The Dryad was wounded, a porcupine of crossbow bolts peppering her chest and body, though she seemed to take no notice of it. When it was all said and done, only Rowan and the injured Dryad stood in the empty clearing amidst the bodies.*
Isdruel: "The Queen will hear of this, treacherous fiend! You and all your kind will pay for what you have done!"
*Her threat hanging in the air, the Dryad’s tendrils wrapped around the bag of mushrooms, pulling them to her. She hefted them over her shoulder and turned away without a second glance, disappearing into the copse of trees as if she had never been there in the first place.* 
*Rowan picked his way across the body-strewn earth towards the forest exit, a pit in his stomach as he went.*
*Nightfall. The forest’s trees closed in with a haunting stillness. Rowan felt cold, clammy nervousness sit in the pit of his gut like a dead, nerveless fish. A stiff breeze blew the swirling leaves into a torrent of falling green.*
*His hand hovered close to his blade, his eyes flicking back and forth, searching for something hidden in the undergrowth. He held his breath, listening for the unseen assailant.*
*Then: the battle cries. The screeching wail of small, green creatures as the Goblin raiding party burst forth from all around. Some were riding wolves, others running forward on foot with an assortment of rickety short bows and plundered, rusty military equipment. *
*He ducked the first charging spearman, breaking the haft of the spear between his hands as he yanked the thing from the creature’s grasping fingers.*
*He slashed at the next one that came riding by on its wolf, dodging the snapping jaws as he cut down the rider in a swift, smooth horizontal strike.* 
*In the confusion, one the Goblins managed to leap forward, leaving a shallow cut in Rowan’s arm before the hero repaid in kind, impaling the creature on the spot with his longer blade.*
*The fight was a chaotic blur; within seconds several of the Goblins lay dead, and the rest had fled screaming into the undergrowth.* 
*Rowan let out a deep sigh, wiping his dirtied blade upon his pant leg before sheathing his blade. His arm smarted from the light cut, but he was all right otherwise. Fucking Goblins.*
*That night, Rowan tossed and turned in his bedroll. His head was hot, his cheeks flushed as he panted, despite the cool air. He was sweating, as he blinked in the darkness, he could see flashes of shapes and whorls of colors bleed across his eyes like a hallucination.*
*He groaned, sitting up out of his bedroll and leaning against a tree, staring up at the stars as his heart beat out of his chest. His hallucinations soon worsened: he saw burbling buboes, infected wounds, the slow, torturous decay of time upon a corpse left out in the open.*
*All the images were different, but all kept this unifying truth in his sight: disease.  The better part of the night passed this way, with Rowan drifting in and out of consciousness in an awful, waking limbo.*
*Amongst the horrid images of creeping, wet death, Rowan suddenly saw a bright light: a beautiful woman engulfed in white glimmers, an elegant voice emerging from her lips.*
Heartsong: "Let me in, Rowan. Let me help you. It is for the best. I am here for you."
*Trust the woman.*
*Rowan could not stand this interminable misery. He let go, allowing this strange woman into… well, he wasn’t quite sure. It seemed that the intent to open himself up to her was enough, as a sudden warmth suffused him.* 
*The woman’s smile became a brilliant, pale light; the radiance blinded him, removing all pain and discomfort. It was as if a fog had rolled away and he could finally see the daylight. She stood before him, glimmering like a strange, luminescent mirage.*
Rowan: "Are you… am I dreaming? Or are you really here in front of me?"
Heartsong: "Both."
*Her smile sent wings of laughter into Rowan’s heart. His breath was taken away by the ease with which she could instill joy.*
Heartsong: "You are lucky the Goblin’s attacked you while my dreaming body was nearby, Rowan."
Rowan: "..What?"
Heartsong: "Ha ha! It is all right: you don’t need to fully understand now. Just know that my name is Heartsong, and that I am here to help you. I am a Dreamwalker."
Rowan: "..."
Heartsong: "I will aid you as best as I can through your recovery. Those creatures will be in for a surprise, when they come for you on the ‘morrow."
Heartsong: "Rest now. Come dawn, you will be hale and hearty, I will prepare you for their arrival."
*The next morning, a troop of Goblins flitted through the boughs of the forest surrounding Rowan’s sleeping place. They crept forward, silent save for the low growling of their wolves on the periphery.* 
*The Goblins had coated their blades in a deadly hallucinatory toxin, and had paid a high price to incapacitate the warrior. They would not be denied their spoils, now that he was helpless to resist.*
*As they came upon the warrior’s full bedroll, a trio of them approached, their weapons at the ready. At a signal from the leader, they flipped open the blanket, beneath which they fully expected to see a feverish and incoherent Rowan.*
*What they discovered instead, was a pile of rocks. Turning to one another in confusion, they chattered back and forth in their language. It was only the sound of Rowan’s battle cry far above them that caused them to stop their loud bickering.*
*Rowan, having waited for his opportune moment to strike, leapt from the branches high above, his sword drawn. The nearest Goblin half-heartedly lifted her sword to fight him, but Rowan simply yanked the hilt from her hands and tossed it away.*
*Surprised, caught off guard and not expecting the warrior to be so healthy, the Goblins panicked and fled, dispersing in all directions. Rowing let out a grunt of satisfaction and brushed himself off. He knew the goblins wouldn’t be back after that stunt.* 
*Seeing that it was now well into the morning, he resolved to continue onwards with his quest, sparing only a glance backwards after packing up to the tree he had lain against. He wondered to himself if he’d ever get to see the beautiful Heartsong again.*
*Resist the illusions with all your strength.*
*Panting, shivering and feverish, Rowan nonetheless mustered his strength and did everything he could to resist the illusions, especially the beautiful siren calling to him.* 
*His resistance seemed to succeed, as her beautiful visage slowly faded away to nothingness, leaving him alone with his visions of death, decay and drudgery.*
*The next morning, a cold and shivering Rowan was rudely awoken by the pack of Goblins from the day before, come to finish the job. He stumbled out of his bedroll, shakily drawing his sword as he struggled to defend himself.* 
*The Goblins spare just enough time to kick his legs out from under him and shove him to the ground before moving to his possessions. One particularly spiteful creature even kicks him in the gut as she passes.*
*Helpless, Rowan watched as the Goblins pilfered his purse. The creatures laugh and call him all manner of names in Goblin as they leave, heaping insults upon him as their wolves snarl and snap from a distance. Darkness claimed Rowan as he once again fell into a stupor.*
*Later that afternoon, Rowan awoke once more, light on coin and feeling profoundly nauseous. His vision had at least returned to normal - thank the gods. And with some effort, he found that he could walk.* 
*With his camp in shambles and his coin purse noticeably lighter, he soldiered on, promising to himself that he’d kick the first Goblin he saw next square in the stomach.*
*Rowan felt the prickling sensation at the back of his neck with the weary awareness of a man too-used to being followed. Craning his neck around for what felt like the hundredth time, he looked over his shoulder, across the wide plains of Rosaria and saw nothing.* 
*He let out a sigh and shouldered his pack, moving onwards towards a small canyon in the distance where he intended to set his trap.*
*Whoever - or whatever - it was, the thing had been pursuing Rowan for days now, hovering just out of sight, always a vague mirage on the horizon, a flicker across the waving fields of grain.*
*Today was the day he would finally catch them in the act… whoever it was. Glancing around at the high ridges of the hills that formed the narrow canyon, Rowan knew that he had found the right place.* 
*The only real way to follow was to take the narrow path through the canyon. Now all that was left was to decide how to engage this would-be stalker.*
*Set up a classic but effective trap.*
*Rowan decided that the sneakier approach was likely the best. Given his lack of real knowledge of what kind of foe he was facing, the element of surprise would be crucial in ensuring his ultimate victory over whatever ended up crashing through the brush.*
*Moving with a speed that belied his own weariness, Rowan took his boots off and removed his shirt, sticking just on the inside of a deep crevice in the wall of the canyon. He wanted it to look like he had found some momentary respite inside the crevice.*
*Taking care to avoid leaving any tracks behind, Rowan scaled the nearby cliffside, scrabbling on hands and knees near the top to reach an ideal vantage point.* 
*Then, he waited.*
*It took several minutes, but Rowan finally managed to spot a strange, furry object moving across the trammeled earth as it entered the mouth of the canyon. He saw the shaggy pelt and dark fur of a Beastman wolf, moving with swift surety towards his hiding spot.*
*It paused for a long moment, lifting its long snout into the air to sniff at the wind.* 
*Fortunately, Rowan had foreseen this eventuality, and had positioned himself downwind of the creature so as to be out of his scent. Noting the discarded boots near the crevice below Rowan’s hiding spot, the Beastman slipped into the crevice.* 
*Rowan took this as his chance. He scurried down the hillside, sword in hand, ready to face his now-cornered opponent.*
*The creature didn’t notice him till it was almost too late. Lunging out of the way of Rowan’s deadly strike, it spun around in place, snarling as it drew its blade.*
*Something off caught in the Beastman’s nose. The creature’s head snapped up to stare directly at Rowan atop the cliff. The warrior’s folly became immediately apparent: he had placed himself upwind and inadvertently given the creature a full whiff of his presence.* 
*Its golden eyes blazed into Rowan’s own, locking gazes with him as a voracious smile spread across its bestial features. It was a monster’s toothy grin, one only the Beastmen were capable of producing.*
*In a flash the creature has drawn its sword, lunging up the short cliff face at Rowan, who had little choice but to defend himself.*
*Face whomever is stalking him head on.*
*Rowan let out a frustrated grunt; he was tired of playing games. If the thing that was following him was so intent on continuing the pursuit, then Rowan would face it head on like a man.*
*He turned to face the entrance to the canyon, drawing his sword in one long, languid movement. Sching! Screeched the blade as it slid from its scabbard.*
*There was the sudden crumbling of rocks overhead, and Rowand glanced up in time to see a grey blur leap at him from the cliffside above.* 
*The height was such that Rowan hadn’t expected an attack from that direction, naively assuming anyone stupid enough to do so would die from the fall. He lifted his blade just in time to block a brutal strike that might have decapitated him had he been less aware.*
*The beast landed to his right and rolled to its feet, snarling at Rowan as it lifted its serrated blade once more. This was no mere mortal: it was a Beastman!* 
*The Wolfish creature grinned, wiggling its blade, which dripped red from the tip. Rowan lifted his hand unthinkingly to his cheek. His hand came away red. Rowan let out a warrior’s yell and charged the creature.*
*Rowan smoothly sidestepped the Beastman’s clumsy strike, smacking into the rock formation next to him and chipping off chunks of rock.* 
*He ducked when the creature slashed in a sweeping half-circle at his head, backpedaling as the monstrous beast continued to advance upon him, giving no space to recover.*
*The creature was faster, stronger, and more ferocious by far than Rowan. It became immediately apparent that he could only hold off the creature for so long by going toe to toe with it.* 
*Rowan batted aside another strike for his head as he searched in desperation for some advantage in the fight. He got in a good swing or two, but the creature’s peternatural agility always saw his precise strikes come only within grazing distance.*
*At last, Rowan slipped, his foot catching upon the uneven ground and giving way. He stumbled backwards, his guard breaking as the monster leapt to take advantage of the opening.* 
*However, instead of disemboweling the warrior, the creature kicked him in the chest, sending him sprawling to the ground. Rowan’s sword clattered out of his hands. Rowan tried to scramble to his feet, but the creature unmanned him by throwing his head back and laughing.* 
Whitescar: "A good tussle."
*Tussle? As far as Rowan was concerned this was a fight to the death! He struggled to his feet, leaping to retrieve his blade. But the Beastman unnerved him by sheathing his own.*
Whitescar: "You’ve got good form, for a pinkskin. You should be honored you held off as long as you did."
Whitescar: "I see now what the Golden One first saw in you… you may yet prove to be the way forward for us."
Rowan: "What in the hell are you talking about?"

Whitescar: "This was a test. You have earned the right to speak with us, for you have earned our respect."

Whitescar: "...But now is not the moment. Now is the time for the hunt!"

*...The Golden One?*
*Years of married life and months of imprisonment have made Rowan careless, and much to his dismay, he failed to notice an old bear trap hidden in the tall grass.* 
*It took him only a few minutes to free himself, but he was unable to carry on for the better part of an hour thanks to the incredible pain from the very nasty gashes now decorating his shin.*
*Thankfully nothing was broken and there was no permanent damage.*
*Once he got back to the castle he'd be able to get magical healing, but in the meantime he'd have to take things much slower and manage with just mundane bandages.*
*Throughout most of the six realms there are small pockets of Solensia's power, around which beings of energy or strongly of the light tend to gather.*
*Some of these nexuses have become the hearts of cities, others end up giving rise to great reefs in the oceans, and in this case, form the center of an enchanting forest glade with a fairy spring in the center.*
*Rowan drank deeply of the pure water and filled his flasks from it before departing on his way.  Already he could feel the rejuvenating effects flow through his body.*
*Jezera didn't care much for his report on the subject, and told him not to bother her about these pockets anymore.*
*Suddenly, a blur of black, white, and insectoid fur fell upon Rowan!*
*He lept back instinctively, whipping out his sword to face his attacker head on. The foe was a drider, a half-human half-spider monster.*
*These monsters were native to the forests of Rosaria and among its most dangerous denizens. The one currently attacking Rowan, a male, obviously intended to make him into a meal if it had the chance.*
*However, the fight quickly turned against the drider.  This beast was large, strong, and overconfident.  It obviously thought Rowan easy prey, which allowed the hero to turn its strength against it in short order.*
*Of course, there was always the possibility that things would go very badly for Rowan very quickly if he slipped up.  The drider's poison would cripple him if it managed to bite him.  It was fortunate then that Rowan didn't screw up.*
*He managed to crash the drider into one tree and then fling it down a hill where it landed in a heap, dazed.  Sensing an opportunity, Rowan quickly rushed down the slope and used some rope to bind the creature's legs and then sent a message to have it picked up.*
*A fully grown drider would be difficult to handle, but it was a prize for the breeding pits that couldn't be passed up.  How often did you capture a live drider without meaning to?*
*The fighting was tense, with every moment being a chance at life or death. The hero was slightly better than his opponent, though he knew that a slip up would quickly reverse their fortunes due to the poison the creature possessed.*
*Finally he found his chance, and managed to lob one of the drider's legs clean off. It shrieked and skittered unsteadily for a moment, giving Rowan a chance to follow up and claim one of its mandibles.*
*Realizing it had been bested, the hero's foe turned away and fled into the woods. He knew that he wouldn't be able to catch a drider in the forest, even one missing a leg. Instead he simply claimed his prize and continued on his way.*
*If you could find the right alchemist, fresh drider poison glands were very valuable.*
*This was not the hero's day, as he was fighting against the creature essentially blow for blow.  Unfortunately, his foes blows could poison him, so Rowan was finding himself becoming weaker as the fight continued.*
*Thankfully he managed to force the creature to retreat in one desperate last attack.  There was no way he could outrun a drider in the forest, so that was the only way he could turn this around.*
*Unfortunately poison didn't suddenly leave the body if you had a chance to rest for a few minutes.  This was going to be another problem added to the pile.*
*The creature's attacks were intense and brutal, forcing the hero back again and again.  Under normal circumstances, Rowan would never have been fairing this badly, but his injuries were catching up with him.*
*After being bitten a second time and finding his strength was fading almost completely, Rowan made the decision to fall back to castle Bloodmeen.  He sent a message to Jezera asking for an immediate recall.*
*Rowan vanished, leaving a very frustrated drider behind.  So bad were his injuries that he was forced to rest for the remainder of the week just to get back on his feet.*
*As the forest opened up into a small clearing. Rowan discovered, slumped against the trunk of a old oak tree, the body of a knight, riddled with arrows. This was the work of no single archer, he knew, but instead an entire gang of bandits.*
*Against that number, even a man in armour had no chance. Many arrows had found the seams between where his plates fit poorly. A few had even punched clean through, leading Rowan think that it must have been cheap, and shoddily made.*
*How long the body had lain there, he did not know, but it must have been a few days judging from the pungent smell of decomposing flesh.*
*The armour was scored with tooth and claw marks as well, suggesting some of the larger forest scavengers had tried to feast on the corpse, before giving up.*
*As far as the knight's killers were concerned, Rowan could see as few signs of human life in his current vicinity as he had while walking through the woods for the better part of the day.*
*Removing the armour to search the knight would take time, leaving him exposed. He would have to think hard whether looting the body was worth the risk.*
*Search the knight*:
*Leave the body*:
*Deciding it was too dangerous, and not wanting to meet the same fate as the knight, Rowan decides not to search the body. Let somebody else take that risk, he thought, as he left it behind to continue his journey.*
*As Rowan suspected, the armour was cheaply made, and would offer more in the way of liability in a fight than it would protection*
*The sword, however, had been made by a craftsman of some skill - and a rather ill-famed reputation. A small rune at the base of the blade told Rowan all he needed to know. A tusked face, twisted in agony as it was being split in half.*
*He held one of the orc-slayers - a group of swords infamously known for being quenched in the blood of captured orcs. A practice that held little merit as far as blacksmithing went - but practicality was not in the creator’s mind.*
*Trying not to grimace at the disgusting creation, he sheathed the blade, and attached it to his belt. He would have no use of it, but to the Bloodmeen orcs this was a rare find, one that would soon be a target of many bets.*
*As Rowan suspected, most of the armour was cheaply made, and would offer more in the way of liability in a fight than it would protection. The sword's blade was pitted, likely to shatter should it come into contact with something more solid.*
*The gauntlets however, were a rare find. Expertly crafted, with subtle runes etched onto the edges of the plate that hinted they had been imbued with some minor enchantment.*
*They would be of little use to Rowan himself, as their heavy construction would hamper his swordplay. But he imagined both Cliohna and Greyhide would love to examine them.*
*They would be of little use to Rowan himself, as their heavy construction would hamper his swordplay. But he imagined Cliohna would be interested in the runes themselves.*
*Thanking the sisters for his luck, Rowan slipped the gloves into his pack.*
*As Rowan suspected, most of the armour was cheaply made, and would offer more in the way of liability in a fight than it would protection. The sword's blade was pitted, likely to shatter should it come into contact with something more solid.*
*After removing all the armour from the body, Rowan had nothing to show for it. If the man had been secreting anything on his person, it had already been picked clean by whoever had killed him.*
*Now he was left with a wasted day, the rather unappealing corpse before him, and the hope that he'd be able to get the smell of decomposition out of his head sooner rather than later.*
*While moving through the brush, Rowan noticed that something was wrong. The background noises were growing quieter than they should be and he felt the tinge of magic in the air. He was on guard now, moving as quietly and as stealthily as possible.*

It was only through magical means that he was able to track Rowan this far, and then only thanks to having warded his slice of the forest.*
*Draw your sword, and rid Rosaria of this blight.*

*The poor bastard tried to maneuver the final zombie between himself and Rowan, but decomposing corpses make for poor meatshields. Rowan’s sword pierced through his chest, impaling both the undead and its master.* 
Rowan: "Should’ve stayed in your crypt, necromancer."

*Besides, killing people like him was a reward in itself.*

*Avoid the necromancer. Discretion is the better part of valor.*

*Eventually he managed to get out of the corrupted part of the forest, at which point his hunter gave up the chase. Whoever that was, he didn't like guests and didn't seem to want anything to do with the rest of the world.*

*Strike a deal with him.*
*Cleaning his throat, Rowan emerged from the trees, hands in the air as he addressed the surprised necromancer.* 
*He explained he represented an emerging power in Rosaria, a power who would very much like to cooperate with people like him. His talents would be of use to the twins.*

*Swiftly, he fled into the forest. But much to his dismay, the necromancer managed sent him a parting gift - a bolt of necrotic energy that took the hero square in the back.*

*He stumbled back, trying to put some distance between himself and the necromancer. But zombies, earlier so laughably slow, now seemed to rush at him with renewed vigor.*

*A playful giggle could be heard in the air. It sounded both friendly and mischievous, which suggested that a forest spirit had taken an interest in Rowan's presence. He knew how this went.*

*For a change, Rowan’s passage through the forest had afforded him a pleasant surprise, instead of the usual brush with danger.*
*In the glade before him he could see a vision in green and brown; a pair of long legs, covered in bark and leaves, rose into a pert, round ass.*
*The woman, obviously a forest spirit, was bent forward from the waist, almost horizontally, and over her back was splayed hair coloured with all the hues of autumn.*

Dryad: "Hello? Is somebody there?"
Dryad: "I’ve been trapped here for hours, please…. Please help me..."
Rowan: "Hang on, I’m coming."

Rowan: "What happened?"
Dryad: "It’s, ah, a bit embarrassing to admit…"
