Rowan: "One of my vaguer notions is that she might have even made you somehow. With Jezera, you never know for sure."
*Shaya’s reaction didn’t disappoint. Her eyebrow arched upwards and didn’t return to normal.*
Rowan: "The second thing I determined is this. I don’t think you’re telling me the real reason you’ve been having me visit. It’s certainly not because you like me, specifically."
Rowan: "I think Jezera ordered you to get close to me. She wanted you to seduce me. To what end, I’m not entirely sure."
Rowan: "But, what I do know for sure, is that almost all of our meetings have been set up in advance for purposes besides the stated ones. You’ve been manipulating me."
*In a dainty gesture, she brought her knuckle to the front of her veil and giggled into it.*
Shaya: "I’m not sure which of your theories is more fanciful, Rowan!"
*In a dainty gesture, she brought her knuckle to the front of her veil and giggled into it.*
Shaya: "And what would give a man of your deductive reasoning such a fanciful idea?"
Shaya: "Come now. Jezera made me? Were she my mother, she’d have to be a little older. No?"
*Rowan let her statement hang in the air between them. He eased back into his chair. Her reaction was expected thus far. Nothing that would shake his confidence in his conclusion.*
Rowan: "Would you like to hear my reasoning?"
*A lull descended over the conversation. Nonplused by his lack of reaction, Shaya reached out and grabbed another almond. Then, rather than eat it. She tossed it back on the plate and rose to her feet.*
Shaya: "This may require wine. Continue, then."
Shaya: "Start with your mistrust of my intentions, if you would. I’m eager to hear what schemes this imagined version of myself is engaged in. She sounds like a fascinating character."
*As she spoke, she poured herself a drink from a pitcher into an ornate goblet.*
Shaya: "Though, in one sense, you are not far off from the truth. You were given our sessions as a reward for your service."
Shaya: "I was ordered to please you. Surely you’re not mistaking the relationship between whore and client for something more sinister?"
Shaya: "But, that doesn’t make our rendezvous insincere. There was no obligation for me to seek out your company, after all."
*Rowan shook his head forcefully in response. *
Rowan: "I've mistaken nothing. What you’ve described to me is but a cover."
Rowan: "All of these sessions have been about making me into a returning customer."
Rowan: "After all, seduction is your expertise. Your work is getting yourself or your agents close to valuable targets. Then to use that proximity to gather information and manipulate their behaviour."
Rowan: "I’m the steward of the castle. A valuable asset to Jezera, but one who must be controlled. It makes sense that she’d want to keep close tabs on me. Perhaps to get more leverage."
*Rowan reached across the table and took one of Shaya’s discarded almonds, popping it into his mouth. He winced slightly; he’d never had an almond before. He’d expected it to be sweeter.*
Rowan: "In fact, it’s fascinating you’d bring up that reward of service. I wasn’t truly the one who discovered the plot. A cloaked stranger came to visit me in the middle of the night and handed me the information that led to Jezera gifting me these sessions."
*He studied her face to see if it would break with surprise, but her attention remained steady. Did that mean that she already knew? Or merely that she was disciplined?*
Rowan: "But, you knew that fact already, didn’t you?"
Rowan: "At the time, I’d thought they’d come to me because Jezera wouldn’t trust them. At the time, I’d asked myself “who would want Jezera to know about the plot, but not to inform her themselves?"
Rowan: "But that was the wrong question. Because the person who gave me that information...was you."
Rowan: "Last night, I cross checked that letter of information with the invitation you’d given me to your party. You told me that the invitation was written in your own hand."
Rowan: "It was the same hand that wrote both. There were some slight variations to throw off an eyeball analysis, but many of the letters had uncannily similar shapes."
Rowan: "I think you were the one who visited me that night."
Rowan: "And I think the reason you did it was because Jezera wanted an excuse to send me to you for further sessions, but needed a cover so I wouldn’t know the true reason."
*Shaya tilted her head and took a sip from her wine.*
Shaya: "A fascinating story. Misdirection. Seduction. Betrayal. Should I be upset that you think me so treacherous, or flattered that you believe me so skilled?"
Rowan: "Is that a denial?"
Shaya: "But of course."
Shaya: "In your charming little tale, you gave no reason to suggest Jezer’aca was behind it. What should I make of this slander?"
*Rowan chuckled.*
Rowan: "Well that brings us back to my other accusation, doesn’t it?"
Rowan: "I will admit, I’ve been noting down some of what you told me about your life in Qerazel. Some of my other observations as well."
Rowan: "Here is what I pieced together from it."
*By now, Shaya had returned to her repose on the couch. With her free hand, she used an eastern paper fan to cool herself.  Her ochre eyes were trained intensely on her companion.*
*Jezera’s trust in her.*
Rowan: "Jezera seems to trust you, and that’s very unusual in and of itself. She barely trusts her own brother. This was what first drew my interest in you."
Rowan: "On the first day we met, She went so far as to tell me that you’re the one person she considers trustworthy beyond doubt. An incredibly strong statement of support."
*She waved her free hand dismissively.*
Shaya: "Surely the cause of your mistrust isn’t that a woman is close to her childhood friend?"
Rowan: "Jezera doesn’t trust anyone. Certainly not her other childhood friends. So... why does she trust you?"
Rowan: "Though, the way you continue to portray your relation with her… that’s not quite true, is it? It’d be more apt to call you lovers in private."
Rowan: "Or perhaps… a Mistress and her Slave."
Rowan: "She has her talons in you pretty deep, doesn’t she?"
*Her eyebrows narrowed slightly.*
Shaya: "A bold thing for a man to make claims about what goes on in private between two people whom he has not seen alone together. One must wonder the source of such a claim."
Rowan: "One must."
Rowan: "You’ve certainly gone pretty far out of your way for her sake. Done things no ordinary person would do for her. Probably some that common standards would call evil."
Rowan: "Is it so strange for me to think that she’d have tested your loyalty somehow? And that the result of the test was a solidification of her trust in you?"
Rowan: "But, that’s just the context."
*Jezera’s role in her training.* 
Rowan: "There’s the matter of your training as a courtesan. If I did my due diligence correctly, you were trained at the Empress of Waters brothel in Qerazel."
Rowan: "The very building we’re sitting in is a testament to your training. Jezera designed it as an identical replica of the original building."
*Shaya took another, careful sip from her drink.*
Shaya: "A fact that I have done nothing to hide."
Rowan: "Indeed, but I also know how you ended up there. Jezera, who’d been your friend at the time, had arranged it."
Rowan: "She convinced you to start, she got the assent of the madame. She even paid out of pocket for your training."
Rowan: "Though, you didn’t much like your training, did you? You don’t show much hesitation now, but there was a period where you were half being forced into it, weren’t you?"
Shaya: "Where did you get that silly notion?"
Rowan: "The way you talked about your apprenticeship; when we were discussing that training song you used. It sounded quite traumatic."
Shaya: "You assume much."
Rowan: "Maybe, but if the methods that were employed on you are half as serious as those you use here... it must have been a trying experience."
Shaya: "This is all a fascinating stroll through my past. But to what end?"
Rowan: "Not much. Simply… there was a period of your life when Jezera was very invested in shaping you for her own aims."
Rowan: "...And you weren’t always entirely a willing participant."
Rowan: "It’s almost enough to make me wonder if you were the one who wanted to be a courtesan in the first place."
*The strangeness of the veil.*
Rowan: "Of course, there is the veil. It’s quite a fascinating touch. It gives you an air of mystique; makes you hard to read. I can see why you like it, as an accessory."
Rowan: "But, you don’t take it off, even in a situation that would warrant it. You’re pretty dedicated to not showing your face."
Rowan: "I’m sure most men think you’re hiding something under there. Some kind of scar or imperfection? Perhaps you’re hiding features that might be recognized in some way."
Rowan: "But, that certainly isn’t true. I happen to know someone who caught a glimpse of you without the veil. And they told me that you’re just as beautiful with the veil gone."
Rowan: "If that’s the case, why would you still keep your appearance hidden? A beautiful face would actually help you draw in customers."
*Perhaps unconsciously, her palm went to her cheek. The delicate tips of her fingers pressed gently against the soft material of the veil. *
Shaya: "If that’s the case, either I’ve been more lax than I’ve intended. Or perhaps this spy of yours is a liar or was prone to exaggeration? Do you truly believe they would tell you the truth?"
*Rowan’s eyes narrowed on her.*
Rowan: "With my life."
Rowan: "Still, I find it fascinating that Jezera is the only one you would purposefully show your face to."
*Shaya responded with a very atypical dismissive snort.*
Shaya: "Some ‘mystery.’ I love Jezera’aca as a sister."
Rowan: "Most people don’t sleep with their sisters."
Rowan: "I, of course, wondered if it was just a custom among whores in the Empire. Or perhaps in the particular brothel where you were trained."
Rowan: "But, no one I spoke to knew anything about such a tradition in Qerazel. Your refusal to show your face is as strange to them as it is to me."
*She sighed.*
Shaya: "I could have told you that myself, my friend. Still, what does any of this prove?"
Rowan: "I think that the veil is there to hide a particular discomfort. It’s not a general or traditional object."
Rowan: "You’re hiding something. Something you don’t feel totally comfortable with. And you’re hiding it from everyone."
Rowan: "In fact, you’re so uncomfortable, you might even dislike mirrors because of what they show."
*Her bodily perfection.*
Rowan: "There’s another matter that drew my thinking in this direction."
Rowan: "At the party, you told Magister Lirio about a boating accident that left you with a scar on your back. Afterwards, I asked you about the truth of the story. You claimed you hadn’t made it up."
*She squinted him with lidded eyes.*
Shaya: "Did I? I barely recall."
Rowan: "You did. But the scar isn’t there, is it Shaya? That night, I looked for it."
Rowan: "So either you were lying to me at the time, or it had once been there, but is now gone somehow."
Shaya: "Surely then, by your logic, I must have been lying."
Rowan: "And yet… it’s more than that."
Rowan: "You don’t have a single scar, do you? For that matter, not even freckles or birthmarks."
Rowan: "Your body lacks imperfections. Anything you might have picked up from day to day living. No pox marks, nothing from childhood."
Rowan: "No wonder you’re so confident you can prepare for performances with only a slight hint of makeup. There’s nothing to cover."
Shaya: "Surely this delightful investigation wasn’t just an excuse to compliment my appearance? Although, it is appreciated."
Rowan: "It’s not natural. Some things, you can hide with makeup and good care. But, it’s almost as if your body is only a few years old."
*That earned Rowan another laugh from his hostess.*
Shaya: "Your most outlandish accusation yet."
Rowan: "Not so outlandish when speaking to the closest confidant to one of the most powerful mages I know."
Rowan: "A woman who has herself admitted to being used as Jezera’s magic guinea pig in her youth."
Rowan: "And whatever the cause, it can’t have been a simple spell either."
Rowan: "I’m no expert on magic nonsense myself, but I know enough to realize that the kind of power you’d need to make a change like that would be a complex and dangerous force to dabble with."
Rowan: "It must have been a very intense and invasive process."
Rowan: "It’d be pretty stupid of me not to draw the straight line from that towards the veil you wear, don’t you think?"
Shaya: "..."
*For once, she didn’t have an immediate retort. Rowan caught on to the hesitation immediately.*
*A change in appearance*
Rowan: "But, why would Jezera have changed to your appearance? It seems drastic, but the motive is obvious."
Rowan: "And some things I’ve picked up suggest you had a major makeover at some point."
Rowan: "Qerazel is very concerned with matters of that sort, no? I’ve heard that the nobility there prize beauty above all else. Someone who wanted to advance there has good reason to pay close attention to their looks."
Rowan: "Consider what you told me about your family. I remember what you said about your family, that they would not even recognize you if they saw you. You meant it literally, didn’t you?"
Shaya: "Must you nitpick every word I spoke to you prior?"
Rowan: "What can I say? You’ve done a good job getting my attention."
*Her debut.*
Rowan: "There’s another incident that’s drawn my interest. At several points, I heard talk of your debut as a courtesan. I think that event was important."
Shaya: "My debut? What do you know of that?"
Rowan: "You told me about it yourself, remember? During my visit over tea time."
*She retreated from him slightly and reached for her goblet for another drink.*
Shaya: "Ah. I had forgotten."
Rowan: "Just what I heard from gossip during the party. You really should have known better than to just let me wander around talking to your customers."
Shaya: "Evidently."
Shaya: "So?"
Rowan: "Just that, if the other conclusions I’ve drawn are true, then there’s a connection. Whenever this change to you happened, it probably happened just beforehand."
Rowan: "Your debut is an important event for your marketability as a courtesan in Qerazel. One where appearance matters most."
Rowan: "Jezera was involved in the process. You said so yourself. She must have been very invested in making sure it went well."
Rowan: "But, there’s something about the event itself that was very unusual."
Rowan: "Most debuts normally happen for a courtesan with years of training and reputation already developed. But, you had your start with nothing. As if you just… appeared out of nowhere."
Rowan: "Your records certainly bear that out. How many clients did you have more than three years ago? I saw almost none."
Shaya: "Ah, so you’ve snooped through my client records as well? A bold admission. A more spiteful woman might find that upsetting."
Rowan: "You’re a spymistress aren’t you? Isn’t subterfuge part of the job?"
*Shaya rolled her eyes.*
Shaya: "This proves even less than your other wild conjectures."
*That's all.*
*Shaya had let him go on, with only the occasional retort in between. But, now it was time for him to get to the point.*
Rowan: "My picture of the specifics is incomplete. But, this is what I do know."
Rowan: "You’re loyal to Jezera. Very loyal, to the point you’d do anything for her. Jezera, being Jezera, saw this as an opportunity. Why let the blind loyalty of a subordinate go to waste?"
Rowan: "So she did something to you. And when it was done, you were the ideal agent. Beautiful, seductive, manipulative."
Rowan: "Whatever she did to you, or made you do, it left your body different from how it had been before. Changed."
Rowan: "And when it was done, you were someone else"
Rowan: "And whatever this change was, it is connected to why you never remove your veil."
*When Rowan finished his pronouncement he studied the reaction of his counterpart. Shaya merely watched Rowan in silence. The silent pause filled the entire room, leaving the two to simply look into each other’s eyes.* 
*So much of Shaya’s thoughts were always hidden behind the veil. Like a wall erected between her and others.* 
*Then, Shaya began to speak. Her words came out with the odd pause, punctuated by her soft speaking tone. It was even softer than usual. Guarded perhaps?*
Shaya: "-And you believe this tale is truly more plausible than the simple truth that I am a private woman when it comes to intimacy with clients?"
Rowan: "Look around you, Shaya. In this castle, the strange is the mundane."
*She placed her goblet of wine down on the table and straightened up to a proper sitting position. For the first time, their pose mirrored each other.*
Shaya: "What if I told you that your mind has wandered in the wrong direction entirely? That perhaps there is a true reason I wear the veil."
Shaya: "...And the reason is that I’m someone quite rightfully in fear of being recognized."
Shaya: "What if, one day, sweet Jezer’aca approached a girl whom she had no business befriending? Someone important. And from that day onward, that girl devoted herself in service to her new blood sister."
Shaya: "But, every day since then she must hide her identity, lest word of who she was get to the wrong people. Perhaps even her family."
*Rowan studied her closely. The notion would be plausible, in theory, yet something didn’t sit right about it.*
Rowan: "I’d wonder, then, why this girl doesn’t take her veil off when she’s alone with me. If it’s a matter of security, then there would be no issue at all. After all, this woman and I would both be on the same side."
Shaya: "..."
Shaya: "Perhaps this woman might wonder if we truly are on the same side."
*Another silence overcame the room. Shaya stared at Rowan. Rowan stared at Shaya. *
*Was what she had said true? It wouldn’t be out of character for Jezera to bring along a noble girl or some other girl of high standing. And such a rationale might explain all the secrecy about her…*
*Rowan frowned. No, that couldn’t be the case. After all, it didn’t address the matter of the scar… or lack thereof. What was the nature of her near-supernatural beauty? Simply being someone important wouldn’t explain that.*
*But, as Rowan considered the matter, Shaya suddenly rose to her feet and gave him a curt bow. Compared to her normal, flowing body language, it was almost rude.*
Shaya: "Please be so kind as to excuse me for a moment, Rowan. I had expected our session to be well under way by now, so this conversation is testing slightly."
Shaya: "Once I freshen up, I will gladly return to continue to reassure you."
Rowan: "Of cours-"
*But, Rowan didn’t even have time to finish his reply before the woman was making for the door. Before he could fully process it, Rowan was left alone.*
Rowan: "Interesting."
*Two things struck Rowan immediately.*
*The first was that her sudden departure meant he had evidently struck a nerve. If she felt compelled to leave so abruptly, then what he’d said to her wasn’t so absurd after all.* 
*The second was that she needed time to compose herself. That would not do.*
*Rowan stood up out of his seat and started down the hallway after her. As it turned out, finding where she’d gone didn’t prove especially difficult.*
*SMASH* 
*Rowan stopped at the entrance to the back dressing room. That was where the sound had come from.*
*Shaya stood alone, surrounded by shards of glass. One of the tall mirrors that lined the walls of the dressing room lay half-shattered on the floor. She stood there, trembling at attention, arms at her sides as her chest rose and fell.*
Rowan: "Shaya..."
*Shaya turned to face him. There was something totally different about her eyes. Their usual serene calm had turned into an intense storm. They bore into him with something approaching hatred.*
Shaya: "Get out."
Rowan: "I-"
Shaya: "Do you not understand this is a dressing room, Rowan? Isn’t there any type of privacy you know how to respect?"
*Rowan took a step backwards. Where had this come from? He’d seen brief flickers of emotion back during the conversation, but this was another matter entirely.*
*Shaya went to an open chest, pulled out a handcarved string instrument, and flung it at him. It went sailing in a sharp arc through the air. Rowan easily ducked out of the way. The instrument shattered against another of the mirrors and clattered to the floor, leaving a crack behind it.*
Rowan: "Shaya. Stop. This isn’t like you."
Shaya: "Is it, Rowan? Is it?"
*He took a step closer. She hunched her back and raised her arms to defend himself. But, he didn’t draw any closer. The question of whether Shaya could fight was a mystery that he had not yet properly answered.*
Rowan: "Shaya. Stop."
Shaya: "I-I said-"
Rowan: "Stop now."
Rowan: "Look, I understand you’re upset. I probably would be too in this situation. But, you’re not going to suddenly disprove my theories by breaking your changing room. So how about we just talk about this? You and me."
Rowan: "Do you really think you’re going to make me forget everything I learned by throwing a childish tantrum? Frankly, I’m disappointed in you. Stop and think for a second."
Shaya: "..."
*From the corner of her eye, she looked into a segment of the destroyed mirror. Its jagged edges there was a reflection of her, showing her at her most erratic. Her breath rose and fell.*
Shaya: "Fine."
*She settled backwards against the mirror. But, her pose was unlike any he’d seen her adopt. Arms crossed over her bosom and one leg over the other. It screamed defiance. She had closed herself off.*
Rowan: "I have to admit, you caught me by surprise there. That outburst was totally unlike you. I thought you were a calm person."
Shaya: "You have a great deal of thoughts about me. Not all are true. I am - normally - a controlled person. But I have never been a calm person."
Shaya: "..."
*She brought two fingers to a wide crack in the mirror and traced it along its course. Her eyes followed the polished nails as they slid down along the edges.*
Shaya: "Not everything you suggested before was correct…"
Rowan: "Hmmmm?"
Shaya: "Mistress Jezera didn’t order me to seduce you. I’ve reported your actions to her, as always, but I refrained from mentioning my full role."
Rowan: "What-"
*She turned her head from him, so that their eyes couldn’t meet.*
Shaya: "I decided to bring you to my bed of my own initiative. You stood out as particularly important from the moment of my arrival. So I immediately set to work on a plan to expand my influence with you."
Shaya: "When I visited you that night in secret, Mistress was unaware of my actions. The evidence had come to me from some of my girls who provide me with regular intelligence reports."
Shaya: "Afterwards, I had gone to Mistress and pretended to have been unaware of what you’d done. When she asked for my suggestion for a reward, I was the one to propose unrestricted access to my services."
*She turned her face back to him. Her eyes blazed with a fire he’d never seen from her. Pride. Surety. All things she’d seemed to lack in the past.*
Shaya: "You presume to understand our relationship, but you are as ignorant as a child."
Shaya: "Mistress doesn’t need to order me to seduce you. If it will make her happy, I will do it of my own will. Without a second thought."
*Rowan took a step back. The bluntness of her words had an impact all on their own. For all of the time and effort he’d put into considering Shaya as a puzzle, had he ever truly seen her as a force onto herself?*
Shaya: "Now. You want to know about my face, yes? I will tell you about my face."
Shaya: "To start with, you should know that what I’ve told you in the past is true. I merely decided there were certain details that were not for you. I really was born to middle-class merchants. I really was in a group of girls of a similar background. And Jezera really did join us."
*She glanced wistfully into the mirror, as if searching for something that wasn’t really there.*
Shaya: "There was Ismena, the fashionable one. There was Aysun, the pretty one. There was Makbule, the one who always knew the right thing to say to boys."
Shaya: "And then there was me."
Shaya: "To my face they said I was the clever one. But, I always knew the truth. I was the ugly one. Or at least, ugly by their standards."
*Rowan tilted his head slightly.*
Rowan: "That drastic?"
Shaya: "Your little theory would not make much sense had I already been beautiful, no?"
Shaya: "Our dynamic changed when Mistress joined. To us, it was like living in the dark and seeing the sun for the first time. We all loved her. We all worshipped her. Within weeks of joining, there was no dispute that she was our leader."
*Her voice took on a tone he’d never heard from her when she spoke about Jezera. It was loving and reverent. It reminded him most of the way that the high priests spoke of Solansia herself.*
Shaya: "But, the others could not see her radiance the way I could. They were always competing. Always seeking their own advantage. And as much as they wished to serve Mistress Jezera, they also wished to use her."
Shaya: "Over time they began to drift away. They had ambitions of their own. Mistress remains in contact with Ismena and Makbule. They remain her agents. But, they have their own lives."
Shaya: "But not me. I told Mistress that I would always serve her. That I would be whoever she wanted me to be. Whatever she wanted me to be."
Rowan: "So she wanted you to be a whore. But, it didn't turn out well, did it?"
*She sighed.*
Shaya: "We were young. We didn’t understand what a truly merciless environment elite brothels are."
Shaya: "I failed her. I could grasp the lessons. But everything was limited by my appearance."
Shaya: "There are things one can learn to give themselves an advantage. How to dress, how to wear makeup, how to do your hair. But, one cannot make the highest quality art without the highest quality materials."
Shaya: "So, Jezera showed me a way to change that."
*Shaya paused to catch her words. She turned from the mirror back to Rowan.*
Shaya: "The following is a secret of the highest order. Not merely the truth of the matter, but also that we are aware of it. Were you not already Jezera’s agent, even telling you this would be unthinkable."
*He ran a hand through his hair. A promise to Shaya to keep a secret carried with it more potential dangers than he’d have liked. But, at the moment, there wasn’t a good alternative.*
Rowan: "I understand."
*Rowan gave her a reassuring nod.*
Shaya: "Perhaps you have heard that the High Lords of Qerazel are renowned for their bodily perfection?"
Shaya: "They would have their subjects believe that it is their superior blood. That they are a higher race, and that this radiance descends through their generations. Perhaps they even imply that Solansia herself had blessed them with her special favour."
Shaya: "Lies. What they hoard for themselves and keep closely secret is magic."
Shaya: "Beneath Qerazel is a vast reservoir in a secret underground labyrinth. It’s so large it could be called a small lake. I am unsure of the origin, but it must have existed since Rakshan times. And from the waters there is a great white mist that wafts across the chambers."
Shaya: "On the walls there were...it is hard to describe. Jezera called them magic runes. But, they were golden and they lined the exterior like a vast ring."
Shaya: "Those who descend into it are changed. There is a picture of themselves in their head, and they emerge to match it."
*Rowan shifted uncomfortably in place. Learning that Jezera was dabbling in dangerous chaos magic would hardly have shifted his worldview. But, the idea that it was the Solansian Elites doing it...*
Rowan: "Wait- “A picture of themselves in their head..."
Rowan: "How much do you know about Nasim and his project?"
Shaya: "Enough to understand the intent behind your question. Your thought has been the same as mine. I’ve ensured he’s under proper surveillance to determine if there are indeed similarities."
Shaya: "But in terms of the magical arts, my only knowledge is what Jezera has taught me. I am afraid that his work is simply beyond me."
*A lake extolling mist surrounded in golden runes…The similarities to Nasim’s chamber were limited, but the principle sounded almost the same.* 
*But the castle’s resident dark wizard was clear on the chamber’s ties to Kharos’ and his chaos magic. Just what on earth was the Qerazel nobility doing?!*
*More questions… Perhaps once they excavate the chamber in the castle’s lower levels, they’ll understand more. This all couldn’t be a coincidence. *
*A chamber capable of changing the human body… Why did it sound so unnervingly similar to what Nasim had him uncover in the castle’s lower levels? *
Rowan: "Continue please..."
Shaya: "It’s unlikely I shall forget that night. We slipped past the guards of the external entrance and through the tunnels. How Mistress learned of this entrance, or even the labyrinth itself, I cannot speak to."
Shaya: "I remember being told how I should picture myself. Jezera had meticulously composed for me the perfect form. One whom men would lose every coin they had to spend time with. With her guidance in mind, I descended into the waters."
Shaya: "And when I emerged…"
*Shaya brought a hand to her forehead and slowly dragged it down the length of her body, all the way to her feet. It was a mockery of a display gesture a hostess might engage in. Her voice raised to a sing-song tone.*
Shaya: "Am I to your liking, M’Lord?"
Shaya: "Hehe."
Shaya: "An interesting thing about the transformation: I had not fully considered what my speaking voice would be in this shape."
Shaya: "But, in my mind, I pictured myself as the perfect courtesan. It is as if the water itself knew what I would consider the voice of the perfect seductress to sound like."
Shaya: "The process was more comprehensive than I could have imagined."
Rowan: "Seems like I’d pieced together most of the story."
*Rowan exhaled sharply. He’d come in reasonably confident about his interpretations. But, to have them vindicated, for the most part, was still a relief.*
Rowan: "That new body must have been quite a change for you? Did you resent Jezera for making you go through with it?"

*Alexia took a spot next to Andras, hands on her hips and an enraged glare on her face.*
Alexia: "Beloved..."
Alexia: "What is going on here? Is it true? Are you about to fight Liurial’s former lover?"
*Rowan chuckled nervously, running a hand across the back of his head. He’d meant for Alexia to learn of this only after the deed was done. That way she wouldn’t worry about him…*
Rowan: "This is nothing. I’ve handled far nastier foes than him before. I’m sure I can handle him without breaking a sweat."
*Andras snorted at Rowan’s assessment. He was acting as if this little lover’s confrontation was yet another spectacle for his amusement.*
Rowan: "Look, it would have been better had you stayed away. I didn’t…I didn’t want you to see it. There's a good reason I don’t want you to see me fighting."
Alexia: "Rowan..."
Alexia: "All this… all this for her? You bring a girl to our bed, now you’re risking your life for her?"
*Rowan frowned.*
Rowan: "I know that when we last spoke of her we didn’t… we didn’t really arrive somewhere we’re both happy with. I promise you, later…once she’s safe, we’ll talk again."
*But, right now, I need to focus on the fight to come. There is a right time and a wrong time for this conversation.*
*Alexia crossed her arms over her chest and went silent. Rowan knew the expression on her face well. This was Alexia closing up.*
Alexia: "Do what you must, Rowan."
Alexia: "We’ll talk at a better time."
*The moment between them was interrupted by Andras swaggering over, giving her a playful nudge to the side. Rowan scowled. He didn’t much like the familiarity he was showing.*
Andras: "Personally, I think widowhood will suit you wonderfully."
*Alexia stared at the demon in shock, momentarily stunned. When sense returned to her, she gave him a hard shove away. The demon laughed but didn’t resist.*
Alexia: "That’s not funny, Andras."
*Rowan let his attention drift back to the rest of the crowd. It had grown even in the time he’d come to examine it. Far in the back, in a shaded segment of the wall, someone had set up a stand with an assortment of snacks.*
*As he squinted, he found a goblin working it, selling steaming slabs of fried meat to some of the orcs.*
*Rowan couldn’t help but smile, albeit briefly. The one running it was none other than Cla-Mini, the young heir of the Cla clan.*
Cla-Mini: "Snacks! We got snacks here! Snacks for a fair price! Don’t watch the fight on an empty belly!"
*Rowan locked eyes with her, and she gave him a wink. Then she went right back to hawking food.*
*But, he didn’t have time for further distractions. In the distance, a second crowd was approaching. Elves of the exile band. Torlene and Galabraith, resplendent in their ceremonial garb, strode forth at their head.*
*Rowan gave his wife one last smile.*
Rowan: "Rowan. Be safe…"
Alexia: "Rowan. Be safe…"
Alexia: "..."
Alexia: "Don't die."
*Rowan thrust his cloak into her arms and turned back to face his foe.*
*Seeing that his moment had come, Rowan threw off his cloak and thrust it into the arms of a nearby orc. *
*Rowan and Torlene met each other in a bare length of wall, equidistant from the two crowds of spectators. As Torlene approached, Galabraith was trying to tell him something, but his words were lost in the wind.*
*The hero’s eyes darted around. This segment of the walls was in horrible disrepair. Crumbling stones, decayed walls… There was a non-negligible risk that it might collapse if too much force was applied to it.*
*The space was tight, confined. This had been Rowan’s intent in choosing this battleground. Somewhere more open might allow room for manoeuvring. And while Rowan prided himself on his quickness with a blade, against Torlene it would have been a disadvantage.*
*When Torlene reached a proper distance from Rowan, he stopped in place and removed segments of his robe. Everything decorative was thrown to the side. He even scrunched his flowing hair into a close bun behind his head.*
*When it was done, Torlene was left nearly naked. He wore only ceremonial short pants that stopped at his knees. His elbows were padded by leather guards with a similar pair strapped to his knees.*
*…And in his hands, he bore his trademark jagged elven blade. Its shape was like a lightning bolt.*
*The elven warrior adopted a fighting stance. His sword hung menacingly over head, his knees bent into a near crouching. It was a ready stance, like a snake coiled up and ready to pounce. His form swayed back and forth rhythmically, as though he were dancing. *
Torlene: "It is good that there are witnesses. All the better. They will see your end, Thief. Liurial will be mine today."
*Trash talk him.*
Rowan: "I wonder what your men will think after I’m done with you. Will they weep and rage and gnash their teeth? I wonder if they’ll think you died honourab-"
Torlene: "Enough. I will silence that roguish tongue of yours."
*Rowan grinned.*
Rowan: "You won’t do it by talking."
*Remain silent.*
*Rowan had passed the need for words by this point. He simply raised a hand and beckoned the elf to approach.*
Torlene: "There is still a path for you to escape your fate, Rowan. Surrender the girl to me, and none of this need happen. We would both walk away, honour intact."
Torlene: "You needn’t do this on her behalf. She will be happy in my custody. It is in her best interest as well."
*Answer him.*
*Rowan shook his head softly.*
Rowan: "You’re misguided, Torlene. You don’t understand the words you’re saying."
Torlene: "..."
Torlene: "So be it. When this day is spoken of, they will not say I was eager for it."
*Remain silent.*
*Rowan had passed the need for words by this point. He simply raised a hand and beckoned the elf to approach.*
*The wind’s howling grew to a shrill screech. Its scream echoed across the vast chasm that awaited either if they fell over the side. For some reason, to Rowan, it almost sounded like a woman’s cry.*
*Rowan closed his eyes and inhaled. Then, he struck. *
*Rowan’s first blow was a noncommittal test to see how his foe would react. But, Torlene was not in the mood for a slow start. He strongly deflected Rowan’s strike, then broke into a flying charge. His sword shot out in a smooth jab towards Rowan’s head.*
*Rowan went careening backward, keeping his footing steady. It paid off: Torlene’s first strike was revealed as a feint, fast turning into a ducking swipe, followed by a second swipe from the same angle. Were he any closer, it might have chopped off Rowan’s leg at the ankle.*
Torlene: "Last time, you experienced my technique when I was off-centre. Off balance. Today, you will see the techniques of a true artist."
Torlene: "-And then you will see no more."
*The two broke off, swords out to enforce distance. Rowan’s longer wingspan kept Torlene at a farther backstep.*
Torlene: "You chose a foolish place for our encounter. I was born on the side of Mount Karjilo. The wind is my friend and the elevation elicits no fear from me. To think that-"
Rowan: "I told you before. You won’t kill me by talking."
Rowan: "Talk less."
Rowan: "I came to fight, not to talk. I don’t need a speech."
*Torlene kept himself in a half-crouch, advancing slowly. His blade whirled in tight circles, sending jabs towards Rowan at a dizzying speed. It was through skill alone that Torlene was able to do so while keeping his stance centered, rarely opening even the smallest of holes in his guard.*
*But Rowan was no novice either. Where Torlene was an acrobatic wonder, he was cold practicality. Rowan kept his posture, moving minimally to match each strike, but conserving as much energy as possible.*
*To an outside observer, such flourishing strikes might be impressive... but to Rowan, they seemed a waste of energy.*
*Rowan slowly fell backwards, trying to manoeuvre his own far larger blade to meet each biting strike. The elf’s speed left him constantly in a state of reaction, unable to retake the initiative. Nevertheless, his guard held.*
*By now, Rowan had already retreated some distance, far enough that his footing had deteriorated. As he ducked a leaping strike, he recalled the elf’s feint-heavy style from their prior bout. There would be a follow-up…*
*It came, almost at the exact moment Rowan expected. A low, flourished strike, pivoting into a leg sweep. Rowan was ready for it—what he wasn’t ready for was when the sweep transitioned into a flying knee, mid motion.*
*Rowan’s body reacted faster than his mind could. As Torlene had closed in on Rowan, he’d opened his own guard. Before the elf’s knee could land the hit, Rowan’s off-hand went flying into the elf’s face, striking a savage blow that sent Torlene reeling.*
Torlene: "urgh!"
*Rowan nearly stumbled back, but he managed to move back into a guard stance. Torlene danced backwards, clutching his jaw.*
*The brief respite didn’t last long. In moments, Torlene was advancing again, raining jabs and feints in recompense.*
*The blow struck Rowan, right in the centre of his abdomen, setting all of his nerves alight. Rowan only barely raised his sword in time to catch the swing that had been meant as a follow-up.*
Torlene: "What’s wrong, human? Not fast enough?"
*Rowan only just managed to retake his guard before the next barrage of jabs came flying at him.*
*Behind him, Rowan heard distances shouting and calling out to him. He tried to keep his focus exclusively on the fight, but some he managed to recognize.*
Andras: "Kick his ass! Make him bleed!!"
Andras: "Get in there! The fuck are you standing around for!?"
Andras: "Hit him! Hit him you piece of shit!"
Rowan: "Rowan! Be Careful!"
*All the while, Rowan grew more familiar with his foe. Weak spinning jabs to disorient, sudden shifts in centre of gravity, mixup using elbows and knees. To a lesser fighter, it might have come across as an incomprehensible storm. But, Rowan’s golden virtue as a warrior was pattern recognition.*
*So, this time, even as Torlene was keeping him distracted with another frantic flurry of blows, Rowan kept his attention on Torlene’s back leg. He was hungry for an opening.*
*He waited until he saw a low crouch, almost like a spring ready to be unleashed. That meant a jumping strike.*
*Torlene lunged forward… only to be met by Rowan, mid-swing. He put all his strength into his arms, aiming to overpower his weaker foe.*
*Such a blow might have been a killing strike to another fighter. Even having caught on to the attack, Torlene’s position left him few options. He only just managed to put his blade between his body and Rowan’s sword, but the ringing force of the blow still slammed him into the railing.*
*But Rowan was too slow, if only by a hair. Torlene managed to catch himself, reversing his momentum backwards. He sailed out of the reach of Rowan’s blade, but his off balance dodge sent him crashing with great force into the railing.*
*The structure let out a sickening creak. Then, all at once, a whole segment of railing collapsed away. Torlene only managed to throw himself back on safer footing before taking a deadly plunge. Up and down the battlefield, stone went plunging away into the dark depths below.*
Rowan: "If he doesn’t kill me, Skordred’s going to…"
*There was a brief lull in the fighting as the two struggled to catch their breath. They circled each other as much as the constrained space would allow, each trying to manoeuvre their foe into a position with their back to the hazardous gap in the wall.*
Torlene: "You may still yield, Blackwell. Drop your sword and kneel. You have shown your mettle. But, your death cannot keep the girl from me."
Rowan: "Are you still talking? Fight me, asshole."
Rowan: "Are you still talking? Fight me."
Torlene: "..."
Torlene: "Die."
*For all Rowan’s skill, he could not match the precise movements of a master of the elven fighting arts. Each time the hero tried to place himself closer to the wall, Torlene used jabs and footwork to push Rowan back.*
*The situation increasingly grew dire. Rowan’s back foot was teetering on the edge of the abyss, with Torlene closing in. One bad step could send Rowan falling to his death. A risk Torlene exploited with a sudden, aggressive advance.*
*It was just what Rowan wanted him to do. At the very last moment, he ducked to the side, trying to give Torlene a shove off the side.*
*It was a clever ploy. And one that nearly worked. But the falling elf managed to grapple with Rowan’s arm. The result sent them both tumbling to the ground at the edge of the precipice.*
*As bad as his position was, Rowan managed to gird himself just in time. The force of the clash sent Rowan stumbling backwards, but not far enough back to fall off the edge. What’s more, Rowan’s unexpected resilience had thrown off Torlene’s momentum.*
*Torlene went tumbling to the ground, right on top of him. The yawning call of the edge threatened them both.*
Alexia: "Rowan!!!!!"
*Rowan could hear his wife’s voice crying out to him in the distance. But, he was too focused on survival to truly pay her mind.*
*Both their swords had clattered out of reach, forcing them to trade unarmed blows. Punches, kicks, and grapples. Such a fight could never be to Rowan’s advantage. Torlene managed to position himself on top, raining brutal elbow blows to Rowan’s head.*
Rowan: "Unff!"
*He scrambled to protect his head and face. He needed to act. Now.*
*He waited till Torlene grew comfortable enough administering his beating to lower his guard. Then, Rowan used the main advantage he had over his foe: raw strength.*
*Rowan reached out, catching one of the elf’s elbows mid-strike. Torlene tried to wrench himself away, but couldn’t slip his way out. Rowan’s grip was vicelike.*
*He saw Torlene’s eyes widen slightly. Rowan let out a great heave, attempting to shove Torlene over the edge. In his desperation, Torlene wrenched backwards. But, Rowan followed, landing a sloppy right hook across Torlene’s nose.*
*But, Torlene was ever the agile fighter. Despite Rowan’s success, he managed to roll out of Rowan’s grasp.*
*Both combatants breathing heavily, there was no attempt by either side to prevent the other from collecting his weapon. They rose to their feet, swords facing each other once again. And so the duel raged on.*
*In his desperation, under pounding assault, Rowan had to do something, anything, to survive.*
*So he took the gamble. He reached up, grabbing Torlene’s wrists as he stuck him. With them in his grip, he surged upwards, head first.*
*His desperate, sloppy headbutt struck Torlene square in the nose. Blood spattered on the stone beneath. Both his and Torlene’s.*
*That broke the grapple. Both fighters stumbled backwards, scrambling to reach  their weapons and returning to their feet.*
*A clash of this ferocity could only go on for so long. Battered and bruised from the multiple blows Rowan had gotten past his guard, Torlene was now less than half the fighter he had been at the start.*
*Because of his broken nose, his eyes were blocked by tears and blood. A nasty gash on his left leg made his acrobatic style of combat nearly impossible. Sheer exhaustion had dulled the speed and dexterity of his strikes.*
*Meanwhile, Rowan was winded, but he was still in pristine condition compared to his opponent. Where Torlene had fought with flashy acrobatics, Rowan had fought with economy of movement.*
*Torlene kept attempting - now desperately - to land low strikes at Rowan’s legs. Rowan had previously noticed Torlene’s propensity to follow his first strike with a second immediately.*
*Earlier, it had caught Rowan off guard. But, now he was the one with the advantage in speed and stamina. He was more than ready to punish such tactics.*
*Knowing he had the victory, the patient hero waited for Torlene to advance. The elf’s fighting style demanded a kind of aggression even if his body was no longer fully capable of it.*
*The morning sun gleamed off of Torlene’s blade as he launched into a final telegraphed charge.*
*The air rang with a clash of steel. After a brief exchange, Torlene fell backwards, his shoulder penetrated by the end of Rowan’s blade. His own jagged sword slipped out of his hand through blood-slick fingers.*
Torlene: "Tsh..."
*A battle of this intensity could only go on for so long. The two warriors had fought themselves to exhaustion. Open cuts lined their bodies where they’d been struck in close combat. Rowan’s hands trembled in the effort of holding his sword aloft.*
*Yet, as grim as the contest was, this was a dynamic that favoured Rowan. The human’s conservative fighting style let him keep his energy, only moving dramatically when forced to shift his footing.*
*Meanwhile, Torlene’s entire strategy was predicated on speed, swiftness, and aggression. All of which were liabilities in a long fight. His once controlled spins and swings grew slower and more imprecise.*
*Seeming to sense this, the Honoured Blade attempted one final jump strike. It had been intended as a mix-up from a swinging low blow, but he hesitated for a fraction of a second in the transition.*
*A fraction of a second too long. Rowan’s mighty swing came down on him with all the weight of a thunderclap.*
*It was a mercy that Torlene was not cut in half. He had just enough remaining reflexes to divert his sword in the way of Rowan’s. However, there was not enough strength in the gesture to properly deflect the strike.*
*Clang. The sickening sound of a sword smashing into another rose above the gale of wind.*
*The elf was sent reeling. His back smashed into a surviving segment of railing before the force of the collision sent him collapsing to the ground.*
*Torlene’s prized jagged blade went flying from his hand. Before he could try to retrieve it, Rowan’s blade was at his neck.*
*Torlene’s eyes said it all. Wide and desperate, with tears and blood streaming down his face.*
Torlene: "End this…"
*Rowan panted for breath. Now that Torlene was defeated and at his mercy, he called to mind the terms of the duel. There were two ways he could win. Surrender or Death.*
Torlene: "Human… you won. End this…"
*Rowan still remembered the command that Jezera had given him. She wanted him humiliated for making things difficult for her. Now that he had Torlene at his mercy, he could obey that order if that was what he truly wished.*
*Rowan inhaled sharply. Then, he...*
*…Spared Torlene.*
*…Stopped. Even as his foe was pleading for Rowan to kill him, he remained in place. After a few contemplative seconds, Rowan let his blade fall to his side.*
Torlene: "I will not yield, Human. Do it!"
*When Torlene spoke, Rowan could see the blood upon his lips. He spat some out with every word. There was desperation in his eyes, something far more fearful was at risk here than his life: the death of his honour.*
*Rowan, moved either by pity or spite, still did not give him the death that he demanded.*
*Torlene’s eyes turned to look at something behind Rowan’s shoulder. He let out a piteous groan. Rowan hesitated to look, worrying that it might be some final trick to get the upper hand.*
Liurial: "Rowan!"
*That got his attention. Rowan turned his head slightly, keeping Torlene in his peripheral vision. Liurial had pushed her way in front of the orcs and had come running towards the area of the fight. His breath came out shakier than he’d intended.*
Rowan: "L-Liurial. Wait…"
*For once, the elf girl didn’t obey a direct order. Instead, she drew close to him. Torlene groaned, shifting his glance between Rowan and the newcomer.*
Liurial: "Rowan… What are you going to do? Are you…"
*Rowan gave her a weak smile.*
Rowan: "I’m not going to kill him."
*With aching arms that screamed for rest, Rowan returned his sword to his scabbard.*
Torlene: "What are you… doing, you fool!? I haven’t yielded."
Rowan: "I don’t care. This is over. If you don’t yield, it would be no different from suicide. There’s no honour in that."
*He gestured towards Liurial. The girl had pressed herself close to his side, clutching him for support.*
Rowan: "And for what, Torlene? For what? I’ve told you half a hundred times. Liurial came to me of her own free will. Your death would be more meaningless than this contest."
Torlene: "You… you… took her from me…"
*His voice was something akin to a croak now. Broken and strained with pain.*
*Rowan was set to answer him when Liurial gave him a look. She was pleading with him to let her speak. Exhausted as he was, Rowan was more than happy to let her.*
*Liurial bent low, placing a gentle hand on Torlene’s arm. Reflexively, he shied away from her touch.*
Liurial: "Torlene… Old friend… What have you done to yourself?"
Liurial: "..."
*Rowan’s fallen foe worked himself back up into a seated position. Liurial knelt down at his side. And put her hands on his wounds. Torlene recoiled from the touch, but Liurial was insistent.*
*Rowan also examined Torlene’s condition. He was certainly battered and bloodied, but most soldiers Rowan had seen who took similar levels of pain survived with proper rest and treatment.*
*Liurial scurried over to Torlene’s discarded clothes and tore off a scrap. When she returned, she applied it to the largest of Torlene’s wounds. Again, Torlene tried to protest, But, Liurial clicked her tongue until he stopped.*
Torlene: "I told you, girl. I haven’t yielded!"
Liurial: "I’m not your girl anymore. Don’t call me that."
*She inhaled sharply, then looked at him with renewed determination.*
Liurial: "Deep down, I always knew it would be your downfall…Every mistake, every failure. I saw the same root in it all. But, I was never…never able to express it."
Liurial: "Finnigold was your father…and you worshipped him for it. Just as he was my keeper and I worshipped him for it. And I think…"
Liurial: "..I think that’s why…when he was gone, we stayed together…You took me in because He would have taken me in. I was precious to you because I was precious to Him."
Liurial: "…you were just like I was. You were lost the whole time. I was lost…and you were lost too."
*She sighed and resumed working on his bandages. Where there was an open wound, Liurial tried to use some of the cloth to stop the bleeding. Torlene still regarded her with annoyed anger but had given up trying to stop her.*
Liurial: "You’re not Finnigold, Torlene."
*She shook her head forcefully.*
Liurial: "Can’t you see, old friend? Here you are bleeding out…begging for…for, you know…just because you couldn’t win a fight you didn’t need to fight."
Liurial: "Why?"
Torlene: "For you…"
*She shook her head forcefully, pressing down hard on the cloth to help stop the gash across his leg.*
Liurial: "Not for me…Torlene. Not for me…For the honour of a man who's gone. To protect the possession of a man who can’t posses anything anymore…"
Torlene: "For you…he stole you…"
*Liurial shook her head again.*
Liurial: "I left. Even before I met him, I left you."
Liurial: "I knew I would have to for a long time. I just didn’t…didn’t admit it to myself. Because the things that came so easy to him when it came to me were so hard for you. …you would get so angry about it…"
Liurial: "And when you got angry…you hurt me."
*Torlene jerked his head away, refusing to face her.*
Torlene: "You were… you were precious to me, I would never…."
*Rowan squatted down so he could rest a hand on Liurial’s shoulder. He could see the tears rolling down her cheek. This was not an easy task that she had given herself. But, Rowan could not interfere.*
Liurial: "And look where that anger took you, Torlene. It destroyed us…and now it’s destroying you. Refusing to yield, even when it would save your life. All to meet your end here…so far away from home."
Liurial: "Don’t do this…Old friend…don’t die for me. I was never what you wanted."
*Whatever strength was left in Torlene’s body failed him. From the way he was slumped over, Rowan was rightfully afraid he might have died. When the power of speech returned to Torlene, it was in a soft tone, devoid of all his power and dignity.*
Torlene: "Liurial. You-"
Torlene: "You-"
*Liurial placed her hands on Rowan’s side, gripping him for support.*
Torlene: "...So he spoke true then...You came to him purposefully…and he had no hand in it…"
Torlene: "...And the true cause…is that you pity and fear me…"
Liurial: "Torlene…"
*The elf slowly came back to life. He used whatever strength he had left to bring himself up into a fully seated position. When he raised his head, it was too Rowan he looked.*
Torlene: "Rowan Blackwell. I yield."
Torlene: "Sir Rowan Blackwell. I yield."
*Rowan rose to his feet once again, extending a hand down to Liurial. But, she continued to care for Torlene until Galabraith had come running to his defeated commander’s side.*
*Only once he’d taken over holding the cloth did Liurial relent and return to her feet. But, not before sharing a brief friendly smile with the hulking elf. *
*Rowan led Liurial back, giving Torlene space. Liurial cried and clutched his side for support. Together, they returned to where Andras was waiting.*
*Rowan led Liurial back, giving Torlene space. Liurial cried and clutched his side for support. Though, truthfully, Rowan might have needed her help standing more than she needed his. Together, they returned to where Andras was waiting.*
*…Humiliated Torlene.*
*...clenched his free hand into a fist. This was the price he had to pay. Jezera’s approval rested on Torlene’s humiliation. Her will would be done.*
*…clenched his free hand into a fist. Torlene had been the instigator of this entire ordeal. The man’s senseless entitlement had not only threatened Rowan’s safety, but that of Alexia and Liurial. Now Rowan had Torlene at his mercy.*
Rowan: "No."
Torlene: "Wha-"
Rowan: "You want me to give you an honourable death? Well, too bad."
*Rowan bent low. His face hung close enough to Torlene’s to glare into his eyes. His defeated foe’s pupils were frantic with pain.*
Rowan: "You did this. At every step, you could have walked away. But you never got it through your thick skull."
*He jabbed a finger into Torlene’s forehead.*
Rowan: "The girl doesn’t want you anymore. How blind are you that you can’t see it? She chose me over you. How did you think you could get her back with just a treaty and a tantrum?"
*Rowan returned to his feet. It cast a dark shadow over his fallen opponent.*
Rowan: "-Or did you go through all this for honour? It doesn’t matter if she actually wants you. According to your code, she belonged to you."
Rowan: "I see what you are. Everyone sees what you are: an entitled child. A fool who ran headfirst into a fight he couldn’t win; all for the sake of your worthless honour."
*Rowan spat on the ground next to Torlene. The elf couldn’t help but recoil slightly, expecting another blow. It was a pitiful sight.*
*Rowan paused. His chest rose and fell rapidly. There was something about having Torlene in this position that offered an intoxicating sense of power. He knew it was wrong, but the more he belittled his fallen foe, the better he felt. *
*Rowan paused. His chest rose and fell rapidly. Already the first pangs of guilt were beginning to hit him. He’d never treat a defeated foe like this normally. Even one as deserving as Torlene.*
*But, playing the part was easier if he let himself rage. So he suppressed that reaction as best as he could and simply let himself ride the anger.*
*His eyes caught the glimmer of Torlene’s sword, fallen nearby. Rowan paced over to it, his fingers closing gently around the intricate, decorative hilt. After examining the blade for a brief moment - turning it this way and that in the sunlight -  he tossed it over the edge.*
Torlene: "My…"
Rowan: "This is what I think of you, Torlene. This is what I think of your ‘honour.’"
Rowan: "Stay away from Liurial. Don’t ever try to speak to her again. Don’t ever try to “strike a deal for her with me again, either."
Rowan: "And if you even think about trying to go behind my back again… I will give you a death that will have no glory. A painful, slow end. You will beg me to stop the pain. So if anyone even remembers you, all they will think of is the shameful way you died."
Rowan: "And if you even think about trying to go behind my back again… I will give you a death that will have no glory. A painful, slow end. So if anyone even remembers you, all they will think of is the shameful way you died."
*Rowan punctuated the point with a cruel kick to the stomach. Torlene curled up in pain. *
Liurial: "Rowan?"
*Rowan turned around. Liurial was standing in front of the crowd of spectators, hands held in a prayer gesture. Her eyes trialed Torlene and Rowan with horror.*
*He felt a knot in the pit of his stomach. She wasn’t supposed to see that.*
*He felt a knot in the pit of his stomach. She wasn’t supposed to see that. No one was supposed to see that.*
Rowan: "I-"
*Had he made a huge mistake? Surely she was over Torlene, but that didn’t mean she necessarily wanted to see him treated this way.*
Liurial: "Old friend…"
*But, Rowan could only get so distracted while the fight was still technically going. He sensed movement and turned to ensure the battered elf was not making some futile attempt against him.*
*Instead, he found him crawling along the ground towards Liurial. Tears mixed with blood as they streamed down his face.*
Torlene: "Liurial…don’t…don’t look...at me like this…"
*Liurial closed her eyes and inhaled. When she opened them again, they shone with a determination Rowan had never seen from her.*
Liurial: "No."
*She shook her head firmly.*
Liurial: "Rowan is right, Torlene. You need to stay away from me now. Forever."
Torlene: "Liurial…"
*Torlene stopped advancing towards her. The strength left him.*
*Rowan thought he saw the start of tears budding in Liurial’s eyes. But, rather than express that as any sympathy for Torlene, she forcefully turned her back. It deprived her former protector, who had just suffered so much for her, of a chance to look at her face.*
Torlene: "..."
