Jezera: "Oh, and don't worry about the day to day operations, we still want you to be our eyes and ears in the world. Your job will be to figure out the big picture."
Jezera: "That includes choosing how to spend our funds and where we should direct our research.  I suppose that would make you our steward."
*Jezera came to a stop in front of an odd pair; a dark dwarf man and a goblin woman.*
*The dwarf had a regal air about him, with his elaborate gold plated clothing, but his appearance was very typical of his race. Rowan noticed right away that the dark man did not like him, his tense stance and glare of disdain was very evident.*
*The goblin woman on the other hand was all smiles. She had the look of a caravan merchant and gave off a practised sense of trying to make herself seem like she was your best friend and had the perfect item that would solve all your problems.*
Jezera: "May I present to you Skordred and Cla-Min."
Jezera: "You two, this is your new boss, the hero Rowan."
*The dwarf, Skordred, spat on the floor as Jezera spoke Rowan's name. On the other hand, the goblin Cla-Min bowed deeply. Jezera ignored their actions.*
Jezera: "Skordred is a dark dwarven master builder, a status that the one who built the first Castle Bloodmeen also held, and lead the team that rebuilt it for Karnas."
Jezera: "He has agreed to resume his old post in service to my brother and I, and will oversee any construction projects you allocate funds for."
Skordred: "Listen, 'hero', I don't want to talk to you more than I have to.  Even if you serve the new masters now, you're part of the group that killed the old master.  I haven't forgiven you for that grave sin."
Jezera: "Not particularly friendly, but like our mother, he is strongly drawn to the darkness. I don't doubt his loyalty in the least."
*Seemingly unable to contain herself any longer, the goblin woman jumped forward and started shaking Rowan's hand vigorously.*
Cla-min: "Tis an honor to finally meet the great master schemer Rowan! A great goblin in human flesh!"
*After a moment Rowan realized with some alarm that the green woman was genuinely fawning over him!*
Cla-min: "There have been so many stories of the great things you've done during the war, of sabotage and trickery! No cheating magic, no big man strength, just honest slinking and stinking."
Cla-min: "It'll be a real honor working under you... or over you if that's your preference."
Cla-min: " To be honest, I prefer being on top myself, but I've got lots of girls in the family who like taking it in all sorts of ways and-"
Jezera: "That's enough. Give the man some space."
*Much to Rowan's relief, the openly affectionate goblin woman stepped back then bowed to him again.*
Jezera: "Cla-Min is the head of a goblin merchant caravan. She's agreed to provide us with the supplies and materials we will need in exchange for access to my portal network. If you need to upgrade your equipment or acquire adventuring gear, she's your woman."
*The short stack posed proudly and winked at the hero. Then she hesitated and seemed to be struck by a sudden inspiration.*
Cla-min: "We've got lots of boys in the family too if you don't go for ladies. I'm sure we can work out-"
Jezera: "Min!"
Cla-min: "Sorry."
*Shaking her head in dismay, Jezera lead Rowan away from the merchant towards the stairs down to the underground section of the castle.*
Rowan: "That was... an interesting experience."
Jezera: "I'd assumed that Skordred would give you the cold shoulder, but Min's over exuberance was wholly unexpected.  Had you ever heard of goblins idolizing you?"
Rowan: "I'd heard a rumor about it once, but I'd discounted it long ago."
*The two of them found Andras in what appeared to be a barracks complex, watching orc soldiers perform training drills. Upon noticing the approaching pair, the red demon's expression soured considerably.*
Andras: "Ah, sister, and servant. Time for the inspection then?"
Jezera: "Dear brother, are you such a sore loser that you can't even manage common courtesies?"
*Andras only growled in response then waved the blue skinned woman off and indicated for Rowan to stay. Jezera waited a moment to see if her brother would say anything else before shrugging and leaving her charge behind.*
Andras: "This is our current military facility. Skordred hasn't had enough resources to get more than an orc barracks up and running out of the ruins of the old underground."
*He went on to explain in detail their current ability to support forces and his recruitment efforts.  Rowan took a tour of the area afterwards and sparred briefly with some of the soldiers.*
*Afterwards he had a very good idea of the current military capacity of the castle.*
*And all that he'd learned suggested that the state of things was not good.*
*At maximum capacity the current facilities couldn't do much more than occupy a handful of villages, and they wouldn't be able to hold them against a major counter attack.*
*On top of that, Andras's current recruitment prospects would take months to fill the barracks.*
*It would take a lot of improvements to the facilities and dramatically increased recruiting to conquer a single one of the six realms, let alone all of them.*
Jezera: "Now that you know what our capabilities are, it's time to learn what me and my brother expect of you in the coming months."
*The three of them were back in the throne room, now with Jezera sitting on the throne and Andras standing at her side.*
Jezera: "Firstly we want you to raise a force powerful enough to take Raeve keep in Rosaria, nearby my portal. This will end the baron's rule in the area and create a foothold for further conquests."
Jezera: "If you can somehow sway the duke to our cause or take control of the keep through delectable subterfuge, that will satisfy us as well."
*The demoness obviously liked the idea of taking over from the shadows. Her brother snorted, clearly he'd prefer the more direct route over the alternatives that his sister had suggested.*
Jezera: "In addition, bring up our overall military capacity to that of a proper army and raise our treasury to contain at least 500 gold crowns. Complete these tasks in six months."
Jezera: "Succeed and you shall earn many rewards."
Andras: "Fail, and you will suffer greatly, Alexia as well."
Jezera: "Good luck, my hero."
Jezera: "With that formality out of the way, the treasury is at your disposal for your first construction projects. Skordred will tell you about what projects are available. We will also start paying you a weekly salary for your work out of the treasury."
Andras: "I would advise against spending that money frivolously. It's what you'll be buying your personal equipment with."
Rowan: "So I'm to work with what I have in your service? I guess Cla-Min will have to live with not seeing me as a customer for a few weeks to come."
Jezera: "Well, if she has something that will help you in our service, perhaps I can be convinced to divert some of our construction funds as a stipend for you to purchase equipment? That is, as long as you don't mind me keeping some of it for my own schemes."
Rowan: "I'll think about it."
Andras: "Then talk to our servants and return when you've come to your decision."
*Rowan knocked on the door to Skordred's workshop.*
*A moment later, the dwarf arrived with a glare in his eyes.*
Rowan: "Let me see your current construction options."
*Evidently the dwarf had expected this, and he handed Rowan a clipboard with three diagrams on it, along with short descriptions of each. They'd probably been prepared for the twins, but now Rowan was the one to receive them.*
*The builder was not happy about this.*
Rowan: "(My options are, a forge, a dark sanctum, or a tavern.)"
Rowan: "(The forge would dramatically improve the power of our soldiers. The dark sanctum would give us another type of soldier and improve our ability to do research, helping in the long term. The tavern would increase the income for our treasury.)"
*Still holding onto the clipboard, Rowan left the workshop behind and headed towards the wagon parked a ways outside the castle's main gate.*
*The goblin woman was much friendlier, eager to show off what goods she had available. Some of her enthusiasm faded when she found out that Rowan didn't have the money on him to buy much yet, but kept at it out of her strange adoration.*
*Cla-Min had a small selection of arms available; nothing fancy, but always useful for anyone in the adventuring profession.*
Rowan: "(Well, time to come to my decision.  Should I start one of the construction projects or give up some of the treasury for a stipend to buy equipment with?)"
*Discuss construction with Skordred*
*Forge*:
Andras: "Excellent. Having proper gear should make my orcs actually somewhat decent in battle. I already have someone in mind to serve as forgemaster. I'll have him in by the time Skordred is finished building the forge."
*Dark Sanctum*:
Jezera: "I'm glad we're going to finally get sorcerers around here, they'll be able to give Cliohna a hand. Hmm, I'll have to see about getting someone to keep the succubi and incubi in line."
*Tavern*:
Jezera: "The earlier we build our income, the faster we will be able to build everything else. I do hope you put the intelligence we get to good use as well. You're going to be playing catch up when it comes to building our armies."
Jezera: "The final decision you'll have to make today is how you want to direct our librarian's research. I understand she's ready to start at anytime, so please pay her a visit right away."
*Rowan entered into the great library of Castle Bloodmeen.*
Rowan: "Never was one for books, I do remember how ecstatic Loralyn was when she first stepped in here."
*He skimmed the aisles, looking for the librarian. There'd been several sorcerers in Karnas's armies that worked in here during the war, but Rowan couldn't remember anyone being known as 'the librarian'.*
*Whoever she was, she wasn't one of the old guard like Skordred.*
*Then the hero found her, standing at a lectern in one of the alcoves. She looked very young, either in the end of her teens or barely out of them by Rowan's guess.*
*Long blond hair ran down her back and she wore very revealing clothing that barely covered her body.*
*The woman appeared to be deeply engrossed in the rather large tome she was currently reading. A stack of similarly sized books rested nearby with a magical staff propped against them.*
Rowan: "So, you're the librarian?"
*As Rowan spoke, she carefully closed the book and turned to face him. Instantly the hero realized that he'd been wrong about her age; the eyes gave it away. They were not the innocent eyes of a girl, but instead ancient and filled with cynicism.*
Cliohna: "Cliohna, and you must be Rowan. I have prepared a list of topics that I can focus my research on, please select the one you think will be best to begin with."
*She took a sheet of parchment off of the lectern and handed it to Rowan. He accepted it and did a quick skim of the topics outlined.*
Rowan: "Okay, I can understand why we'd need to work on diplomacy or set up a contact network for research, but why exactly do you have exploration techniques and history of the war on here?"
Rowan: "I probably know more about the war than most, and have plenty of scouting experience."
Cliohna: "Ah, but how much do you know about how the world has been reshaped after the war? Have you worked with charting courses for armies or have you been trained in the use of cartography and surveying equipment?"
Rowan: "Uh..."
Cliohna: "I could go to great lengths to explain why each and every one of these items will be of great use to the twins and your service to them."
Rowan: "No, I think that's fine."
Cliohna: "Good, I'll keep it short then. Any of these are perfectly fine to start with, the main thing that will be important from here on out is that you don't focus your efforts too hard in any one category."
Cliohna: "After all, having great soldiers and knowledge of tactics will not be useful if you don't have the diplomatic skills to recruit new armies to your cause."
Cliohna: "The expertise to train and breed monsters will not go far if you haven't the skill to find their nests in the first place."
Cliohna: "Now, lord Rowan, let me know when you have made your choice."
Cliohna: "Very well. I will begin my work and submit a report when I've finished."
*Evidently this was the end of the conversation. Cliohna turned back around and selected a different tome from the stack. With a wave of her hand, it floated out of the pile and settled itself onto the lectern as the old book took its old place in the pile.*
*Rowan simply shook his head and said goodbye before taking his leave. That woman did seem to be human, but he was certain that she was a lot older than she seemed.*
*The power he felt radiating from her must have been similar to Loralyn, who herself was one of the most skilled of the remaining elven mages.*
*He returned to the throne room.*
Andras: "It seems that concludes your duties, for now."
Jezera: "Are there any question you have about the castle?"
Rowan: "I'm curious, where did you find Cliohna? I can tell she's a powerful magic user, an ancient one at that, but I've never heard of her. Even most of the elves only live for a couple centuries, but she seems even older than that."
*The blue skinned demoness only smiled.*
Jezera: "I don't know where Cliohna is from.  She approached us, not the other way around. The deal is, she gets full access to the library in exchange for doing our research. That's the extent of our relationship."
Jezera: "At any rate, it is getting late and you should get to bed soon. We're sending you out to explore again in the morning after all."
*A servant burst into Rowan’s office mere minutes ago, pale faced and terrified. Through a shaking voice she recounted what had happened.*
*Passing by the room of one of the Fae Ambassadors, she said she heard snarling, and the sound of loud crashing and thumping that shook the walls themselves.*
*The roaring had only grown louder as she ran from the site. She said the stone rattled with the sounds of its roars. The rest of the staff were terrified to go into that wing of the castle.*
*Now, standing just outside Whitescar’s room, Rowan could hear that loud crashing, the heavy sound of growling drifting in from the other side of the door like a rumble in his chest.*
*His hand hesitated on the doorknob. For a brief moment Rowan was struck with a queasy, preylike sensation.*
*But he had a task to do, so he set aside his scruples and pushed open the door.*
*The room had been torn to pieces. Barely anything was recognizable: shattered bits of furniture coated in ripped sheeting run through with claws.*
*The armoire had been toppled over onto the bed as if thrown with great force. Shards of wood stuck up out of the cracked interior like stakes from the sheer force of its breaking.*
*Rowan surveyed the damage. Nothing had been left untouched, the room was now a corrugated maze of dust and debris.*
*And there, in the center of the destruction, loomed the great white beast who had so boldly walked through the portal to face down the Twins alone.*
*A Fae, a real Fae from the stories, prowling the narrow space with a look on his face that promised violence. The air stank of his scent: an earthy, masculine aura of predatory intent. *
*Evidently he’d gotten tired of waiting.*
Whitescar: "Grrh. Useless finery."
Rowan: "Is the room not to your liking, Ambassador?"
*The Wolf paused in his hectic pacing, his head snapping over to look straight at Rowan. The two stared each other down.*
Whitescar: "A cramped cave, bloated with mortal luxuries. I struggle to imagine a less likable place."
Rowan: "The idea was for you to be comfortable."
Whitescar: "Fae were not born to be comfortable. We were born to hunt, to sleep beneath the open sky."
Whitescar: "I’d prefer a grove of rotted elms to this… confinement."
Rowan: "You are, of course, free to leave the castle at any point if you’d prefer, Ambassador."
*Whitescar let out a low rumbling sound deep in his throat, which Rowan interpreted as a gruff chuckle.*
Whitescar: "So... you have come."
Rowan: "I have. On behalf of the Twins, I welcome you to Castle Bloodmee-"
Whitescar: "Stop. Flattery tires me, human."
Whitescar: "Empty words are a waste of air, forced platitudes even moreso."
Rowan: "I only meant it as a sign of respect."
Whitescar: "Respect is earned through action, not seduced through frivolous boot-licking."
*To Rowan’s surprise, the beast smiled, pulling back his lips to expose the long line of his fangs.*
Whitescar: "...I did not expect you to speak up in my defense in the Throne Room."
Rowan: "I was only trying to defuse the situation."
Whitescar: "You did well. I was in the wrong. One does not enter another’s den to make demands, no matter how foolish they may be."
Rowan: "Well don’t get too comfortable with yourself. Jezera and Andras aren’t likely to change their minds on the matter."
Whitescar: "Yes. That much is clear. Hence my abandonment in this room."
Rowan: "If you know, then why stay?"
*The Fae fell silent. He turned his back to Rowan, his long tail twirling pensively in slow circles.*
Whitescar: "A good question. If we are doomed to fail, then why the prohibition on returning?"
Whitescar: "Is this a test? Does she seek to teach us a lesson?"
Whitescar: "...Hmmh. No. That heathen witch would never agree to it."
Whitescar: "A punishment, then? Have I angered her?"
*Whitescar put a thoughtful claw to his chin, letting out a dissatisfied grunt.*
Rowan: "Angered who?"
*Whitescar’s slitted eyes refocused on Rowan again. A nervous thrill ran up his spine.*
Whitescar: "Our Queen is mercurial, she likes to speak in riddles. Often she has a hidden agenda, concealed in mundane matters."
Whitescar: "I have no purpose here. It is a waste of my time, and yet... I must linger."
*As if connecting two thoughts together, the wolf’s gaze sharpened. He loomed over Rowan with a sudden, terrifying presence.*
Whitescar: "You are curious to me, human."
Rowan: "Why is that?"
Whitescar: "You seemed surprised when I arrived through the portal."
*Rowan affected a careless shrug.*
Rowan: "Of course I was. Most mortals were raised to think your people are merely fairy tales."
Rowan: "To see you appear, in the flesh, right in front of me… it was quite shocking."
*The Fae fixed him with a dark look. A low growl emitted from his throat.*
Whitescar: "I said surprised, not shocked."
Whitescar: "You were expecting me, just not at that moment."
Rowan: "I don’t follow your meaning."
Whitescar: "Yes. You do."
Whitescar: "You cloud your words, but I hear it. There is a waver in your tone. You don’t speak with conviction."
Whitescar: "You knew I was coming, didn’t you?"
Rowan: "No."
Whitescar: "Honesty is the root of respect. You expect me to treat you as an equal? Then cease your deceit."
*Tell Whitescar you were warned beforehand.*
*Rowan briefly considered telling Whitescar the full truth, but Heartsong’s relationship to him complicated things. Rowan cast a glance around him at the ruination of the room.*
Rowan: "...A Fae has been visiting me in my dreams. She told me that you would be coming shortly before you arrived."
*At this Whitescar’s eyes went wide. He leaned down to stare directly into Rowan’s eyes. The wolf bared his fangs.*
Whitescar: "Who?"
Rowan: "I don’t know. She did not give a name."
Whitescar: "One of Arzyl’s twisted sycophants, no doubt."
Whitescar: "How long has this been going on?"
Rowan: "Not long. Some weeks before you arrived."
Whitescar: "What lies did she feed you?"
Rowan: "None. She forced me to relive some old memories, then asked some questions. We spoke only briefly in person."
Rowan: "She believed that I could… help your people. And that she could help me."
Whitescar: "Whatever help that witch and her followers promise you, it is poison."
*Deny his accusation.*
Rowan: "I have seen enough strange things in this world to no longer be shocked by the unexpected."
*The Fae’s countenance darkened.*
Whitescar: "You lie."
Rowan: "Why would I? What do I have to gain from playing dumb?"
Whitescar: "I don’t know. That is what concerns me."
Whitescar: "It is the kind of falsehood that Arzyl and her ilk are fond of perpetrating. Slippery. Evasive."
*Pretend Jezera told you about the Fae.*
Rowan: "Mistress Jezera has had dealings with your kind in the past."
Rowan: "She told me there was a chance that you would contact us."
*At this Whitescar let out a deeper growl.*
Whitescar: "...I do not like it. The witch has already sunk her talons into her."
Whitescar: "One reminds me too much of the other. At least the red brute would try to slay me in honest combat."
Rowan: "...He may have mentioned something to that effect, after your dust up in the throne room."
Rowan: "You speak of your fellow ambassador like she is your enemy."
Whitescar: "That is exactly what she is."
Whitescar: "No true Fae can suffer a soul-eater. She is an abomination, a scourge on the court of the Queen. If Sol were awake, he would weep at the ruin she has brought to our people."
Whitescar: "And yours."
Whitescar: "Her arrival here is like casting embers into dry grass. Nothing good can come of it."
*Who is this “Sol you refer to?*
Whitescar: "Our god. Our savior. A Dragon of incalculable age and wisdom."
Rowan: "Of all the pantheons of Solanse, I have never heard that name used in reference to a God."
*Whitescar let out a dismissive growl.*
Whitescar: "There is no ‘pantheon,’ there is only Sol."
Whitescar: "Your foreign gods do not interest us. They are callous. Capricious. Uncaring. It is a wonder that you follow them at all."
Rowan: "...And Sol isn’t any of those things?"
Whitescar: "The fact that you must ask speaks to your ignorance."
Whitescar: "Would Solansia intentionally intervene to save a species she had no hand in shaping?"
Whitescar: "Would Kharos willingly sacrifice himself to rescue a beleaguered people, poised on the brink of annihilation?"
Whitescar: "Order and Chaos. A petty dichotomy. Halves of a whole at war with itself. Sol is beyond either of these things."
*Rowan’s eyebrow rose. A god who was wholly independent of both Solansia and Kharos? It was as if the Fae was telling him that he’d figured out how to turn the ocean upside down.*
*Rowan made a mental note to look further into this fabled “Dragon. He had never heard the name before.*
*Arzyl eats souls?*
Whitescar: "Yes. Her and her tittering minions in the Midnight Court."
Whitescar: "You think that warped form is the body of a natural-born Fae?"
Whitescar: "She wears the skin of those whose souls she has devoured, pantomiming an immortal existence to delay her own life cycle indefinitely."
Whitescar: "It is disgusting. Parasitic. A Fae should live and die like any other creature, to be reborn again by the caring touch of Sol."
Whitescar: "Were it not for the Concordat, I would have already torn her throat out."
Rowan: "The Concordat?"
Whitescar: "Perhaps if I come to know you better we will speak further on it. It is… a shameful episode."
*Tell me more about your Queen.*
Whitescar: "Kassandra? You do not know of her?"
Rowan: "The more you tell me, the less I seem to really know about your kind."
Rowan: "I have heard children’s stories of a fairy queen, but-"
Whitescar: "She would scoff at the title. But it is an apt one."
Whitescar: "She is the Great Awakener, the first Fae that Sol rescued. He was drawn to her spirit, and she became bound to him."
Whitescar: "If a Fae’s soul is a glimmering candle, then hers is a roaring bonfire."
Whitescar: "It was Kassandra who led our people in the aftermath of Sol’s fall, guiding us through the winding ways of the Netherweald, till we learned the proper paths ourselves."
Whitescar: "Kassandra is our ruler, both Queen and prophetess. She is Sol’s voice until he can speak to us once more, and as such is wise beyond judgement."
*The wolf seemed to hesitate, his ears flattening momentarily against the back of his head.*
Whitescar: "Though… I have, in my naive ignorance, begun to waver into hubris of late. I sometimes find myself worried."
Rowan: "About what?"
Whitescar: "That the Queen may have a blind spot."
Whitescar: "Arzyl still lives, in direct defiance of all virtue. But Kassandra has prevented me thus far from punishing her sacrilege."
Whitescar: "Even now, the witch tests my resolve. I am powerless to cleanse the Midnight Court of its corrupting influence until her majesty gives the command."
Whitescar: "Sol’s divine will is enigmatic at times."
*You mentioned a life cycle?*
Whitescar: "It is no secret. It is the same as yours."
Whitescar: "Mortality is a gift, it is our place as spirits of nature to share in that experience. Fae are born, we live, we die."
Whitescar: "The only difference for us is: Solansia and Kharos do not hold the chain to our souls. When we die, we are reborn, to continue the cycle."
Rowan: "If that’s the case, then why would Arzyl bother to steal other people’s bodies?"
*Whitescar bared his teeth, exposing long fangs.*
Whitescar: "Because she is infested with ego."
Whitescar: "It is a long, painful process to reincarnate. Centuries can pass between our return, and during that time our souls… suffer."
Whitescar: "She has no patience for such a struggle. Better to steal the lives of others than to earn one of her own."
*I have no further questions for you.*
Whitescar: "…Hmh. It has been good to talk openly and directly with someone, after all this dithering."
Rowan: "Look, I understand your frustration. My task is to mediate the issues between Bloodmeen and your people."
Whitescar: "There is only one true solution to that problem."
Rowan: "So I’ve gathered. But until such time as I can either find a compromise or your Queen recalls you, you’re stuck here."
Rowan: "…I think it’s pretty evident you don’t much care for your room?"
*The Wolf bared his teeth and cast a dismissive paw in the direction of the wreckage.*
Whitescar: "I have made my opinion clear."
Rowan: "I’m certain the maids will thank you for your bluntness."
*Rowan nodded towards the window.*
Rowan: "The Rakshan Wastes are a bit sparse on habitable environments, but there is a small forest not far from the castle itself."
Whitescar: "I know of it. Sickly. Drained. But clinging to life. I admire it’s tenacity to endure in such harshness."
Rowan: "…Would you prefer to lodge there until such time as I call upon you again?"
*The wolf took cautious note of Rowan’s stoic expression.*
Whitescar: "The demons will be loathe to let me out of their sight, so close to their lair of stacked stones."
Rowan: "You’re not dealing with them, you’re dealing with me. And something tells me you hardly need my permission to go where you please."
*Whitescar let out another rumbling chuckle.*
Whitescar: "Courtesy is fickle. But your honesty is appreciated."
Whitescar: "..."
Whitescar: "I do not know what to make of you, human."
Rowan: "I guess that makes two of us, Fae."
*The beast very nearly smiled, his lips curling into a half-snarl.*
Whitescar: "You carry yourself with great dignity, yet you move like a chained bear. I know the look: I once bore it myself."
Whitescar: "There is… something about you. Something- grrnh…"
*He let out a contemplative growl, his eyes narrowing on Rowan as he loomed over him.*
Whitescar: "If your masters will not heed my warnings, then perhaps you can be convinced with raw proof."
Rowan: "I like to think of myself as a credulous man."
Whitescar: "Meet me in the forest then, after I have had time to hunt. I will give you proof of that which your masters meddle with."
Rowan: "Why not just show me now? Isn’t that why you’re here?"
*The Fae drew back, letting out a soft yip of displeasure. He almost looked… apologetic.*
Whitescar: "I am unbalanced. Askew. My thoughts were scattered when we first met, my words poorly chosen. This room has only further agitated me."
Whitescar: "I need time to steady myself, to live true as a wild Fae. I must pray to Sol as well, hear the wisdom he speaks to me in my dreams."
Rowan: "Then you will have that time, Whitescar. But when we meet again, I expect answers."
*Something shifted in the wolf’s posture. His shoulders seemed to relax, his stalking slowing to a more sedated prowl.*
Whitescar: "I had all but given up on this reality and its shortsighted denizens."
Whitescar: "You are different."
*Then, without so much as a goodbye, the Fae flung himself from the window. It happened so fast Rowan didn’t even have time to process it.*
*One moment the hulking creature was there, the next he had somehow squeezed his large form through the window and disappeared into the night.*
*Seeing that he was now alone in the trashed room Rowan turned on his heel and went to inform the soon-to-be-aggrieved cleaning staff.*
*The narrow, winding corridors closed in around Rowan as he descended into the deeper bowels of the Castle’s innards. Every footstep was punctuated by a cacophonous echo, as if his very presence was disturbing the ancient, dessicated ruins of the now-lost civilizations that had built upon them, one on top of the other.*
*Dust hung heavy in the air, the collected offal of thousands of years of stagnation fluttering about like mouldering moths in the gloom. He had come to this abandoned section of the Castle’s basement for one purpose: to speak to the enigmatic Wolfman.*
*The task became increasingly daunting the deeper Rowan went, moving through the cramped confines of the tomblike warrens with a nervous hand at his sword hilt. He turned a corner, coming to a small stone antechamber leading still deeper into the interior, and was caught off guard by what he saw.*
Whitescar: "I will tell you if anything changes; for now, we must assume that the Twins’ decision to make him the arbiter of this dispute is an honest one."
Whitescar: "It does not seem to be a trick on their part. Or if it is, I can’t fathom the reason for it."

*The two cursed and fled down a staircase.  After giving a moment for his eyes to adjust to the darker interior, Rowan chased after them.  It wasn't that difficult a trail. There were scrolls and parchments scattered all along the cellar.*
*The hero found them arguing over their fallen work. Now the priest was desperately imploring his lady to hurry along and leave the scrolls behind, while she insisted on saving their research.*
*Loud crunching from above announced that the battle outside had been decided and orcs were now pouring into the structure. Rowan announced his presence and implored the two of them to give up. They still had a chance to save both their lives and their research.*
*While he had no idea who the priest was, Rowan did recognize the woman's crest and called her by family name.*
*His words seemed to have an affect on her, as she made known her surrender.  The priest was shocked at this, but also agreed to fall in line now that his lady had given up.*
*After giving clear orders that the two prisoners were not to be harmed, Rowan ordered the orcs to take them back to Bloodmeen along with the wine.  Perhaps Cliohna could make use of them.*
*This vine growing many vines that most of their research seemed to focus on was far beyond his understanding.*
*While the woman froze up, the priest stepped in front of her and told her to flee.  Before Rowan could react, the holy man summoned the power of Solansia and sent a shockwave into the wall.*
*The result was likely not what had been intended, as the whole section of dirt, wood, and bottles collapsed inward on top of the man!  Rowan was forced to flee lest a part of the wall fall on him as well.*
*He retraced his steps, leaping past the collapsing walls and managing to keep his footing in the muck that formed after a wine bottle broke. Eventually finding his way up to the surface floor when the ground finally stopped shifting.*
*With the immediate danger passed it was time to turn attention back to the matter of the girl. Obviously there was another way out of the cellar, so if she'd survived the priest's sacrifice she might very well be making her escape now.*
*Rowan sent the orcs fanning out around the building to catch her. Luck was on his side, as they soon caught her trying to pile her scrolls onto a horse at a hidden exit. Her dedication to knowledge was admirable and Rowan hoped that Cliohna would find a use for her.*
*This vine growing many vines that most of their research seemed to focus on was far beyond his understanding.*
*He retraced his steps, leaping past the collapsing walls, but stepped into a pool of mud from one of the broken bottles. It sent him tumbling down and soon Rowan's legs were buried in dirt.*
*Thankfully the ground stopped shifting and the immediate danger passed. It took Rowan several minutes to free himself from the earth and the rough fall was something he'd be feeling in the morning.*
*By the time he'd returned to the upper floor, the noblewoman was long gone.*
*A shame, she and the priest might have been of use to Cliohna's research. This vine growing many vines that the few scrolls he'd recovered depicted was far beyond Rowan's understanding.*
